CCCXX Of Saints

Blasphemy ●●●○

Day 320 of 365

Take the halo off before you admire anyone.

Saint Anthony Tormented by DemonsMartin Schongauer, c. 1470

Lately orphaned and eighteen or twenty years old, Antony of Egypt heard a gospel read in church. In it Jesus tells a rich man to sell all he has[1] and give to the poor, and Antony went out and did it. Athanasius, the bishop who wrote his life, records that he gave the villagers the family land, some two hundred acres of good soil[2], sold the rest, and handed his young sister to a house of virgins[3] to be brought up, so that he could give himself to the discipline unencumbered.

He spent most of the next eighty-odd years in a tomb, a deserted fort and then a mountain in the desert, fighting what he took to be demons. Decades on, coming down from the mountain, he saw his sister grown old in her virginity[4] and the leader of other virgins, and Athanasius records that he rejoiced. The churches that venerate him call him the father of monks.

Athanasius gives the sister no name and no word. She was a little girl[5] when her brother placed her, and the life measures her only by how well she kept the arrangement he made for her. The Quran’s sura of the cave has a servant of God, whom the tradition names al-Khidr and honors, kill a boy for fear that he would one day burden his believing parents with defiance and disbelief[6], and the boy goes unnamed as well.

Each of these halos was paid for by someone else, a sister handed over at an age when she had no say and a boy killed for a sin he had not yet committed. The tales that honor the saint never record what either of them thought of the bargain, and the reverence they ask for goes whole to the one who made the bargain.

Declaration: My heroes are the ones who stayed home with their sisters.

The Rite · Christian

Take a holy card, print or page showing a saint or hero of the faith you were raised to admire, write across it in marker the worst thing that figure did, read aloud what you wrote, and hang it upside down where you eat.

Testament · What did the holy figure you most wanted to resemble as a child actually do?

CCCXXI Of Death

Heresy

Day 321 of 365

Eat today what the regime is saving for later.

Death: My Irony Surpasses All OthersOdilon Redon · To Gustave Flaubert, 1889

The oldest verified human being on record was a Frenchwoman who died in nineteen ninety-seven at a hundred and twenty-two[1]. She smoked from the age of twenty-one until she was a hundred and seventeen, took a small glass of port after meals, and sometimes ate a kilo of chocolate in a week[2]. Ecclesiastes, which tradition credits to Solomon in his old age[3], had long before said what the three religions of the book later built doctrines to deny. The same fate meets the human being and the beast, and all return to dust[4]. The dead know nothing and have no further reward, and their love and their hatred and their envy perished with them[5].

Its counsel is to eat your bread with joy and drink your wine with a glad heart, since there is no work and no knowledge in the grave[6]. The longevity regimes skip the Preacher. They treat death as a defect awaiting a patch, and their devotees keep a rule stricter than a monk’s, the supplements counted out by the dozen and the blood drawn and charted on a schedule, all of it spent on a reprieve that nobody has yet been granted, the woman with the chocolate included.

Health is worth having for the life it allows, and the regime spends that life buying more of it, the bread refused and the wine poured away for a decade nobody can promise. The dead of every regime lie as still as the dead of every feast. The Preacher gave his order to eat with joy to people who would die early or late, and he meant the bread for the years when the eater still has teeth.

Declaration: The regime charts its blood every quarter, and I mean to die with honey on my fingers.

The Rite

Say aloud your exact age and then I will die. Then slowly eat warm bread, fresh from the oven or the bakery and thick with salted butter and honey, the loaf you have been refusing.

Testament · What are the pleasures you postponed worth, set against the longer life they bought?

CCCXXII Of Lovers

Indulgence

Day 322 of 365

Love whoever wants you back, and ask no one’s leave.

Francesca and PaoloGustave Doré · Inferno, Canto V, 1861

The children could not speak the language of Judah. Nehemiah, back from the Persian court, found Jews married to women of Ashdod, Ammon and Moab, and their children talking half in the speech of Ashdod[1] and in the tongues of their mothers’ peoples, and he took the children’s speech as evidence against the fathers. He cursed the men, struck some of them and pulled out their hair[2], and made them swear by God to give no daughter to a foreign son and take no foreign daughter for their sons or for themselves.

A child takes its words from whoever raises it. The mothers had kept those houses long enough for the language spoken in them to be theirs, so the marriages Nehemiah cursed were households that worked, two peoples under one roof. Even Solomon, he told the men, had been led into sin by foreign women[3]. A grandson of the high priest had married the daughter of Sanballat[4], Nehemiah’s old enemy, and Nehemiah chased him off and wrote that he had cleansed them of everything foreign[5].

The line he drew is drawn still by faiths that keep a book of marriages. Classical Islamic law forbids a Muslim woman a husband of another faith[6], and a temple sealing requires two members[7] in good standing. A Catholic needs a dispensation to marry an unbaptized person validly[8], and canon law grants it only after the Catholic promises to do all he can to have the children baptized and raised in the Church[9]. That promise is Nehemiah’s fear of the children’s speech, written into law. The rules are drawn for the marriage that lasts long enough to raise children, and whoever you were barred from loving was barred because the keepers of the book feared the two of you would make a household.

Declaration: My bed keeps no border, and no elder stands guard at its door.

The Rite

Spend an hour in public, hand in hand, with the person your faith or family would never have let you love. With no such person, eat alone at a restaurant of a people your elders kept you from, dressed as for a lover, and order your dish in their language.

Testament · Whom have you wanted that someone else’s rules forbade you?

CCCXXIII Of the Book

Blasphemy ●●○○

Day 323 of 365

Read the book they hid from you.

The Lovers ReadingGustave Doré · Inferno, Canto V, 1861

In twelve twenty-nine the crusade against the Cathars had just ended, and the Council of Toulouse set sworn searchers for heretics in every parish[1]. It forbade lay people to keep the books of the Bible beyond a book of psalms or a book of hours, and above all in the common tongue[2].

Rome’s Index of Forbidden Books ran for four centuries, and in nineteen sixty-six, the year it stopped enforcing the list, it declared that the list remained morally binding[3]. The Mishnah, on Rabbi Akiva’s word, counts anyone who reads the outside books[4] among those who lose the world to come. The second letter of John tells its readers to receive no false teacher into the house[5], and not even to wish him well on his way.

The plate catches two readers at the moment he leans in to kiss her, the book loose in her hand. At the curtain behind him another man crouches with his blade drawn.

Toulouse kept from lay hands the very scriptures its priests read aloud at every Mass, which puts the danger it feared in the reader, since the words were already the Church’s own. The Index, Akiva’s ruling and the shut door each reach for the same person, someone alone with a page and no keeper at the elbow. Whatever that person concludes belongs to them, since no searcher sworn in any parish could follow a reader into a shut room and argue the page back out of a mind. Unable to stand at every elbow, a council that had just watched a crusade end kept the remedy the plate keeps behind its curtain, a man with a drawn blade.

Declaration: I keep the forbidden shelf by my pillow and leave the lamp burning until I finish the chapter.

The Rite · Christian

Read, as far as one sitting carries you, in bed, the most explicit love story you can find, with your own Bible closed beneath it as a bookrest.

Testament · Which book did someone take out of your hands, and what did they fear it would do to you?

CCCXXIV Of False Counsel

Reckoning

Day 324 of 365

Weigh advisers by what they have seen.

The False CounsellorsGustave Doré · Inferno, Canto XXVI, 1861

Rehoboam had two sets of advisers and three days to choose between them[1]. The northern tribes came to Shechem to make him king and asked one thing first, that he lighten the yoke his father Solomon had laid on them[2]. The old men who had stood before Solomon told him to speak kindly and the people would serve him forever[3]. The young men he had grown up with told him to say that his little finger was thicker than his father’s loins, and that where his father had chastised them with whips he would chastise them with scorpions[4].

He took the young men’s line nearly word for word. Ten tribes walked out on the spot. They stoned the officer he sent to collect the forced labor, Rehoboam escaped to Jerusalem in his chariot[5], and the tribes made another man king[6]. The narrator credits the turn to the LORD[7], to fulfill a prophecy against Solomon’s house, and also reports the choosing. He never mentions the young men again or records any loss of theirs.

The two benches differed in what the book says of them. The old men had stood before Solomon while he lived[8], and they told the son of the yoke to be a servant. The young men had grown up with Rehoboam[9] and stood before him, and the book credits them with no other post. Over those three days he had the old men’s advice and the young men’s side by side, and he took the one that matched what he wanted to say.

Declaration: I keep the old men on my bench, and the young men who gain from my yes can advise the next prince.

The Rite

Write the hardest question you are facing and send it today to the adviser whose counsel has held up best. Then take off your list the one whose advice has never once cost them anything to give, number deleted or feed muted, and owe them no explanation.

Testament · Where has the advice you follow most often actually led you?

CCCXXV Of Discord

Heresy

Day 325 of 365

Stop nodding.

The Sowers of DiscordGustave Doré · Inferno, Canto XXVIII, 1861

Proverbs counts six things the Lord hates and then, in the Hebrew idiom of six and even seven, adds a seventh[1], placed last where the weight falls, the one who sows discord among brothers[2]. For centuries the Church excommunicated, exiled or burned the sowers of division among its own brothers. It called them heretics. In Greek the word had meant a choice.

The founder of the Church says he came to bring a sword and to set a man at variance against his father[3]. The rabbis preserved the rejected rulings of the house of Shammai beside the rulings of the house of Hillel[4] that prevailed, and the Talmud explains the victory of the house of Hillel by its manners, that its teachers taught the opinions of Shammai beside their own and named them first[5]. The Mishnah says that an argument for the sake of heaven is one that will endure[6]. Discord is condemned when it threatens the authority and treasured when the authority owns it.

The household and the office keep the proverb under the softer names of harmony and alignment and enforce it the same way, so that everyone nods at the table and complains in the car on the way home. The Hebrew word satan means an adversary, the one who stands opposite in a dispute, and in Zechariah the satan stands at the high priest’s right hand[7] to accuse him, an officer doing a court’s work until the Lord rebukes him. A hearing with no one opposite is a ceremony. A family that has let one person’s opinion go unanswered at dinner for twenty years has been holding that ceremony, and whoever finally answers it takes the place at the right hand that scripture gave the satan, and the rebuke that came with it.

Declaration: I disagree out loud and pass the salt in the same breath.

The Rite

Pick a view someone pressed on you until you nodded, from someone who cannot hurt you for dissent, and tell them today, face to face or by voice, that it is foolish and why. Skip it where they are dangerous or hold your livelihood.

Testament · Which opinion have you sat through for years, and what has your silence cost you?

Sources

[1] Prov 6:16

[2] Prov 6:19

[3] Matt 10:34–35

[4] m. Eduyot 1:5; b. Eruvin 13b

[5] b. Eruvin 13b

[6] m. Avot 5:17

[7] Zech 3:1–2


CCCXXVI Of Looking Away

Mastery

Day 326 of 365

Refuse your eyes to suffering you cannot touch.

The Traveller RebukedGustave Doré · Inferno, Canto XXIX, 1861

The last verse of Isaiah sends the worshipers out of Jerusalem to look at the corpses of the men who rebelled, whose worm does not die and whose fire is not quenched[1], and to find them loathsome. On the Sabbath of the new month the synagogue reads the chapter aloud and repeats the verse before at the close[2], so that the reading ends on worship, and the corpses are still read aloud one verse earlier.

Crowds gathered for the Inquisition’s burnings in Seville and the burnings at Smithfield, and food vendors worked the crowds at the Tyburn hangings, and for most of history a public death was a show a pious audience could attend with a clear conscience, since the suffering had been certified as deserved.

A person can now spend hours a day watching suffering they can do nothing about, a war on another continent, a flood in a town they will never visit, and call it conscience or staying informed. The feeling is the one Isaiah handed his worshipers on the walk out to the corpses, a place among the righteous at the edge of someone else’s ruin, and the platform sells it by the minute with an advertisement beside each death. An evening given to the flood teaches the shape of every collapsed roof and the name of one rescued dog. The dog was saved without you. Pity follows the eyes, and eyes that spent the evening on a drowned town an ocean away left the sick friend down the street alone with a cold supper.

Declaration: A stranger’s flood on a screen has no claim on my evening.

The Rite

Delete or log out of the app you watch the world’s disasters on, and take the hour it would have had to someone near you in trouble, carrying a meal, cash or a pair of working hands.

Testament · What have you won by watching the suffering you watch most?

Sources

[1] Isa 66:24

[2] Isa 66:23–24


CCCXXVII Of the Prophet Split

Blasphemy ●●●●

Day 327 of 365

Count yourself among the damned, and sleep soundly.

The Sowers of SchismGustave Doré · Inferno, Canto XXVIII, 1861

Whoever wishes to be saved, the Athanasian Creed begins, must before all things hold the Catholic faith, and whoever does not keep it whole and undefiled will without doubt perish everlastingly[1]. Clergy chanted it at Prime[2] and Anglican congregations recited it on feast days, as a creed, for centuries. Christian polemic had long filed Islam as a heresy[3] and its prophet as a renegade, and the engraving above shows the prophet of Islam in a Christian hell, split from chin to groin.

The tractate Gittin, in the William Davidson edition of the Talmud, tells of Onkelos raising Yeshu the Nazarene from the dead by necromancy to ask his sentence, and hearing it, boiling excrement, for having mocked the words of the sages[4]. The Quran honors Jesus as a prophet and promises the fire to those who associate others with the god, and counts the claim that the god is the Messiah, son of Mary[5], as one. The Book of Mormon repeats the line from the end of Mark, that whoever believes not shall be damned[6].

Add the sentences together and nearly every human being who ever lived is in somebody’s hell. Jesus is in one of them. Read side by side, the damnations look like warrants issued by rival courts, each enforceable only where its court sits and void everywhere else, and no court has jurisdiction over a defendant who walked out of all of them. That defendant stands in the largest crowd in history, and the sentences passed on the people you love have no officer to serve them.

Declaration: The fires disagree about who burns, and I leave them to settle the matter between themselves.

The Rite · No faith

Find the verse near the end of Mark that damns whoever does not believe, and print it. Say the names of three people you love, each followed by In good company, then bury the page in a flowerpot and plant something that fruits over it.

Testament · Which of your old faith’s damnations did you believe longest?

[1] Athanasian Creed 1–2

[2] Roman Breviary, Sunday Prime; BCP 1662, Morning Prayer rubric

[3] John of Damascus, De haeresibus 100

[4] b. Gittin 57a (William Davidson ed., Sefaria)

[5] Quran 5:72

[6] Morm 9:23; Mark 16:16


CCCXXVIII Of the Severed Head

Heresy

Day 328 of 365

Put the head back on the body.

Bertran de BornGustave Doré · Inferno, Canto XXVIII, 1861

A headless trunk walks among the damned on the plate above, holding its own head by the hair like a lantern[1]. It belongs to Bertran de Born, the troubadour who set the young English king against his father[2], and the head explains its own sentence, that for parting a father from a son it carries its brain parted from its root[3].

Paul wrote that the flesh lusts against the spirit and the spirit against the flesh, so that you cannot do what you would[4], and it has often been preached as a war in which the will must master the body. Ignatius of Loyola gave his Jesuits a particular examination of conscience to be made twice a day, at noon and at night, with a dot for every fall[5], so that each man could check at night whether the second line held fewer dots than the first.

Overthinking passes for self-awareness now, and a person can spend an evening on the attachment style behind a single text message and call it growth. Meanwhile the body has been reporting, the jaw that sets when one name lights up the phone, the shoulders that come down in one friend’s kitchen and nowhere else, and the head, busy with its commentary, files none of it.

Bertran’s sentence was for parting a father from a son. Yours is milder and self-chosen, a year of evenings answering the name that lights up the phone and sets the jaw, and none spent in one friend’s kitchen where the shoulders come down.

Declaration: The animal that carries me keeps better records than my conscience ever did.

The Rite

Name aloud the person or place your body leans toward and the one it recoils from. Go where it leans today, an accepted invitation or an evening in that friend’s kitchen, and turn down the other’s next request.

Testament · What has your body been telling you about a person or a place that your head keeps arguing with?

Sources

[1] Inf. 28.121–122

[2] Inf. 28.134–138

[3] Inf. 28.139–141

[4] Gal 5:17

[5] Ignatius, Spiritual Exercises 24–31


CCCXXIX Of the Long View

Indulgence

Day 329 of 365

Finish the list of losses, then stand up.

The Last PouchGustave Doré · Inferno, Canto XXIX, 1861

Habakkuk complained to his god of violence and got an answer worse than the complaint, a promise to raise up the Chaldeans, that bitter and hasty nation[1], who would gather captives like sand[2]. He took his stand on his watch, he says, and set himself upon the tower to see what would be said to him[3].

The book closes with the prophet setting out his own worst case item by item, the fig tree without blossom, no fruit on the vines, the olive failing, the fields yielding no food, the flock cut off from the fold and no cattle in the stalls[4]. It is the inventory of everything a farm can lose, drawn up while the army was still coming[5], and two verses later he is back on his feet on the high places[6], sure-footed as a deer. The list comes first and the footing after, joined by one word, yet. His belly trembled at the report, he says, his lips quivered and rottenness entered his bones[7], and he rejoiced anyway, and calls the LORD God his strength.

Micah makes the same fig tree the picture of peace, each man seated beneath his vine and his fig[8] with none to make him afraid. Habakkuk gives that picture up in advance, fig tree and fold, before the army arrives, and finds he still has his feet, sure-footed as a deer. He had asked for an answer, the answer was the Chaldeans, and it was after hearing it that he set himself on the tower to wait for what came next.

Declaration: I counted every loss before it came, and none of them gets to run my life.

The Rite

Write down, item by item, everything the danger you fear most could take from you, read the list aloud once, then climb to the highest place you can reach today and stand there and say aloud Let it come.

Testament · Which loss have you dreaded for years without once naming it in full?

[3] Hab 2:1

[7] Hab 3:16

[8] Mic 4:4


CCCXXX Of the Aging Body

Blasphemy ●●●○

Day 330 of 365

Treat your body at the pharmacy and never at the altar.

The FalsifiersGustave Doré · Inferno, Canto XXIX, 1861

Leviticus gives most of two long chapters to skin. A swelling, a scab or a bright spot is brought to the priest, who checks whether the hair in it has turned white, shuts the sufferer away for seven days, and pronounces clean or unclean. The unclean must tear their clothes, leave their hair loose, cover the upper lip and call out unclean wherever they go, and live alone outside the camp for as long as the mark remains[1].

The rabbis later read the disease as a sentence for slander[2], on the strength of Miriam, who turned white as snow[3] after speaking against Moses. When the disciples met a man blind from birth they asked whose sin had caused it, his own or his parents’. Jesus cleared all three and kept the body as a message all the same, since the blindness was there so the works of the god could be displayed in him[4]. A hadith promises the Muslim that the prick of a thorn wipes away some of his sins[5]. As punishment, as display or as payment against a debt of sin, every one of these readings makes the body a page the god writes on.

Near its close Ecclesiastes describes an aging body part by part, the grinders ceasing because they are few, the almond tree in white blossom and the grasshopper a burden, and the description itself charges no sin. The priest had a sentence for every scab and a bandage for none, and what he read as a verdict was an ailment, which wanted a medicine box.

Declaration: Every scar I carry was written by weather and years, and no god signed it.

The Rite · Christian

Open your own Bible in the bathroom at the chapter of John where a man is born blind so the god’s works can be displayed, set your ointment and bandages on its pages, and keep the book in the medicine cabinet.

Testament · Who taught you to read a mark or ailment on your body as a judgment?

Sources

[1] Lev 13:45–46

[2] b. Arakhin 15b–16a

[3] Num 12:10

[4] John 9:2–3

[5] Sahih al-Bukhari 5641


CCCXXXI Of Rivals

Reckoning

Day 331 of 365

Keep score openly, and salute only the fair win.

The Mad ShadesGustave Doré · Inferno, Canto XXX, 1861

Leah called her first son Reuben, because the god had seen her misery and now her husband would love her. She called the second Simeon, because the god had heard that she was unloved, and the third Levi, because this time at last her husband would be joined to her[1]. Her sister Rachel, the loved wife and the barren one, gave her maid to Jacob and named the maid’s second son Naphtali, saying she had wrestled great wrestlings with her sister and had won[2].

Leah bought a night with him from Rachel[3] with the mandrakes her firstborn had found in the field. For years the two women measured their lives against each other in the currency their world prized most, which was sons, while the man they competed for went on preferring Rachel and her children. Rachel died in childbirth on the road and named the boy son of my sorrow[4].

The sons were counted as points, and Jacob’s open preference for Rachel’s firstborn handed his older sons the scoreboard. Out of envy[5] they sold him to a caravan for twenty pieces of silver[6]. In Egypt Joseph, the son the sisters had been counting against each other, ended the score at last by feeding the brothers who had sold him, telling them they had thought evil against him and that he would nourish them[7]. Rachel was buried by the road to Bethlehem[8] and Leah in the family cave at Machpelah[9], and the only man who put the account down was the one it had cost most.

Declaration: My children will inherit my house and none of my feuds.

The Rite

Tell the sibling, cousin, colleague or friend who beat you fairly at something, in one sentence, that they won it. In the next sentence name the contest you mean to take from them.

Testament · What would you have to win to call settled the score you still keep with someone you grew up beside?

CCCXXXII Of Masks

Heresy

Day 332 of 365

Wear the face that serves you, and know it.

MyrrhaGustave Doré · Inferno, Canto XXX, 1861

Judah’s first two sons married Tamar and died, and he promised her the third when the boy was grown, then kept him back. She waited in widow’s clothes, openly herself, and the boy grew up and was not given to her[1]. So she took the widow’s clothes off, covered herself with a veil and sat by the road to Timnah, where her father-in-law would pass. Judah took her for a prostitute, offered her a young goat from his flock, and left his seal, its cord and his staff with her as a pledge[2].

Three months later he heard she was pregnant by harlotry and ordered her brought out and burned[3]. She sent the pledges to him with word that their owner was the father, and he knew them and said she was more righteous than he was[4]. The bare face had waited on his promise and got nothing. The veil got his seal in an afternoon, and the seal got her life back and a verdict in her favor from the man who had sentenced her.

Matthew sets her name in the third verse of his gospel[5], Thamar, in the line that runs down to Jesus, and in its twenty-third chapter has Jesus curse the scribes and Pharisees, woe after woe, as hypocrites[6], the Greek word for an actor in a mask. The feeds keep the curse and forget the genealogy. They want the self shown raw on every channel and the grief narrated to strangers, and they call any reserve a lie. A face put on for a purpose is a tool in the hand, and Genesis gave its verdict to the woman holding one. A face shown bare to everyone, for nothing, is a tool as well, held by the crowd that asked for it.

Declaration: Whoever wants my bare face can wait for it in widow’s clothes, as Tamar waited on Judah.

The Rite

Choose a face for one errand today where you want something, calmer or colder or more charming than you feel, and keep it on until you have what you came for. At your own door, hang it up with your coat.

Testament · Where do you give away more of yourself than the situation has earned?

Sources

[1] Gen 38:11, 14

[2] Gen 38:15–18

[3] Gen 38:24

[4] Gen 38:25–26

[5] Matt 1:3

[6] Matt 23:13–29


CCCXXXIII Of Volume

Beauty

Day 333 of 365

Raise your voice without waiting for the cue.

NimrodGustave Doré · Inferno, Canto XXXI, 1861

At Jericho, Joshua forbade the people to shout or let a word out of their mouths until the day he gave the order[1]. For six days the army circled the city in silence with seven priests blowing rams’ horns in its midst, the horns sounding and the men mute, and on the seventh day the order came, the people shouted, and the wall fell flat[2]. The noise belonged to the priests until the general released it.

The Talmud kept the silence for the standing prayer and dropped the release. A man who lets his voice be heard in the standing prayer is of little faith[3], and one who raises it is counted among the false prophets, who shouted to their gods, the kind the prophets of Baal on Carmel[4] would illustrate. The Quran has Luqman teach his son to lower his voice in general speech, since the harshest of all sounds is the braying of the donkey[5].

The synagogue kept loudness for its offices, the shofar in an appointed mouth, and the mosque the call to prayer given to Bilal because his voice carried farther[6], and the Talmud filed the raised voice in the standing prayer with the doubter and the false prophet, excusing only a man praying alone who cannot hold his mind on the words under his breath. A congregation gets it on cue, an amen in its place and a response at the leader’s signal. Raised to full strength where nobody gave the order, the same throat fills a room to the walls.

Declaration: I have kept quiet in enough prayer rooms to be owed a lifetime of noise.

The Rite

Play the grandest music you love as loud as the room will bear, somewhere nobody will be disturbed, and sing over it at the full size of your voice. End on a shout held for as long as your breath lasts.

Testament · Where did you learn to make yourself small in sound, and who gained by it?

Sources

[1] Josh 6:10

[2] Josh 6:4, 14–20

[3] b. Berakhot 24b

[4] 1 Kgs 18:27–28

[5] Quran 31:19

[6] Abu Dawud 499


CCCXXXIV Of Giants

Blasphemy ●●○○

Day 334 of 365

Learn the forbidden craft, and wear what you make.

The GiantsGustave Doré · Inferno, Canto XXXI, 1861

Genesis keeps the giants to four verses. The sons of God saw that the daughters of men were beautiful and took wives from among them, the giants were on the earth in those days, and the children of those marriages became the mighty men of old, the men of renown[1], and three verses later the god resolves to blot out man and beast. The book of Enoch, which the Ethiopian Orthodox Church still counts as scripture and the letter of Jude quotes[2], tells the rest at length.

Two hundred watchers came down on Mount Hermon[3], took wives, and taught what they knew. Azazel showed men how to work metal into swords and bracelets and how to paint the eyes[4], others taught herbs and spells and the paths of the stars, and the giants born of those unions grew until they had eaten everything humanity could grow and began to eat humanity[5]. Enoch lays the corruption of the whole earth to what Azazel taught and has the god tell an angel to ascribe all sin to him[6]. The sentence fell on teachers and taught alike, the watchers bound in the dark and the earth drowned[7].

Every craft those chapters name comes from the accused, and the charge against them is that the lessons took. The god’s answer was to drown the pupils, and their arts came through the water anyway, so that the forged bracelet and the painted eye are on every street the flood was sent to clear. A ring worked at a bench today is a watcher’s lesson passed from hand to hand, worn on the hand the flood was sent to stop.

Declaration: Every bracelet I own is contraband from heaven, and I wear them all.

The Rite · Christian

Read today’s horoscope for your sign aloud, the paths of the stars the watchers taught and the churches call divination, then put on one piece of gold you own and wear it for the rest of the day.

Testament · Which skill or adornment were you taught to fear as the beginning of corruption?

CCCXXXV Of the Ground

Heresy

Day 335 of 365

Take your strength from the ground, the way Antaeus did.

AntaeusGustave Doré · Inferno, Canto XXXI, 1861

The man in Genesis is formed of dust taken from the ground[1], and the Hebrew makes a pun of it, adam out of adamah, the earthling out of the earth. His sentence before the expulsion sends him back to it. The ground is cursed for his sake and will bring forth thorns and thistles[2], and he will eat bread in the sweat of his face until he returns to it, for dust he is and to dust he will return[3].

The Greeks told of Antaeus, a son of Earth, who could not be beaten in wrestling while he stood on her, since every fall gave him his strength back[4]. Heracles killed him by lifting him off the ground[5] and crushing him in the air.

Simeon climbed a pillar in the Syrian hills and lived on top of pillars for thirty-six years[6], each higher than the last, the final one over fifty feet. When he fell ill and the emperor sent three bishops[7] to bring him down to a physician, he stayed where he was, and the Church made a saint of a man held off the earth until he died. Strength comes up from below. Hands that have been in dirt want salt and bread torn with the fingers, and a body set down on bare ground with a heavy meal in its lap is a wrestler back on his mother. The ground the god cursed for the man’s sake has fed him every meal he has eaten, and it collects one payment, in the grave.

Declaration: I sit in the cursed dirt to eat, and I get up from it stronger.

The Rite

Carry the heaviest meal you want outside and eat it with your hands, sitting on bare ground, a lawn, a garden bed or a field.

Testament · What were you taught to rise above that you would rather sit down in?

Sources

[1] Gen 2:7

[2] Gen 3:17–18

[3] Gen 3:19

[4] Lucan, Pharsalia 4.593–655

[5] Apollodorus, Library 2.5.11

[6] Theodoret, Religious History 26; Catholic Encyclopedia, s.v. Simeon Stylites

[7] Catholic Encyclopedia, s.v. Simeon Stylites


CCCXXXVI Of the Thaw

Mastery

Day 336 of 365

Ride down to meet what frightens you.

The Traitors in the IceGustave Doré · Inferno, Canto XXXII, 1861

Nabal of Carmel owned three thousand sheep[1], and when David’s young men came at shearing time to ask for food he railed at them and sat down to a feast like the feast of a king[2]. His wife was already on the road. A servant had warned Abigail that evil was settled against the house[3], and she loaded donkeys with two hundred loaves, five dressed sheep and two hundred cakes of figs[4], rode down to meet them, and talked David out of a massacre while her husband was still drunk.

In the morning, when the wine had gone out of him and she told him, his heart died within him and he became as a stone[5], and about ten days later the god struck him dead[6]. The text puts about ten days between the stone and the god’s blow. The god of Job claims the frost as his own, asking from whose womb the ice came and boasting of the face of the deep frozen hard[7]. A psalm adds that the thaw is his as well, sent down by his word[8]. What the chapter has him send is a blow.

Abigail moved the other way. David blessed the god for sending her[9]. The chapter records what she did instead of freezing, the road ridden down toward four hundred swords[10] and her own words at David’s feet before he had said one to her[11]. The woman who rode it was David’s wife before the chapter closed[12], and the husband who waited had gone from stone to corpse.

Declaration: The stillness I called patience was fear with good posture, and I have broken it.

The Rite

Put the demand, offer or price you swallowed last time to the person you froze before, or to the nearest equal. Speak before they do, stand if they are standing, and ask for more than you expect.

Testament · Before whom does your body turn to stone, and what has that cost you?

CCCXXXVII Of the Kick

Blasphemy ●●●●

Day 337 of 365

Aim the kick higher than the beaten man.

Bocca degli AbatiGustave Doré · Inferno, Canto XXXII, 1861

Break the enemy’s teeth in his mouth, a psalm asks the god, and it promises that the righteous will rejoice at the vengeance and wash their feet in the blood of the wicked[1]. Malachi closes the prophets with the same picture, the saved leaping like calves let out of the stall and the wicked trodden down like ashes under the soles of the faithful[2] on a day that burns like an oven. Salvation in both comes with a license to kick. The enemy under the foot is no longer a threat. He is already beaten, and the treading is a pleasure granted afterward to the winners.

The first book of Nephi gives the license its plainest scene. Nephi finds Laban fallen to the earth drunk by night[3], and the Spirit presses him to kill the man. Nephi shrinks, he says, having never shed the blood of man[4], and wishing he need not. The Spirit speaks twice more, that the Lord has delivered Laban into his hands and slays the wicked to bring forth his righteous purposes, and between the speeches Nephi supplies reasons of his own, that Laban had sought his life, would not hear the commandments[5] and had taken the family’s property. The third speech adds that it is better one man perish than a nation dwindle in unbelief[6]. Then he takes Laban by the hair and strikes off the head with Laban’s own sword[7]. What held out in the scene was a man shrinking from a helpless drunk, and heaven pressed three times to overrule him.

Declaration: I return the license Nephi was given over a drunken man at night, and the god who wrote it can answer for the heads it has excused since.

The Rite · Christian

Set a cross on the floor, your own crucifix or two sticks tied together, and kick it across the room. Pick it up and drop it top first into the kitchen bin among the scraps.

Testament · Where would your first kick land among the parts of the god’s apparatus that still stand over you?

Sources

[1] Ps 58:10

[2] Mal 4:3

[3] 1 Ne 4:5–7

CCCXXXVIII Of Ugolino

Reckoning

Day 338 of 365

Pass sentence on the wrong that went unanswered.

UgolinoGustave Doré · Inferno, Canto XXXIII, 1861

Archbishop Ruggieri’s party seized Count Ugolino of Pisa[1] on the first of July, twelve eighty-eight, and shut him in the Gualandi tower called the Muda, with two of his sons, Gaddo and Uguccione, and two of his grandsons, Nino and Anselmuccio. They were held there until March of twelve eighty-nine, when the tower was opened on the eighteenth and all five were dead of hunger[2].

Paul wrote to the Christians at Rome in the twelfth chapter of his letter. Recompense to no man evil for evil[3], he said, and if it be possible, as much as lieth in you, live peaceably with all men. Dearly beloved, avenge not yourselves[4], but rather give place unto wrath, for it is written that vengeance belongs to the Lord and he will repay. If thine enemy hunger, feed him[5], and if he thirst, give him drink. Six years after the five died, Ruggieri was still archbishop of Pisa.

In the ninth circle of Hell the count, frozen in the ice, sets his teeth in the archbishop’s skull[6] where the brain meets the nape, and the wronged one is the one still gnawing. The promise in Romans asks the wronged to keep the file open on the god’s behalf, for a hearing set for no date, and the waiting is where the gnawing happens. A verdict closes a file, and Nicholas IV’s summons of April 1289 left no verdict on record, so the one with standing to give it is the one who was wronged. Ruggieri died at Viterbo on the fifteenth of September, twelve ninety-five, holding the see[7], and by the twentieth Boniface VIII had named his successor.

Declaration: I pass my own sentences, and I pass them while I live.

The Rite

Write the name of the one who wronged you and went unpunished, the charge, and the penalty beneath it. Write today’s date under the penalty. Read it aloud once, standing, sign it, and lock the page in a box. Then throw the key away where you cannot get it back.

Testament · Whose wrong against you has gone unanswered, and what penalty fits it?

CCCXXXIX Of the Pelican

Heresy

Day 339 of 365

Spend on yourself what you were taught to spend for others.

Ugolino in the TowerGustave Doré · Inferno, Canto XXXIII, 1861

Medieval bestiaries told of a pelican whose chicks had died, and who tore open her own breast and brought them back with her blood. The Church took the bird for an emblem of Christ and the Eucharist and carved her on altars and on the doors of tabernacles, and a eucharistic hymn still sung before the reserved sacrament calls Christ the loving pelican[1] and begs to be washed clean in his blood. The zoology was false, and the picture of the parent who gives her own body to the young stayed on the altar anyway.

Paul had called himself the Corinthians’ father in the faith[2], one father among ten thousand instructors, and in his second letter he told them that parents should lay up for their children[3], that he sought them rather than their goods, and that he for his part would most gladly spend and be spent for them[4], though the more he loved them the less he was loved, which is the pelican’s gift in a father’s mouth.

A parent takes the first portion when the dinner is cut. The coat bought for no one else, with the wool warm against the collarbone, the bath run hot enough to redden the shins, a room with a lock and a plate carried into it, are the upkeep of the one adult the children can see. Children who watch a parent eat the good end of the loaf see a grown life enjoyed, with the butter still soft on the knife, a picture the pelican never gave them.

Declaration: Whoever I love gets me in one piece, and the pelican can keep her wound.

The Rite

Spend money today on a pleasure nobody else will share, and take it alone for two hours. Then claim a standing outing of your own, a regular hour out of the house, and announce it to anyone you live with as already begun.

Testament · Which piece of the life you have handed over entirely to others would you take back first?

Sources

[1] Adoro te devote, st. 6

[2] 1 Cor 4:15

[3] 2 Cor 12:14

[4] 2 Cor 12:15


CCCXL Of Evening Meetings

Indulgence

Day 340 of 365

Be comforted by someone you can touch.

The Meeting of Isaac and RebekahGustave Doré · La Grande Bible de Tours, 1866

Isaac, the Talmud tractate on blessings says, instituted the afternoon prayer[1], and the rabbis found it in a single verb. Genesis says he went out into the field as evening came on, to do something, and the Hebrew word is rare enough that English Bibles cannot agree whether he went to meditate or to take a walk[2]. Whatever he went for, he lifted his eyes and saw camels coming. On one of them sat Rebekah, fetched by Abraham’s servant from his father’s kindred in Mesopotamia, and when she saw him she got down from the camel and covered herself with her veil.

He brought her into the tent of his mother Sarah, she became his wife, he loved her, and he was comforted after his mother’s death[3]. The god is absent from that sentence, and so is the prayer. Sarah had been dead about three years[4] when the camels came.

The rabbis built a daily office on the walk, the afternoon prayer the devout have said standing ever since, and built no office on the tent. Church and synagogue still meet a mourner the same way, with set words at set hours, a psalm by the coffin and a prayer said for the dead, and the synagogue bars the mourner from his own marriage bed for the seven days of shiva[5]. Genesis puts the cure in the other place. The field heard him out at evening and left him grieving, and what ended it was a woman in his mother’s tent with her body beside his own.

Declaration: I take my mourning to bed with someone breathing, and the field can keep the prayers.

The Rite

Spend two hours with the person you love best, held and unhurried, with food brought to wherever you lie, and stay there together. Alone, run a long hot bath, oil your skin, and lie in clean sheets for the hour after.

Testament · Whose body has comforted you better than any prayer, and how long is it since you asked for it?

Sources

[1] b. Berakhot 26b

[2] Gen 24:63

[3] Gen 24:67

[4] Gen 17:17; 23:1; 25:20

[5] b. Moed Katan 15b, 21a


CCCXLI Of the Sons

Blasphemy ●●●○

Day 341 of 365

Pay nothing on a claim that rests on nothing you signed.

The Sons of UgolinoGustave Doré · Inferno, Canto XXXIII, 1861

Count Ugolino’s two sons and two grandsons starved beside him in the Tower of Hunger[1], shut in from July 1288 until the March after, for a treachery the archbishop of Pisa charged against the father.

Paul supplied the principle for ordinary bodies when he told the Corinthians that they were not their own, having been bought with a price[2]. It names no sum and no date. The first letter of Peter names the coin, and the gospel has the Son of man giving his life as a ransom for many[3]. It is the precious blood of Christ, a lamb without blemish and without spot, and the faithful are assured they were ransomed with nothing so cheap as silver or gold[4], which leaves the balance beyond any wage they could earn.

The sentence that still works on grown adults, long after the child has left home, opens with after everything we did for you and closes on a sum, a visit or a loan or a silence kept on request. It is the same purchase moved into a kitchen, and Peter named the price of the first one in blood. A claim on your time or your body that rests on having been raised and fed rests on a contract the child was in no condition to sign, and the parents who chose to have you made the only offer in the matter and took on its costs when they made it. Ugolino’s sons stood surety for their father without being asked, and the archbishop collected from them in the tower.

Declaration: No one who fed me holds a bill I signed.

The Rite · Christian

Write PAID IN FULL across the verse in your own Bible where Paul says you were bought with a price, sign it, tear the page out, and file it with your receipts.

Testament · Which claim on your body or your time still rests on nothing but the fact that you were raised?

[1] Dizionario Biografico degli Italiani, vol. 37 (1989), Gherardesca

[2] 1 Cor 6:19–20

[3] Matt 20:28

[4] 1 Pet 1:18–19


CCCXLII Of the Sleeping Serpent

Heresy

Day 342 of 365

Guard only what is yours.

Satan Finds the Serpent AsleepGustave Doré · Paradise Lost, Book IX, 1866

A psalm sung in synagogue and church alike says that the keeper of Israel neither slumbers nor sleeps[1]. The Throne Verse of the Quran, which Muslims are taught to recite at bedtime for protection[2], says the same of its god, that neither drowsiness nor sleep overtakes him[3]. The Hebrew word the psalm uses for that keeper is shomer, the watchman who walks the wall while the town sleeps.

Genesis puts the same verb to work in Eden. The god sets the man in Eden to till it and to keep it[4], the watchman’s word again, so that the first human being is given a post before he is given a wife. The serpent, the subtlest beast of the field[5], is given none, and when it speaks to the woman it speaks as a creature whose time is its own.

The modern vigil is kept on a phone beside the bed. Alerts arrive at every hour, the mind walks its perimeter from waking until sleep, and a whole trade sells the dark before dawn back to the faithful as discipline, given to the inbox and the cold shower. The watchers admire one another for it and ask the ones who sleep eight hours how they manage. A watch is always kept on behalf of whoever owns what is watched, and the god praised for never sleeping still drafted a man to guard his trees. Whoever answers the alert at two in the morning has taken up Adam’s post, and every hour of it is spent guarding someone else’s garden.

Declaration: The insomniac on the throne can count his own trees tonight, and I sleep coiled with the serpent.

The Rite

Tonight turn off notifications on every app that can reach you after dark and leave the phone outside the bedroom. If you wake in the night, do not go to it. As you lie down say aloud This post was never mine.

Testament · What do you check in the night, and who profits from your checking?

[2] Sahih al-Bukhari 2311

[3] Quran 2:255

[4] Gen 2:15

[5] Gen 3:1


CCCXLIII Of the Garden Path

Beauty

Day 343 of 365

Take the long way, and let your eye steer.

The Serpent in the GardenGustave Doré · Paradise Lost, Book IX, 1866

Isaiah wants every valley raised and the crooked made straight[1], and the same book names a twisting thing it wants dead. In that day, it promises, the god will take his great sword to Leviathan the crooked serpent[2], the twisting one, and slay the dragon that lives in the sea. The book that loves a straight road also loves a dead serpent, and it paves a highway of holiness where even fools who walk it will not go astray[3].

Moses and Proverbs lay the same road. Moses forbids Israel to turn aside to the right hand or to the left[4], and Proverbs tells the son to ponder the path of his feet[5] to turn neither way and to remove his foot from evil. The psalm uses the serpent’s own root, aqalqallot, for the walkers who turn aside. Those who turn aside to their crooked ways, it says, the god will lead away with the workers of iniquity[6].

The straight road is the road with one destination, the one named at the start, and the crooked road goes where the eye goes, along the water and under the tree whose shape stopped you, and it comes in late with the afternoon spent on what the walker chose. Four books lay one map, the valleys filled, the feet kept to the road and the twisting serpent dead, and the book’s own word for the walkers who turn aside is the serpent’s word. A walker raised on that map goes from door to door for a lifetime and arrives having seen the pavement.

Declaration: Isaiah paved his highway for fools who could not be trusted to wander, and I wander.

The Rite

Go today by the longest beautiful route you know to somewhere you must be, on foot if you can. Stop at the first thing that holds your eye, and stay until you have had your fill of it.

Testament · What have you walked past for years because the straight way was quicker?

CCCXLIV Of the Serpent

Blasphemy ●●●○

Day 344 of 365

Lay one childhood warning beside what happened.

The Serpent Slinks AwayGustave Doré · Paradise Lost, Book IX, 1866

On the day you eat of the forbidden tree, the Lord God tells Adam, you will die[1]. The serpent tells the woman that she will not, that her eyes will be opened and she will be like gods, knowing good and evil[2], and the chapter then confirms him on every point that can be checked at once. They eat, and their eyes are opened[3].

The god, conferring with whoever else is present, admits that the man has become like one of them, knowing good and evil, and posts guards on the road to the other tree before the man can live forever too[4].

The later canon and the Church blackened the serpent, Revelation naming it the devil[5] and the sculptors setting it under the Virgin’s heel, and none of them could alter what Genesis itself records, that of the two forecasts made in the garden the serpent’s was met within that very chapter, and the god’s, which named a day, came due, on the count of Genesis, nine hundred and thirty years later, when Adam died.

Touching yourself would ruin you, rock music would open the door to demons, the world would end before you finished school, the friend who left the faith would be miserable within a year. Each came with a warning or a date, and most of the dates have passed. A threat that has missed its date has been tested, and whoever issued it, the god in the garden first among them, must be read by his record of dates the next time he names one.

Declaration: I eat what I was warned off and keep the open eyes, which came on the very day the god had set for my death.

The Rite · Christian

Open your own Bible at the page where the god tells Adam he will die on the day he eats, strike through the warning, write nine hundred and thirty years beside it, and sign your name under the figure.

Testament · What did you give up to escape a warning that never came due?

CCCXLV Of the Second Bite

Reckoning

Day 345 of 365

Let no verse count your children holy for you.

Adam and Eve After the FallGustave Doré · Paradise Lost, Book IX, 1866

The woman eats, and for the length of a clause she is the only one in the garden who has tasted the fruit. Then she gives some to her husband[1] who is with her, he eats, and the eyes of both are opened[2], and they sew fig leaves into aprons. One has eaten and one has not, they share a bed and a bank account, and each looks across the table and waits.

Paul tells a believer married to an unbeliever to stay if the unbeliever is willing[3], and his ground is that the unbeliever is made holy, which the children are said to prove. The same rule runs both ways, for the brother with an unbelieving wife and the woman with an unbelieving husband, if the unbeliever is pleased to dwell with them. The unbelieving husband is made holy by the wife[4], he says, and the unbelieving wife by the husband, or else their children would be unclean, and as it is they are holy[5].

The child has no vote in it. A child is counted holy by the church on a parent’s account before he can read the verse that does the counting, and the unbelieving parent is counted by the same rule. The one who has eaten owes that count nothing, and the child owes it nothing either. If the unbeliever departs, Paul says, let him go[6] and the brother or sister is not under bondage in such cases, so the same chapter that counts the child holy also lets the household break.

Declaration: Paul calls me holy by way of the one I married, and I decline the holiness and keep the marriage.

The Rite

Write to one church asking that your family’s names come off its roll, cradle roll or mailing list, send it today, and say Nobody counts us but us.

Testament · Which kindness in your house would you trust more if the church were out of the room?

CCCXLVI Of Hiding

Heresy

Day 346 of 365

Meet the next prying question with silence.

Adam and Eve HideGustave Doré · Paradise Lost, Book X, 1866

Calling into a garden he planted, to a man he made, the god of Genesis asks the man where he is[1], and it is the first question he ever puts to a human being. The man has heard the sound of him walking there[2] and answers from among the trees where he and the woman have hidden themselves. He was afraid, he says, because he was naked[3]. The trees had hidden him well enough that the god had to call out, and it was the answer that gave him away. The god’s next question is who told him so[4], as though a creature wanting cover could only have learned it from somebody else.

The epistle of James told believers to confess their faults to one another[5], and the Fourth Lateran Council, in the year twelve fifteen, obliged every Catholic of age to confess all their sins to their own priest at least once a year[6]. The newer piety holds its sessions in the sharing circle and in the app that asks each day how you feel and shows your friends the answer, and it calls the disclosure authenticity.

It treats a person with an unshared interior as a person with something to hide, and it calls the hiding a sickness. Anyone asked to prove an inner life by posting it is being told that a feeling nobody has seen did not happen, and the circle that waits in silence for you to speak has a confessor’s patience without his discretion, since the priest at least was bound by the seal[7]. A thought nobody has been told is the one thing a person owns outright, and an inner life published in full belongs to its audience.

Declaration: A god who had to call out where art thou has admitted the trees work, and I keep a grove of my own.

The Rite

Walk alone for an hour among trees, a park or a wood, with your phone left at home, and come back without saying where you went. If anyone asks, answer I was out.

Testament · What did you once confess that was never anyone’s business, and who was doing the asking?

CCCXLVII Of the Talents

Mastery

Day 347 of 365

Dig up what fear has buried.

Hell Awaits Satan’s ReturnGustave Doré · Paradise Lost, Book X, 1866

In Matthew’s parable a master going abroad leaves five talents with one servant, two with another and one with a third, each according to his ability, and on his return settles accounts. The first two have traded and doubled their sums. The third, afraid of a hard master, had buried his talent in the ground[1] and hands it back intact, and the master takes it from him, gives it to the man with ten[2], and has him thrown into the outer darkness[3].

A scholarly minority reads it[4] as the portrait of a harsh lord who rewards whoever makes him rich. The master himself tells the frightened servant that he ought at least to have put the money with the exchangers, so that it came back with interest[5], and he never asks how the man with ten came by them.

Every servant in the story answers to the same lord, and the one servant it punishes is the one who was afraid. The third servant says so himself, that he was afraid and went and hid the talent, and the lord answers from the servant’s own description of him, reaping where he had not sown[6], as a man who has no quarrel with it. The master repeats the reaping and the gathering back to him without a quarrel, and the conclusion the servant drew from them, that a hard man is safest left alone, is the one that ruined him. Burying the talent protected nothing, since the hard man collected anyway and threw the servant out.

Declaration: I would sooner lose my one talent in trade than hand it back clean to a lord who reaps where he never sowed.

The Rite

Name the bid, pitch or application you have held back for fear of a hard answer, for a post, a client, a contract or a commission. Send it today, and ask for more than you expect to get.

Testament · Whose hardness have you used as a reason to keep your one talent in the ground?

[2] Matt 25:28

[3] Matt 25:30

[4] Herzog, Parables as Subversive Speech (1994)

[5] Matt 25:27

[6] Matt 25:26


CCCXLVIII Of Hissing

Blasphemy ●●●●

Day 348 of 365

Hear every hiss as a complaint from the one you left.

The Fallen Become SerpentsGustave Doré · Paradise Lost, Book X, 1866

Through Jeremiah the god promises to make Jerusalem a desolation and a hissing, so that everyone who passes will be astonished and hiss at all its plagues[1]. Lamentations shows the passersby clapping their hands and hissing and wagging their heads at the daughter of Jerusalem[2] and asking if this is the city men call the perfection of beauty, the joy of the whole earth. Micah threatens a city the same way, with desolation and its people a hissing, for keeping the statutes of Omri, a king of Israel[3].

Jeremiah 18 says, Because my people hath forgotten me, they have burned incense to vanity, and they have caused them to stumble in their ways from the ancient paths, to walk in paths, in a way not cast up, to make their land desolate, and a perpetual hissing[4]; every one that passeth thereby shall be astonished, and wag his head.

The god speaks the hiss to Solomon as well, after the temple’s dedication, and there it is conditional. He says he has hallowed the house Solomon built to put his name there for ever, but if Solomon or his children will not keep his commandments and go and serve other gods, then will I cut off Israel out of the land which I have given them, and this house, which I have hallowed for my name, will I cast out of my sight, and Israel shall be a proverb and a byword among all people, and at this house, which is high, every one that passeth by it shall be astonished, and shall hiss[5]. Asked why, they shall answer, Because they forsook the LORD their God.

Declaration: I walked out under a hiss, and I keep my will.

The Rite · Christian

Read aloud the verse of Lamentations where the passersby hiss at Jerusalem, then print the Apostles’ Creed, recite it through in one long hiss with every s drawn out, and crush the page in your fist and drop it in the bin.

Testament · Whose hissing has followed your best decision, and what did that decision win you?

CCCXLIX Of Sin and Death

Heresy

Day 349 of 365

Eat one meal today consulting nothing but your mouth.

Sin and Death DepartGustave Doré · Paradise Lost, Book X, 1866

James draws death’s family tree in a single verse, desire conceiving and bearing sin, and sin, grown to its full size, bearing death[1], so that death, in this telling, descends from appetite, a hand reaching, a mouth open.

Paul made the genealogy doctrine. Death came into the world through one man’s sin[2], he told the Romans, and the wages of sin are death[3], and from that letter the Church built its teaching that death entered through sin[4], an intruder admitted by a crime. Genesis makes the man from dust before any bite, and when it passes sentence it says he is dust and will return to dust[5], which describes his material. Genesis does threaten death on the day of the bite[6], but when the sentence falls the god posts a guard on the tree of life, lest the man eat of it and live for ever[7], which treats the man as mortal until he is fed from that tree, so the verse takes from him the remedy and leaves the dust.

A watch counts the day’s steps and an app weighs every meal against a target, and the discipline promises years added at the far end for appetites refused now. It is the old genealogy with the theology filed off, death still descended from appetite and still to be held off by refusal. Meanwhile butter browns at the edge of a pan, and a thick cut of meat takes its salt and gives up its fat, and the whole kitchen fills with a smell no tracker scores. Whatever years refusal at the table adds to a life, the refuser pays for them with a thinner supper every night on the way to the same grave.

Declaration: The undertaker keeps the only count of my days that matters, and I refuse to do his bookkeeping at dinner.

The Rite

Cook the dish you have been rationing against a longer life, the butter and cream and marbled meat, and eat every bite slowly at a laid table, with the watch off your wrist and the tracking app closed for the day.

Testament · Which dish have you been refusing yourself, and what did the refusal promise?

CCCL Of Fasting and Grief

Reckoning

Day 350 of 365

Eat well in front of whoever enjoys your sorrow.

The Fourth DayGustave Doré · Inferno, Canto XXXIII, 1861

When Elkanah’s household went up to sacrifice at Shiloh[1], his wife Peninnah, who had children, provoked his wife Hannah, who had none, until Hannah wept at the feast and would not eat. The first book of Samuel says twice in two verses that the god had shut up Hannah’s womb[2], and it gives the taunting as the consequence, so the sorrow at that table was made above and served at the meal by a woman with sons.

Her husband asked why she wept and would not eat, and whether he was not better to her than ten sons[3]. She rose and prayed at the house of the god with her lips moving and no sound, until the priest Eli took her for a drunk and told her to put away her wine[4], and she answered him that she was a woman of sorrowful spirit and no worthless daughter[5]. Eli sent her off with a wish that her god grant what she asked[6], and she went her way and ate, and the text says her face was no longer sad[7].

A grief that refuses its portion at the rival’s feast does the rival’s work, since a woman who will not eat puts the taunt on display for the whole table. Hannah’s face had changed over a plate before anything she asked for arrived. Her own vow had set the price, and the god who had shut the womb opened it on her terms, the boy handed to the sanctuary once he was weaned[8]. She paid it. Then she sang over her enemies with an enlarged mouth[9], giving every line of the triumph to the god who had shut the womb. Peninnah drops out of the record after the first chapter, and the second opens with the barren woman’s song.

Declaration: I keep Hannah’s appetite and her boast, and her god gets no son of mine.

The Rite

Cook the dish you love best. Before the first bite, say aloud four lines boasting of what you have now over whoever made a sport of your grief or your lack, then eat all of it.

Testament · Who made a sport of your grief or your lack, and what have you won since?

CCCLI Of the Ark

Blasphemy ●●●○

Day 351 of 365

Choose your crew by what each did when everything went under.

Noah Builds the ArkGustave Doré · Paradise Lost, Book XI, 1866

A bull of Boniface the Eighth settled your fate in the year thirteen hundred and two. The one Church, it said, is the one ark, outside which everything on earth was destroyed, and submission to the Roman pontiff is necessary to salvation for every human creature[1].

The ark it borrowed is specified with a shipwright’s care, three hundred cubits by fifty by thirty, gopher wood pitched within and without. Genesis lists eight saved[2] and gives a reason for one of them, since the god tells Noah that it is he who has been seen righteous[3]. His wife, his sons and their wives came aboard on the household’s ticket, and one of those sons was Ham, who saw his drunken father naked once the ground was dry and brought a curse down on his own son Canaan[4]. You would have drowned among the unnamed rest of the earth. The god shut the door himself[5], and the first letter of Peter makes the flood a figure of baptism[6].

In the Quran the line runs through Noah’s own house. He calls to his son to come aboard, the son answers that he will climb a mountain, and a wave comes between them[7]. When Noah pleads that the boy was of his family, the god answers that he was not, because his conduct was unrighteous[8], and the only conduct the passage shows is his refusal to come aboard. Genesis draws the waterline around the house of one man who did all the god commanded him[9], the bull around a bishop in Rome, the Quran at a call from the deck. The people who stood beside you when you left crossed that line to do it, and a god who sorts his passengers by obedience would have left every one of them in the water.

Declaration: Noah’s god sealed the door on everyone outside one household, and I would rather drown with my friends than float with his family.

The Rite · Christian

In the margin of the flood story in your own Bible, draw a boat of your own, write aboard it the names of those who stood by you when you left, and black out Noah’s family with a marker.

Testament · Which of those who stayed with you when you left would your old faith have shut outside the door?

CCCLII Of the Drowned

Reckoning

Day 352 of 365

Tally the flood before you admire the bow.

The FloodGustave Doré · Paradise Lost, Book XI, 1866

Genesis hangs the rainbow in the cloud as the god’s own reminder. Whenever it appears, he tells Noah, he will look on it and remember his covenant[1], and the waters will never again become a flood to destroy all flesh[2]. The chapter sets up no stone for the drowned.

Genesis leaves them unnamed and uncounted, man and cattle and creeping thing and bird together[3], and a later gospel remembers what they were doing when the water came, eating and drinking and marrying and being given in marriage[4]. The covenant that followed was made with Noah, his sons and every creature that came out of the ark[5], the fowl and the cattle included, and the drowned were no party to it. The god had announced beforehand that he himself would bring the flood[6]. Afterward he promised the survivors never to do it again, and the sign he hung in the sky is a monument to his own restraint.

Rules are relaxed the same way, with the old reason left standing and the change announced to those who stayed. A congregation that cut you off from your family now permits what it cut you off for, the youth you spent under a prohibition is spared the next generation, and the men who enforced it call it an adjustment. The relaxation is their bow, hung where the faithful can admire it. The sermons add restoration, a resurrection of the body or a paradise earth where every loss is handed back, so that nothing need be grieved, since all of it is coming back. A loss grieved at its full size goes on the books against the men who imposed it, and a loss promised back is written off before anyone has counted it.

Declaration: Mercy from the hand that opened the sluices is a receipt, and I file it with the damages.

The Rite

Write a tally of what one relaxed rule cost you, a line for each person, year and chance it took. Draw a bow across the top, write beneath it the name of whoever enforced the rule, and read every line aloud, ending This is what your rule cost.

Testament · What did a rule cost you that its later relaxation has never reckoned with?

CCCLIII Of Rules

Heresy

Day 353 of 365

Take what you like and answer no doorkeeper for it.

The People Beg MosesGustave Doré · Paradise Lost, Book XII, 1866

The revelation the Latter-day Saints call the Word of Wisdom announces in its second verse that it is sent by way of greeting, not by commandment or constraint[1]. It names wine, strong drink, tobacco and hot drinks as unfit for the body[2]. Within ninety years keeping it had become a condition of entry to the temple, the hot drinks had been read as coffee and tea, and a bishop asked about all of it before he signed a recommend.

The office that asks those questions is older than the advice. At Sinai the people heard the thunder and the trumpet, stood far off, and begged Moses to speak to them in the god’s place, promising to hear and do whatever he brought back[3], so long as the god did not speak to them and kill them[4]. Moses had carried messages up the mountain before, and their fear made the errand an office, the god telling him to stand by and receive every commandment for them[5]. The god had spoken the ten words to the whole assembly himself[6] and added no more, and everything after came down through Moses, until the rabbis counted six hundred and thirteen commandments[7].

A go-between has little to sell but the difference between advice and law. Advice is taken or left in private and leaves him idle. A law can be asked about at a door, and a failure of it can be confessed to him, repaired through him and certified by his signature, so a counsel that passes through his hands can come out the other side as a condition of entry. A rule set for your own reasons is kept or dropped at your own table, where nobody holds a pen over a recommend.

Declaration: Advice sent by greeting turned into a gate pass, and I was never asking to be let in.

The Rite

Brew the best coffee or tea you can buy, the hot drinks a bishop asks about, and drink it slowly at your own table. If anyone asks whether you keep a rule you never chose, say I keep my own counsel.

Testament · What did you once do freely that someone now asks about before letting you in?

[1] D&C 89:2

[2] D&C 89:5–9

[3] Deut 5:27

[4] Exod 20:18–19

[5] Deut 5:31; Exod 19:3–8

[6] Deut 5:22

CCCLIV Of the Exit

Beauty

Day 354 of 365

Leave the room where little is asked of you.

Adam and Eve Leave ParadiseGustave Doré · Paradise Lost, Book XII, 1866

Coats of skin, which the god made and put on them himself[1], were what Adam and Eve wore out of the garden. Genesis gives them no tears. The verse that follows the posting of the cherubim has the man knowing his wife and the woman conceiving[2].

The garden set one standing task, the tending of it[3], and little else to do. No child had yet been born in it, no one had died, and the one open question was the tree, whose fruit was forbidden. The nearest things to invention recorded there before the bite are the naming of the animals[4], which the god set before him, and one cry of recognition at the sight of the woman[5], and neither made a tool, a trade or a town. Within a chapter of the expulsion one son tills and another herds[6], and Cain founds a city and names it for his own son[7].

Paradise is a waiting room with good planting, and Genesis offers one way out of it, an appetite indulged against orders. Plenty of people sit in such a room, a post that asks little or an arrangement kept because it is pleasant and because so little ever happens in it. The exiles took their bite and wore the coats out, and the cherubim were left with a flaming sword[8] to guard a garden to which no one in Genesis asks to return. Cain’s city stands east of Eden[9], and the only thing Genesis has human hands make inside the garden is the apron of fig leaves[10] sewn after the bite.

Declaration: Every city was founded outside paradise, and I would pay that price again.

The Rite

Cancel one arrangement that keeps your days pleasant and empty, a subscription, a standing call or a seat on a committee, and send the cancellation today, saying as you send it I am leaving the garden.

Testament · Which easy arrangement have you kept only because so little ever happens in it?

CCCLV Of Lucifer

Blasphemy ●●●○

Day 355 of 365

Speak up at the table that expects your silence.

LuciferGustave Doré · Inferno, Canto XXXIV, 1861

Over its great candle at the Easter Vigil the Roman rite gives Christ the name Lucifer, the morning star that never sets[1]. The taunt asks how the son of the morning is fallen from heaven. The word is Latin for the bringer of light. The Latin Bible put the same word into Isaiah’s taunt[2], and Origen and others read it as the devil’s name[3].

The plate gives the name to a figure frozen in ice to the middle of his chest, great bat’s wings spread behind him and his chin resting on his clasped hands. He does not speak in the plate, and in the book it illustrates he weeps as he chews and says nothing. The older books let him talk, and even the Gospels let him speak in the wilderness[4]. In Job the satan is asked where he has come from and answers directly, with a report of his travels over the earth. The satan of Job stood in the divine council and disputed with the god over Job[5], and the Quran’s Iblis answered his maker to his face[6], asked for a reprieve until the day of resurrection, and was granted it[7].

The church kept the name’s light for its own Christ, and a later pen gave its bearer the ice and the silence. A household can hand the same arrangement to whoever leaves. That silence was written in the fourteenth century, long after Job and the Quran let him argue, and it holds only while the one in the ice agrees to keep it.

Declaration: The ice was only ever ink, and I have a voice that pen never gave him.

The Rite · Christian

Copy the verse in your own Bible where Jesus calls himself the bright morning star onto a slip, with Lucifer written over the name of Jesus, paste it over the printed verse, and read it aloud to whoever is in the room, or to the empty room.

Testament · Where have you caught yourself posing as the silent one who left?

[2] Isa 14:12

[3] Origen, Princ. 1.5.5

[4] Matt 4:3–10

[5] Job 1:6–12; 2:1–6

[6] Quran 7:12

[7] Quran 7:14–15


CCCLVI Of the Thousand Years

Heresy

Day 356 of 365

Hold no seat for a promise that names no day.

Satan Bound for a Thousand YearsJean Duvet, c. 1555

In Revelation an angel comes down with the pit’s key and a great chain in his hand and seizes the dragon, that old serpent. He binds him for a thousand years, throws him into the abyss, and shuts and seals it over him[1]. After the thousand years, the chapter adds, he must be let loose for a little while[2].

Christians have waited on timetables like it for nineteen centuries, and some of them acted on it. The Anabaptists who seized the German city of Munster in fifteen thirty-four proclaimed it the New Jerusalem and held it until the siege broke them a year later. In sixteen sixty-one some fifty Fifth Monarchy Men rose in London for the reign of King Jesus, held out four days, and saw their leader hanged, drawn and quartered[3] within a fortnight. Followers of the Baptist preacher William Miller fixed the return of Christ for a day in eighteen forty-four[4], and the churches that grew from them kept the expectation when the day passed.

A household can live on the same calendar. Someone promises to stop drinking once the job settles, and every dinner and every plan is arranged around a change one person controls and has never once dated. Revelation at least gave its prisoner a term, a thousand years and then a little season[5], and the Millerites had a day to be disappointed on. A promised change with no date owes nothing on any day, and the patience spent on it is a loan made without terms, recoverable on demand.

Declaration: Whoever wants my patience can name the day, and I will be elsewhere on the one after.

The Rite

Take back the key you lent, the access you granted or the seat you saved for whoever has made you wait longest, and give the place to someone who turned up. Where that person would answer with force, say nothing to them.

Testament · What have you kept giving the one whose promised change you have waited on longest?

[4] Snow, Advent Herald, 21 Aug 1844, p. 20; Dan 8:14

[5] Rev 20:3, 7


CCCLVII Of the Well

Indulgence

Day 357 of 365

Claim the water you hauled.

Eliezer and Rebekah at the WellGustave Doré · La Grande Bible de Tours, 1866

Abraham’s servant knelt his ten camels[1] by the well outside the city of his master’s kin, at the hour the women came out to draw water[2], and asked the god for a sign. The girl who, asked for a drink, offered water for the camels as well would be the one[3]. Rebekah came down with her jar on her shoulder and gave him a drink, and then, unasked, said she would draw for his camels until they had finished, and ran between the trough and the well until all ten were watered[4].

The servant watched in silence, and when the camels had done drinking he hung a gold ring on her nose and two heavy bracelets on her arms[5], then bowed down and blessed the god for leading him[6]. Her brother and her father heard the story that evening and declared that the thing came from the Lord[7]. Asked at last whether she would go with the man, Rebekah answered that she would go[8]. The chapter records her choosing three times, to draw, to keep drawing and to leave home, and the men around her credit heaven for the match.

You have drawn water for other people too, at work and at home, and watched the credit go to a manager or the will of heaven. The servant at least paid in gold before he bowed to give thanks. Credit handed to heaven never comes back down. No one audits heaven’s share, and whoever lets it go is paid, if at all, by whoever chooses to pay. Her brother Laban ran out to the well when he had seen the ring in his sister’s nose[9], and before Rebekah rode away on one of the camels[10] she had watered, he and their mother had been given precious things of their own[11].

Declaration: Heaven never lifted a jar, and I keep my thanks for the arms that did.

The Rite

Buy yourself a ring, a bracelet or a chain, the best you can afford without debt, as the wage for work someone else was thanked for. Put it on with your own hands and say I hauled this.

Testament · Who or what took the credit for the last heavy work you did?
