[7] al-Tabari, History, years 66-67 AH


Satan’s Portion

Counter-rite · kept by Muslims

12 Rabi’ al-awwal

Keep Satan’s portion.

In Fashion, as a Snow White Rose (Canto XXXI)Gustave Doré · The Divine Comedy: Paradiso, Cassell edition, 1868

Anas, who served the Prophet as a boy in Medina, is the source for a story in Muslim’s Sahih. Gabriel came to the child Muhammad while he was playing with other children, threw him down, split open his chest and took out his heart, removed a clot of blood from it[1] and told him that this was Satan’s portion in him[2]. Then he washed the heart in a golden basin with water from the sacred well and put it back. Anas adds that he saw the marks of the stitching on the Prophet’s chest[3].

The Mawlid keeps the birthday of that child, on the twelfth of the third month by the Sunni count. A hadith in Bukhari’s collection says that Satan touches every child at birth, which is why it cries, and excepts only Mary and her son[4]. Put the two hadith together and everyone else keeps the clot, and it took an angel opening a chest to take it out of one boy. The Quran’s Satan enters its story by one act. Told to bow to the first man, he refused and claimed to be the better of the two, made of fire where the man was made of clay[5].

Read beside the Quran’s Satan, the portion an angel cut out of one boy is the refuser’s share, the part that hears a command and weighs it before it bows. The Prophet’s obedience was made by surgery, on a child held down on the ground in the middle of a game. The other children there ran to his nurse and reported a killing[6], and every faith that teaches a child to distrust the part that weighs a command is telling that story again.

Declaration: Let the angel wash the Prophet’s heart in his golden basin. Mine keeps its portion.

The Rite

Cook a chicken or lamb heart, eat it whole, and say as you swallow Satan’s portion, and mine. Keep it private.

Testament · What were you taught to cut out of yourself, and what will you give it to do?

Sources

[1] Sahih Muslim 162c

[2] Sahih Muslim 162c

[3] Sahih Muslim 162c

[4] Sahih al-Bukhari 3431

[5] Quran 7:11–12

[6] Sahih Muslim 162c


Fifty Prayers

Counter-rite · kept by Muslims

27 Rajab

Haggle with every duty handed down to you.

Down Whose Steps I Saw the Splendours (Canto XXI)Gustave Doré · The Divine Comedy: Paradiso, Cassell edition, 1868

In one night, the Quran says, the god carried his servant from the sacred mosque to the farthest mosque[1], and the hadith fill in the rest. A white beast smaller than a mule and bigger than a donkey, whose every stride reached as far as its eye could see[2], carried the Prophet to Jerusalem, and from there he rose through the seven heavens, meeting Moses in the sixth, until he came to the god and was given the believers’ duty, fifty prayers a day[3].

On the way down Moses stopped him, asked what had been laid on his people, and told him to go back, since they would never manage fifty. Moses sent him back again and again. Each time the god gave way, until the duty stood at five and the Prophet, urged once more, said he was ashamed to ask again[4]. So the central rite of Islam was fixed by a negotiation in which a prophet coached by another talked an all-knowing god down by nine tenths. In one telling the god has the last word, that the five would count as fifty in reward[5], since his word does not change.

That clause lets the god keep his number on the books while the believer prays a tenth of it. The hours your employer expects and the visits your family claims were set by people who opened high, the way the god did on the night he named fifty. Embarrassment stopped the Prophet at five, and whoever set your figures is counting on it to stop you at theirs.

Declaration: Moses sent a prophet back until the god of heaven came down to five, and nobody who sets my hours outranks that god.

The Rite

Pick one demand you accepted at its first price, the hours, the visits, the fee, and say to yourself what Moses said, Go back to your Lord and ask for less. Then put a lower figure to whoever set it, today, and if they give way, ask again.

Testament · Which demand did you accept at its first price, and what will you counter with?

Sources

[1] Quran 17:1

[2] Sahih al-Bukhari 3887

[3] Sahih al-Bukhari 3887

[4] Sahih al-Bukhari 3887

[5] Sahih al-Bukhari 349


The Month of Fasting

Counter-rite · kept by Muslims

1 Ramadan

Drink when you are thirsty.

Hagar and Ishmael in the WildernessGustave Doré · La Grande Bible de Tours, 1866

From the first thread of dawn until the sun is down[1], for the twenty-nine or thirty days of the month, nothing passes the lips of a fasting Muslim, water included. The month is kept because the Quran says the book was first sent down in it[2]. The rule began harder, as the hadith collections report. A man who fell asleep after sunset without eating had to go without until the next sunset, and an Ansari of Medina named Qays ibn Sirma came home fasting, asked his wife for food, fell asleep while she went to find some, worked through the next day unfed and fainted at midday[3].

The verse that followed, in Bukhari’s account of Qays, allowed food and drink and the marriage bed through the whole night, until the white thread of dawn shows against the black, and told the believers that the god knew they had been betraying themselves[4] and had relented. The rule was amended in its prophet’s lifetime. The same law excuses the sick and the traveler[5], who make the days up later.

The plate shows Hagar in the wilderness with the boy Muslim tradition makes the Prophet’s ancestor, and in that tradition she runs seven times between two hills before a spring breaks from the ground beside the child[6]. In both tellings the water comes only when the child is near death. The fast asks for a month of that thirst by choice, with hunger offered up as proof of obedience. A thirst answered before anyone faints concedes nothing to the god and costs nothing the law itself did not give back.

Declaration: A law that needed a fainting man before it showed mercy will not be the one to tell me when I may drink.

The Rite

Today in daylight drink a tall glass of cold water slowly and eat a meal you enjoy, where no one who can report you will see.

Testament · What do your appetites ask of you now that you were taught to treat them as a test?

Sources

[1] Quran 2:187

[2] Quran 2:185

[3] Sahih al-Bukhari 1915

[4] Quran 2:187

[5] Quran 2:184–185

[6] Sahih al-Bukhari 3364


The Night of Power

Counter-rite · kept by Muslims

27 Ramadan

Make one night worth a thousand months.

The Angel and Women at the Empty TombGustave Doré · La Grande Bible de Tours, 1866

The Prophet came out to tell his companions which night was the Night of Power, found two men quarreling, and lost the knowledge[1]. He told them to seek it on the odd nights of the last ten[2]. The Quran calls it better than a thousand months[3] and says the angels and the Spirit come down in it by their lord’s leave on every errand, and that it is peace until the rising of the dawn[4]. The commentators identify it with the blessed night in which every wise matter is made distinct[5], the decrees of the year to come.

A thousand months is eighty-three years, longer than most lives, and the verse sets one night of worship above all of them. A quarrel between two men cost every Muslim since a fixed date, and the loss was turned into ten nights of vigil. The devout keep all ten to be sure of one, awake on the mat while the year ahead is believed to be written, and the only part they are given in its writing is to ask.

The verse prices that night by its traffic, the angels and the Spirit coming down on every errand. A night of your own is priced by what you bring. One spent with the people you would give up sleep for, on a date you chose and wrote down, outweighs the ten nights of vigil kept for a ruling handed down from above. The angels’ decree is the claim that your year was written before you lived it, and a room of chosen people still talking at dawn is a year being written by its owners.

Declaration: Whatever comes down on the Night of Power finds me asleep after a better night of my own.

The Rite

Send the invitations now for a night you name yourself, to stay up until dawn with the people you like best, and write the date on your calendar in ink.

Testament · Whose voices are worth a lost night’s sleep, and what would you want said before dawn?

Sources

[1] Sahih al-Bukhari 2023

[2] Sahih al-Bukhari 2017

[3] Quran 97:3

[4] Quran 97:4–5

[5] Quran 44:3–4


The Breaking of the Fast

Counter-rite · kept by Muslims

1 Shawwal

Feast on your own word, fasted or not.

Solomon Receives the Queen of ShebaGustave Doré · La Grande Bible de Tours, 1866

Fasting is forbidden today[1]. The law that spent a month withholding food in daylight turns on the first day of the next month and forbids going without, and Bukhari records that the Prophet would eat dates, an odd number of them, before he went out to the Eid prayer[2]. Families pay the small charity of the fast-breaking before the prayer and then go visiting in new clothes, and the tables carry a month of postponed appetite.

The Quran tells of a queen in Sheba whom a hoopoe reported to Solomon as the ruler of a rich country with a magnificent throne and a people who bowed to the sun[3]. She sent gifts, which he refused[4], and before she arrived he had her own throne brought to him. When she entered his palace she lifted her skirts to cross a floor she took for water, which proved to be glass, and then she submitted with Solomon to the lord of the worlds[5]. In the first book of Kings she arrives with camels loaded with spices and gold, tests the king with hard questions and goes home with everything she asked for[6].

The same woman ends twice, once won into submission by a trick floor and once leaving laden, and the difference is who set the terms. The law of the fast keeps the terms for itself. Both its orders, the month without and the morning with, were given to the appetite without consulting it, so that even the Eid table is laid by command. A feast eaten because the calendar turned is the fast’s last instruction, and the feast worth sitting down to is laid by the hungry, for guests they would cross a desert to see.

Declaration: I go to the table the way the queen of Sheba left Solomon’s court, carrying everything I wanted and owing him nothing.

The Rite

Lay a table today for the people you most want at it, with the dishes you want and nothing the occasion requires. Before the first bite say I set the terms of this table.

Testament · Who would sit at your table if no law had laid it?

Sources

[1] Sahih al-Bukhari 1990

[2] Sahih al-Bukhari 953

[3] Quran 27:20–24

[4] Quran 27:35–36

[5] Quran 27:44

[6] 1 Kgs 10:1–13


Standing

Counter-rite · kept by Muslims

9 Dhu al-Hijjah

Leave the god his fast and settle with people.

Jonah Preaches to the NinevitesGustave Doré · La Grande Bible de Tours, 1866

Hajj is Arafat[1], the Prophet said. On the ninth day of the month of the pilgrimage, upward of a million and a half pilgrims[2], the men in white, leave Mina for the plain of Arafat and stand there from noon until sunset, around the hill called the Mount of Mercy, begging forgiveness, and a pilgrim who misses the standing has missed the Hajj. It was there, in the year six hundred thirty-two, that the Prophet gave his farewell sermon from the bottom of the valley and told the crowd that their blood and their property were as sacred to one another as that day[3].

Muslims at home fast the day, and Muslim’s Sahih records the Prophet’s hope that the fast of Arafat wipes out two years of sin, the year past and the year to come[4]. One day without food in daylight pays off two years, one of them not yet lived. The jurists confine the pardon to lesser sins against the god, and a hadith in Bukhari’s collection holds a wrong done to a brother open until it is settled with him[5], so what the fast clears in advance is the one account in which nobody can be harmed.

The loan from a friend, the shift a colleague covered and the sum still owed to you all close between the parties, in kind and on merit, and an afternoon’s hunger settles none of them. A pardon the god issues for an empty stomach costs him nothing, and every account that costs anything is held by someone you can phone.

Declaration: The friend who lent me the money outranks the Mount of Mercy, and he is paid first.

The Rite

Pay back today, in full and with something extra, one debt to someone who never chased it, and ask nobody’s pardon. If you are owed, send the debtor one plain demand naming the sum.

Testament · Whom do you owe for a kindness they never mentioned, and who has been hoping you forgot?

Sources

[1] Jami at-Tirmidhi 889

[2] GASTAT, Hajj Statistics 1446H and 1447H

[3] Sahih Muslim 1218

[4] Sahih Muslim 1162b

[5] Sahih al-Bukhari 2449


The Sacrifice

Counter-rite · kept by Muslims

10 Dhu al-Hijjah

Admire no obedience that would kill a son.

The Testing of Abraham’s FaithGustave Doré · La Grande Bible de Tours, 1866

The Quran asks the boy, and he agrees. Abraham tells his son that he has seen in a dream that he must sacrifice him and asks what he thinks, and the son answers that his father should do as he is commanded and will find him patient, if the god wills[1]. When both have submitted and Abraham has laid the boy face down, the god calls out that the vision has been fulfilled and ransoms the son with a great sacrifice[2]. The Quran never names him. Most later Muslim scholarship says Ishmael, and Genesis, where the boy carries the wood for his own fire up the mountain, says Isaac[3].

Eid al-Adha falls on the tenth of the pilgrimage month, and families who can afford it slaughter a sheep, a goat, a cow or a camel and share the meat in thirds, for the household, for friends and for the poor. The Quran says what the god takes from the slaughter. Neither the meat nor the blood reaches the god[4], only the piety of the one who offers it, so what he collects every year is the readiness, the thing he collected on the mountain.

The story honors a father for being ready to kill his son on the word of a dream, and in the Quran’s telling it honors the son for consenting, which is worse, since it holds up a son agreeing to his own death as the model of faith. The ransom arrives only after the boy is laid face down, so the test was passed at the moment both had yielded. A command to kill a son is passed only by refusing it, and by that measure the man the feast honors failed, and a sheep pays for his failure at every Eid.

Declaration: Asked for my son, I would have walked down the mountain with the boy and let the god find another father.

The Rite

Roast lamb for adults you chose and eat it with your hands. Before the first cut, lay the knife flat beside the meat and say No dream gets the child, and give the best cut to the guest who came farthest.

Testament · Who pays for the obedience you were raised to admire?

Sources

[1] Quran 37:102

[2] Quran 37:103–107

[3] Gen 22:2–6

[4] Quran 22:37

The Other Rites

On 142 days the page prints one rite, labeled with the tradition it answers. The rites for the other traditions stand here by day. The rite for a reader raised in no faith, or in a faith not named, is the one marked no faith.


Days 1 to 121

Day 1 Of Wakingon the page: Christian

Catholic. Stand, say your own name, and make the Morning Offering to it, keeping the prayers, works, joys and sufferings and dropping every intention. I offer you this day’s prayers, works, joys and sufferings, and the whole of the profit is mine.

Orthodox. Stand, say your own name, and say the Jesus Prayer once to it with the plea for mercy struck out. Child of no god, I ask no mercy, and I am on my feet.

Latter-day Saint. Stand where you used to kneel, pray to yourself in the form you were taught to use for Heavenly Father, ask for nothing, and close in your own name. I say these things in my own name, amen.

Jehovah’s Witness. Leave the day’s text unread, stand, and say the psalm line Witnesses know with yourself as the maker of the day. This is the day that I have made, and I will rejoice in it.

Jewish. On waking, stand and say the Modeh Ani with yourself as the one thanked. I give thanks before myself, living and awake, for a soul that was never on loan.

Muslim. On waking, stand and say the words for rising from sleep with the praise turned on yourself. Praise be to me, who woke myself from sleep, and I go back to no one.

No faith. Stand, say your full name aloud, then turn away the guest of the old table grace, the god you were spared. Come, Lord Jesus, and be no guest of mine.

Day 3 Of Fallingon the page: Christian

Catholic. Say aloud the words your Church keeps for one who leaves, apostate or lapsed or fallen away, then say what you did in plain past tense. Lapsed, they call it. I chose the door.

Orthodox. Say aloud the Greek word your church uses for one who leaves, apostate, which means one who stands away, then give the plain verb. I stood away, on my own legs.

Protestant. Say aloud the word your church kept for people like you, backslider, the King James word for a heifer that would not be driven, then say what you actually did, in two words. I left.

Latter-day Saint. Stand as at a fast and testimony meeting and bear your testimony in the old words with one word changed. I know this church is not true, and I left it standing up.

Jehovah’s Witness. Say aloud whichever of the elders’ words fits you, inactive or disassociated or removed from the congregation, the new name for disfellowshipped, and add your own judgment of it. It is the best thing I have done.

Jewish. Say in English the phrase the Orthodox keep for those who leave, gone off the path, and then give the verb it hides. I walked off it.

Muslim. Say aloud the word the jurists keep for you, murtadd, which means one who turns back, and then answer it. I turned, and I am alive.

No faith. Say aloud the churches’ word for people raised outside them, lost, and then tell the god of Abraham where you have been standing the whole time. Here, on level ground, with no need of you.

Day 5 Of Favoron the page: Christian

Catholic. Say grace over whatever food or drink is in your hand, with the giver changed. Bless me, and these my gifts, which I am about to receive from my own work.

Protestant. Say aloud the name of the person whose approval you chased hardest in your church, then close the account between you for good. I am finished performing for you.

Latter-day Saint. Say aloud the question the bishop asked you in your recommend interview, whether you sustain the leaders of the Church, and answer it as one who has closed the audition. I sustain myself, and the audition is over.

Jehovah’s Witness. Say aloud the most hours you ever put on a field service report in one month, then give yourself the verdict nobody gave you. That was enough.

Jewish. Hold a piece of bread and say the blessing over it with yourself as the one who brought it forth. Blessed am I, who bring forth bread from the earth.

Muslim. Say in English the prayer Abraham and Ishmael made as they raised the foundations of the Kaaba, Our Lord, accept this from us, and then answer it yourself as the only judge present. Accepted, by me.

No faith. Say aloud the word people use when they claim the god of Abraham favored them, blessed, then close your audition with him. Keep your favor. I have my own.

Day 7 Of the Floodon the page: No faith

Christian. Name the one person behind a harm you have been charging to many, and answer that person alone today, by blocking the number or ending the favor, against Paul’s order to leave vengeance to the god. Say it as you act. Vengeance is mine.

Latter-day Saint. Fill a bath, go under once, and say the baptismal prayer over yourself with no priesthood holder present and no authority but your own. Having been commissioned by myself, I baptize myself in my own name.

Jehovah’s Witness. Phone one worldly friend, the kind the Society says Armageddon will sweep away as the flood swept Noah’s neighbors, and set a date to eat together. When you hang up, say it aloud. Nobody drowns for my sake.

Jewish. Eat a plate of pork while you read aloud the chapter where the god sorts the clean beasts from the unclean for the ark and then drowns the rest of both.

Muslim. Draw the beasts of the ark two by two on a sheet, each with its eyes, the pictures a hadith says their makers will be told to make alive. Say over each pair You drowned these. Breathe them back.

Day 8 Of Nakednesson the page: Christian

Protestant. Take the purity ring or pledge card you were given, or draw one, declare the vow void aloud, and say whose shame it really was. Then drop the ring among your loose change, or the card in the recycling.

Latter-day Saint. If you were endowed, put one set of temple garments in the trash uncut, or anything you wore for modesty’s sake if you were not, and hand the shame back aloud. That shame was never mine.

Jewish. Recite the Shema with nothing on, which the law forbids in the presence of uncovered flesh, keeping every word as you learned it. Then hand the shame back aloud. That shame was never mine.

Muslim. Take your own Quran in hand with nothing on and without first washing as for prayer, and read aloud from it slowly, the purity the jurists require ignored. Then hand the shame back. That shame was never mine.

No faith. Print Noah’s curse on his grandson with the blessing of the god of Shem that follows it, read both aloud, and curse that god by name for letting it stand, the blasphemy Leviticus punishes with stoning. Then throw the page out.

Day 10 Of Callingon the page: Christian

Catholic. Say Mary’s answer to the angel as the Angelus has it, Behold the handmaid of the Lord, then say it again with the owner removed. Behold the handmaid of no one. Be it done to me according to my word.

Protestant. Say aloud Isaiah’s answer to the call, Here am I, send me, then say it again with the one sent changed. Here am I. Send yourself.

Latter-day Saint. Say aloud the opening of a mission call, You are hereby called to serve, then write it on a card with yourself as the one served and sign it in your full name. I am hereby called to serve myself.

Jewish. Say Abraham’s answer when the god called him, Hineni, which means here I am. Then say it again with its owner named. Here I am, for me.

Muslim. Say the opening of the pilgrim’s Talbiyah, Here I am, O God, here I am, then say it again with the owner removed. Here I am, here I am, and no one owns me.

No faith. Say aloud the plan someone else drew up for you, the career or the town, in their words. Then say what it would have cost you in years, and turn the post down. I decline the post.

Day 12 Of Sodomon the page: Christian

Catholic. Lay a holy card of a saint face up on the table, bury the face in salt, and as you leave the room turn round and look at it. I looked back, and I am still standing.

Latter-day Saint. Open your hymnbook, or a printout of it, at Press Forward, Saints, pour salt over the page until the title is gone, then name aloud the one teaching from your years in the Church you never let yourself question, and question it. I looked back.

Jehovah’s Witness. The Watchtower has used Lot’s wife to warn Witnesses against missing the world. Pour salt over a copy you own, or a printed page of one, name aloud one worldly thing you miss, I miss it, and I am going back for it, and do it today.

Jewish. Open your own Chumash at the chapter where Lot’s wife looks back, pour salt over the page, and lick a pinch of it from the paper. She looked, and so do I.

Muslim. Copy in your own hand the verse where Lot tells the crowd his daughters are purer for them, write beneath it A prophet who says this to a mob is no guide of mine, and bury the page in salt.

No faith. Print the passage of Genesis where Lot’s wife looks back, bury it in salt on a plate by the door, and every time you leave the room today, stop and look back at it.

Day 14 Of Hopeon the page: Christian

Catholic. Say the opening of the Act of Hope, O my God, relying on your infinite goodness and promises, I hope, and stop there. Finish the sentence in the present tense. I hope for nothing. I have this day, and I am spending it.

Protestant. Say the old cry of the first Christians, Come, Lord, and answer it with how long it has gone unanswered. Nearly two thousand years. I have stopped waiting at the door.

Latter-day Saint. Sing the chorus line of the Primary song, Families can be together forever, then say aloud what you will do today with the people you love in this life, and do it. Together now, for as long as it lasts.

Jehovah’s Witness. Describe aloud the paradise in the Watchtower pictures, the lion beside the lamb and the fruit heaped in baskets, then buy the best fruit you can find and eat it today, in this system of things.

Jewish. Say the line of the creed that waits for the messiah, Though he tarry, I will wait for him every day, then say it again with the last clause changed. Though he tarry, I have stopped waiting.

Muslim. Say aloud the thing you have long promised yourself, with the if God wills the Quran tells believers to add to every plan, then strike the condition out and do it today, or the first part of it. I will.

No faith. Write on a slip of paper the thing you have put off longest, pin it where you will see it, and do it before the day is over, or the part of it you can afford without borrowing. Not someday. Today.

Day 15 Of Blessingon the page: Christian

Catholic. Raise your right hand as the priest does at the end of Mass, trace the cross over your own head, and give the blessing in your own name. I bless myself, and no priest need be in the room.

Latter-day Saint. Read aloud the line of your patriarchal blessing that declares your lineage, or say from memory the lineage you were told you came from, then pronounce your own in its place, naming what you want. I am of no tribe, and I bless myself.

Jewish. Raise your hands with the fingers parted in the priests’ sign, which only a descendant of Aaron may make over the congregation, and give the priestly blessing to yourself. May I be blessed and kept, by my own hand.

Muslim. Say the blessing you were taught to give others, may God bless you, then say your own name and bless yourself with God left out. I bless myself, and I ask no one’s leave.

No faith. Write your own blessing in Isaac’s form, what you want of heaven’s dew and the earth’s fat and whom you mean to outrank, sign it, read it aloud, and pin it above your bed.

Day 17 Of the Ladderon the page: No faith

Christian. Read Jacob’s vow at Bethel aloud with the parties reversed, as the one who now sets the terms. If I keep myself, feed myself and bring myself home, then I will be my own god.

Protestant. Say aloud the promise from Malachi you heard at offering time, that heaven’s windows open for the tither, then say the sum you gave over the years in your own figures. I paid every coin, and no window opened.

Latter-day Saint. Say aloud the verse in the Doctrine and Covenants that every blessing is predicated on obedience to a law, then name one blessing you obeyed for and never received. I kept the law, and the blessing never came.

Jehovah’s Witness. Say aloud what the Society teaches, that Christ began ruling in nineteen fourteen and the Kingdom will act soon, then name one person you knew who believed it and died waiting. The promise was never kept. It is void.

Jewish. Say Jacob’s condition at Bethel, that he would come back to his father’s house in peace, then name aloud what came to your own house instead. The condition failed, so the vow is void.

Muslim. Say aloud the verse in which God buys the believers’ lives and wealth in exchange for the garden, and then cancel the sale. My life and my wealth are not for sale.

Day 19 Of Fearon the page: No faith

Christian. Say the psalm’s line with yourself as the one who sets the table, I prepare a table before me in the presence of my enemies, then name aloud the one you fear and fetch the one fact that would confirm the fear or end it. I am ready.

Catholic. Say the old prayer to Mary, Remember, O most gracious Virgin Mary, that never was it known that anyone who fled to your protection, implored your help, or sought your intercession was left unaided, then name the one you fear and find the fact yourself.

Latter-day Saint. Sing Fear not, I am with thee from How Firm a Foundation as your own voice speaking to you, then name your adversary aloud, write the one question that would settle whether the fear is true, and send it today. I will stand.

Jehovah’s Witness. Say aloud the fear you were raised on, Armageddon will come before I grow up, and count the years it has failed to come. Then name the person you fear now and find out one fact about them today.

Jewish. Say the evening prayer’s plea, Remove the adversary from before us and from behind us, then name your own adversary aloud and find out today the one fact that would confirm the fear or end it.

Muslim. Say the answer the believers gave when told the people had gathered against them, God is enough for us, then say I am enough for myself, and name aloud the one gathering against you.

Day 21 Of Gluttonyon the page: No faith

Christian. Commit all five of Gregory’s ways of gluttony at one dinner, begun before the hour you usually eat, on the dearest dish you can buy, richly sauced, more than you need, and eaten with open appetite, with no grace before it and no penance after.

Orthodox. Eat a rich meat dinner, the meal your Church’s weekly fast days forbid, and take the first bite before the hour you usually eat.

Protestant. Order the richest plate you can and eat every bite of it slowly, with no grace before or after.

Latter-day Saint. Cook yourself the richest cut of meat you can buy, the flesh the Word of Wisdom holds back for times of cold or famine, and make a feast of it, a full plate eaten slowly and with pleasure.

Jehovah’s Witness. Raise a glass of wine, or whatever you drink, to your own appetite before a rich meal, the toast the Society says grew out of drinking to the gods, then eat the whole plate slowly and with pleasure.

Jewish. Eat bread and a rich meal until you are full, with no washing of hands before it and no grace after, though Deuteronomy commands a blessing whenever you have eaten and are full. I ate, I am full, and I bless no one.

Muslim. Eat the richest dish you can buy that has pork in it, slowly and past the third of the stomach the hadith leaves for food, then stop when you are full.

Day 22 Of Hardened Heartson the page: Christian

Catholic. Write on a card the sin you last named to a priest in the confessional, write under it the words by the hand of God, and burn the card in the sink.

Orthodox. Write on a card the sin you confessed with the priest’s stole over your head, write under it the words by the hand of God, and burn the card in the sink.

Latter-day Saint. Write on a card the sin you confessed to a bishop in a worthiness interview, write under it the words by the hand of God, and burn the card in the sink.

Jehovah’s Witness. Write on a card the doubt you were warned would carry you out of the truth, write under it the words by the hand of God, and burn the card in the sink.

Jewish. Write on a card the line of the Yom Kippur confession for the sin committed by hardness of heart, write under it the words by the hand of God, and burn the card in the sink.

Muslim. Write on a card the doubt you were told came from Satan, write under it the words by the hand of God, and burn the card in the sink.

No faith. Write on a card the sin a believer once told you that you were born in, write under it the words by the hand of God, and burn the card in the sink.

Day 24 Of Cattleon the page: Christian

Latter-day Saint. Spend an hour with a dog or a cat, yours or a friend’s with its owner’s leave, idling on the floor beside it, the idle time the Doctrine and Covenants forbids, with your whole attention on it.

Jehovah’s Witness. Spend an hour of the time you were raised to give to field service on a dog or a cat, yours or a friend’s with its owner’s leave, sitting with it and giving it your whole attention.

Jewish. Take a dog, yours or a friend’s with its owner’s leave, off its leash to run in a yard or an off-leash area, against the Mishnah’s rule that a dog be kept tied with chains, and play with it until it tires.

Muslim. Spend an hour with a dog its owner lets you meet, in the house if you are invited, and feed it from your hand before you part, against the hadith in Bukhari’s collection that has angels refuse a house with a dog.

No faith. Print the passage about the fifth plague and put it under the food bowl of a dog or cat, or a dish of seed for birds, so a beast gets some use from the god who killed Egypt’s herds.

Day 26 Of Limboon the page: Christian

Catholic. Print the canon that orders an infant in danger of death baptized without delay, or copy it out by hand, nail the page to a scrap of wood, and drive the nail through the word delay.

Latter-day Saint. Take the card or record of a baptism for the dead you performed, or write on paper the name of one dead person you were baptized for, and tear it in half. You were never mine to save.

Jehovah’s Witness. Go to the children’s graves in a cemetery near you and lay one small stone on a grave, with no tract or verse left beside it. You rest here, and no one decides who wakes.

Jewish. Say the mourner’s Kaddish aloud to its end for an infant who died before thirty days, a child the law sets outside formal mourning, yours or a friend’s.

Muslim. Copy out the hadith in which the Prophet, asked where the dead children of unbelievers go, answers that God knows best what they would have done, then strike through the answer and write your own beneath it. They had done nothing.

No faith. Print the Florence decree that sends those who die in original sin alone down into hell, fold it into a paper boat, and sink it in a basin of tap water until the ink runs.

Day 28 Of Desecrationon the page: No faith

Christian. Print a picture of the Virgin Mary, lay it in the bottom of your shower, and urinate on it. Run the water until it is pulp, then throw it away.

Orthodox. Lay an icon you own, or a printed one on stiff card, flat on the counter and use it as a board to cut raw meat, then wash it in the sink with the dishes.

Protestant. Slide your own whole Bible, or a thick stack of printed pages of one, under the short leg of a table you use every day, so the sermon holds up the dinner, and eat a meal at the table.

Latter-day Saint. If you were endowed, act out before a mirror the penalty signs the endowment used until nineteen ninety, laughing after each. If you never were, use your Book of Mormon or hymnbook as a coaster for a wet glass.

Jehovah’s Witness. Wedge a door open with your own New World Translation and leave it there as a doorstop, stepping over the name of Jehovah each time you pass.

Jewish. Throw your own prayer book, whole, with the Name of God on every page, into the trash can among the food scraps instead of the burial of worn holy books, and take the bag out.

Muslim. Lay the Quran you own on the floor inside your front door and wipe your feet on it as you come and go, the book the law says may never touch the ground. Keep it private.

Day 29 Of Plunderon the page: No faith

Christian. Sell or trade in one religious gift you were given, a study Bible, a plaque or a cross on a chain, and spend the same sum on yourself today, against the command to sell what you have and give to the poor.

Latter-day Saint. Spend a tenth of your last pay on something fine for yourself, the tenth the Church calls the Lord’s, and use it today.

Jehovah’s Witness. Take the sum you would once have put in the contribution box at the Kingdom Hall over a month, and spend it today on one fine thing for yourself.

Jewish. Take what you would drop in a tzedakah box over a month and spend it today on one fine thing for yourself.

Muslim. Open an account that pays interest, the riba the law forbids, with a first deposit of one month’s giving, and spend its first interest on one fine thing for yourself.

Day 31 Of the Seaon the page: Christian

Latter-day Saint. Break shop bread into a bowl of water and eat it, the sacrament of bread and water taken unworthily and on purpose, which the Book of Mormon says brings damnation. Name the drowned of Pharaoh’s army over it. I eat this for the drowned.

Jehovah’s Witness. Over a bowl of water, speak aloud to the drowned soldiers of Pharaoh as though they could hear, which Witnesses are taught the dead cannot do. You went down for his glory, and he gets no comfort from me.

Jewish. Take off your shoes and sit on the floor beside a bowl of water for an hour, as a mourner sits, though the law keeps that mourning for close kin, and mourn Pharaoh’s drowned. Horse and rider, I sit for you.

Muslim. Over a bowl of water, wail aloud for Pharaoh’s drowned army, for whom the Quran says neither heaven nor earth wept, and tear the collar of an old shirt, the mourning of the days of ignorance a hadith disowns. Do it alone.

No faith. Over a bowl of water, speak to Pharaoh’s drowned army. Every chariot in Egypt and every horse, I mourn you, and I comfort no god.

Day 33 Of Commandmentson the page: No faith

Christian. Draw the Ancient of Days, the god as Daniel saw him with hair like white wool, on a sheet of paper, the likeness the second commandment forbids, and carry it folded in your wallet for a week.

Catholic. Set the richest cake you can buy on a stand at the head of your table, light a candle before it as before a saint, and eat it slice by slice, the honor the Catechism calls idolatry when it goes to pleasure.

Orthodox. Turn an icon of Christ to face the wall, stand a mirror in its place, and bow to your own reflection with the sign of the cross. Before me, no other.

Latter-day Saint. Draw the First Vision with your own face in the pillar of light where the Father stands, carry it in a coat pocket for a week, another god set before him in your own house.

Jehovah’s Witness. Spill a glass of water across your own table on purpose and swear over the mess with the name you were taught to hold above every other word. Jehovah, look at that. Then wipe it up and eat a meal there.

Jewish. Shape a figure of the god of Sinai with a face out of bread dough, the very likeness the second commandment forbids, bake it, and eat it at your own table, face first.

Muslim. Draw a face for Allah, an image every school of the faith forbids outright, on any paper with any pen, and pin it inside a cupboard door.

Day 35 Of the Calfon the page: No faith

Christian. Cut from your own Bible the page where the Levites kill three thousand of their brothers, burn it in the sink, grind the ash between two spoons and strew it on a glass of water as Moses strewed the calf. Three thousand for a statue.

Catholic. Wrap a plaster saint you own, or a cheap one bought for this, in a cloth, pound it to powder with a hammer, and strew the dust on a bowl of water as Moses strewed the calf, then pour the bowl out on the earth.

Latter-day Saint. Cut the gold angel Moroni from a temple picture you own or print, grind the cutting to crumbs between your palms, and strew them on a bowl of water as Moses strewed the calf.

Jehovah’s Witness. With a yellow marker, draw a golden calf over the cover of a Watchtower you own and write Governing Body beneath it. Then tear it to crumbs, strew them on a sink of water as Moses strewed the calf, and pull the plug.

Jewish. Stack gold-wrapped chocolate coins into a calf on your own open prayer book, then unwrap them, crush the chocolate to crumbs over the page, strew the crumbs on a glass of water and drink it, as Moses made Israel drink theirs.

Muslim. Tear from your own Quran the page where Moses vows to burn the Samiri’s calf and scatter it in the sea, grind it to crumbs between your palms, and strew them on a bowl of water behind a closed door.

Day 36 Of Tabletson the page: Christian

Catholic. Pour the holy water you keep at the door down the sink, or bless a cup of tap water yourself and pour that out. Fill the font or a bottle with your best scent, and touch it to your throat before an hour of pleasure.

Latter-day Saint. Dress for an hour among strangers in the clothes your upbringing called immodest, bare shoulders or bare knees, the cut you were taught to measure against the garment line, and enjoy the looks.

Jehovah’s Witness. Raise a glass with someone you like and drink a toast to a rule you broke, the toasting custom The Watchtower traces to pagan offerings to the gods. To the rule, in pieces. Wine, or whatever you drink.

Jewish. Take the mezuzah from your front doorpost, or roll up a printed Shema if you never hung one, and fix it to the bathroom door, which the law leaves bare as no fit place for the Name. Run a long hot bath behind it.

Muslim. Say aloud a pleasure you will take within the hour and the time you will take it, plainly, without the inshallah the sura of the Cave commands for every plan, and take it at that time.

No faith. Write six hundred sixty-six across your forehead in eyeliner or ink, the other place Revelation sets the mark, and wear it at home through an hour of whatever pleasure you like best.

Day 38 Of Dissenton the page: No faith

Christian. Read aloud the words in John where the risen Christ gives his disciples the power to remit sins, which churches have read as an office for their clergy, and use it on a pleasure you once confessed. I remit it. Then take that pleasure again.

Catholic. Say over yourself, in the priest’s place, the absolution the Church reserves to him, for a pleasure you once confessed. I absolve you, in my own name. Make the sign of the cross over yourself, and take that pleasure again.

Orthodox. Drape a scarf over your bowed head as the priest lays his stole over a penitent, say the absolution over yourself for a pleasure you once confessed, I forgive and absolve you, then lift the scarf and take that pleasure again.

Latter-day Saint. Lay your hands on your head, whether or not you were ever ordained, and with the opening words of a priesthood blessing release yourself from a pleasure you once confessed to a bishop. By the authority I hold, I release you. Then take it again.

Jehovah’s Witness. Announce, in the voice of a Governing Body member, an adjusted understanding that releases you from a pleasure you once confessed to the elders, We now have an adjusted understanding, and this is no longer a sin, then take that pleasure again.

Jewish. Stand as the high priest stood on the Day of Atonement and say over yourself the words that were his alone, for a pleasure you confessed in the long list of that day. From all your sins you are clean. Then take it again.

Muslim. Write yourself a fatwa releasing you from a pleasure you once begged forgiveness for, sign it with your own name as mufti, the ruling a hadith says no one may give without knowledge, and act on it today.

Day 40 Of the Bronze Serpenton the page: Christian

Latter-day Saint. Take any olive oil and consecrate it aloud as the priesthood consecrates oil for the sick, though no one ordained you. I consecrate this oil. Then use it as plain oil on a squeaking hinge or a stiff lock.

Jehovah’s Witness. Wear a cheap cross on a chain for an hour at home, the shape the Society calls pagan, teaching that Jesus died on an upright stake, and while it hangs on you read John’s verse lifting the son of man as Moses lifted the serpent.

Jewish. Murmur over any sore spot, or over the back of your own hand, the verse in Exodus that names the god your healer, I am the Lord who heals you, the charm the Mishnah says forfeits the world to come. Then see to the body yourself.

Muslim. Hang a blue charm against the evil eye on your wall, bought for a few dollars or drawn on card, the kind of amulet a hadith says it is shirk to hang, and sit beneath it for ten minutes.

No faith. Draw the bronze serpent on its pole as Numbers describes it, write beneath it the creed you have made of your cure, and tear the drawing in two as Hezekiah broke the original. Keep using the cure.

Day 42 Of Jerichoon the page: No faith

Christian. Find the battle of Jericho in a children’s hymnbook or Bible you kept, and over the tumbling walls write what the next verse records, man and woman, young and old, put to the sword. Then put the book back on its shelf.

Latter-day Saint. Across a picture of Jericho’s falling walls from a Church manual or children’s book you own, or a print of one, write the next verse of Joshua, man and woman, young and old, put to the sword, and keep it with your scriptures.

Jehovah’s Witness. Write the next verse of Joshua, man and woman, young and old, put to the sword, across the falling walls in the Society’s children’s book of Bible stories, or across that page of your own New World Translation.

Jewish. In your own prayer book, across the Aleinu, which an old tradition credits to Joshua at Jericho, write the verse that tradition leaves out, man and woman, young and old, with the edge of the sword, and say it over the page.

Muslim. In your own Quran, across the verse of al-Ma’ida where Moses orders his people into the holy land the god has written for them, write in pencil what the book of Joshua says the entering cost Jericho. Man and woman, young and old, put to the sword.

Day 43 Of the Ferrymanon the page: No faith

Christian. Say aloud the cancellation of the passage someone booked for you when you were baptized or prayed over. I cancel my passage. I am staying on this side.

Catholic. Say the prayer for the dead with its petition reversed, and make yourself its subject while you are still alive. Eternal rest I decline. Let the light shine on me now, while I can see it.

Latter-day Saint. Say aloud the name of the kingdom you were raised to aim for, the celestial, and decline it. I decline the celestial kingdom. This one will do.

Jehovah’s Witness. Say aloud the promise you were taught to give at doorsteps, and then your own correction of it. You can live forever on a paradise earth. I will live once, here, and that is enough.

Jewish. Say the opening of the Kaddish with this life as its subject. Magnified and sanctified be this life, in the world as it is.

Muslim. Answer aloud the three questions the two angels are said to put to the dead in the grave, about your lord, your religion and your prophet. My lord is myself. My religion is this life. My prophet is no one.

Day 45 Of Achanon the page: Christian

Catholic. Write on a card the sin you last told a priest, or the one you never told, seal it in an envelope, and hide it under your mattress or a floorboard, as Achan hid the silver under his tent. This one stays out of the confessional.

Latter-day Saint. Write on a card what a bishop asked you about in a worthiness interview, or would ask, seal it in an envelope, and hide it under your mattress or a floorboard, as Achan hid the silver under his tent. That stays between me and me.

Jehovah’s Witness. Write on a card what the elders asked you, or would ask in a judicial hearing, seal it in an envelope, and hide it under your mattress or a floorboard, as Achan hid the silver under his tent. That is my business.

Jewish. Write on a card a wrong you once recited among the sins of the Yom Kippur confession, seal it in an envelope, and hide it under your mattress or a floorboard, as Achan hid the silver under his tent. This one I keep.

Muslim. Write on a card a sin you once told another person about, seal it in an envelope, and hide it under your mattress or a floorboard, as Achan hid the silver under his tent. This is hidden, and it is mine.

No faith. Write on a card something a parent, teacher or boss once made you confess, seal it in an envelope, and hide it under your mattress or a floorboard, as Achan hid the silver under his tent. This is mine.

Day 47 Of Aion the page: Christian

Catholic. Write your last failure on one line, and on the next the sin you would have confessed for it, and strike the second line through. Below, write the count you went in with and the true figure, and say aloud The count was wrong.

Orthodox. Write your last failure on one line, and on the next the sin a confessor would have named for it, and strike the second line through. Below, write the count you went in with and the true figure, and say aloud The count was wrong.

Protestant. Write your last failure on one line, and on the next the sin a sermon would have blamed for it, and strike the second line through. Below, write the count you went in with and the true figure, and say aloud The count was wrong.

Latter-day Saint. Write your last failure on one line, and on the next the unworthiness a bishop would have looked for, and strike the second line through. Below, write the count you went in with and the true figure, and say aloud The count was wrong.

Jehovah’s Witness. Write your last failure on one line, and on the next the spiritual weakness the elders would have named, and strike the second line through. Below, write the count you went in with and the true figure, and say aloud The count was wrong.

Jewish. Write your last failure on one line, and on the next the sin you would have atoned for, and strike the second line through. Below, write the count you went in with and the true figure, and say aloud The count was wrong.

Muslim. Write your last failure on one line, and on the next the sin you were told brought the trial, and strike the second line through. Below, write the count you went in with and the true figure, and say aloud The count was wrong.

No faith. Write your last failure on one line, and on the next the flaw of character you blamed for it, and strike the second line through. Below, write the count you went in with and the true figure, and say aloud The count was wrong.

Day 49 Of Victory Songson the page: Christian

Catholic. Tell the friends who stood with you how your last rival fell, in full and in detail, and let them cheer every part of it.

Orthodox. Turn the icons of your icon corner, or any holy picture you keep, to face the wall while you tell the friends who stood with you how your last rival fell, so the god sees none of it, and let them applaud.

Latter-day Saint. At Sunday dinner with friends, tell how your last rival fell and what it cost them, and laugh with the table for as long as the story lasts.

Jehovah’s Witness. Write down how your last rival lost, the rejoicing at an enemy’s fall that Proverbs forbids, read it aloud to friends at your table, and let them laugh. I enjoyed every word of that.

Jewish. Read aloud the proverb against rejoicing when your enemy falls, lest the LORD see it, then tell a friend at your table exactly how your last rival fell, and laugh. Let him see it.

Muslim. Tell a friend over a meal how your last rival lost, in full, and enjoy the telling, with no praise to God added at the end. I did this, and I enjoyed it.

No faith. Sing aloud the closing prayer of the song, that all the god’s enemies perish, then answer it with your own victory at a good dinner. So perish all your enemies, Lord. I am one of them, and I won.

Day 50 Of the Undecidedon the page: Christian

Catholic. Stand as at Mass for the Creed, say its first line aloud, then answer it cold. I do not believe in one God, and I will not be lukewarm about it.

Orthodox. Light the lamp before your icons, or a candle before any holy picture, then put it out with your fingers and leave it dark for the day. I will not burn lukewarm for you, so I will not burn at all.

Protestant. Say King Agrippa’s line aloud as the old English Bible gives it, then give your own answer to the god. Almost thou persuadest me, and almost is all you will get.

Latter-day Saint. Raise your right hand as at a sustaining vote in General Conference, and cast the vote almost nobody in that hall has ever cast. I am opposed.

Jehovah’s Witness. Name aloud one political question you were raised to stay neutral on, and take a side on it, out loud, for the first time. On this, I take a side.

Jewish. Say seven times, as the congregation does at the close of Yom Kippur, the line that declares who is god, with yourself in the Name’s place. I am the god.

Muslim. Recite al-Fatiha as far as the line that says you alone we worship and you alone we ask for help, then turn it on the speaker. Me alone I worship, and me alone I ask for help.

No faith. Say aloud to the god your culture raised everyone to answer to, in one sentence and with no softening, what you think of him. I was never yours, and I am not starting now.

Day 52 Of Vowson the page: No faith

Christian. Say aloud the promise made in your name at baptism, to renounce the devil and all his works, answer it I never promised that, and pour a glass of water down the drain for the font that sealed it.

Catholic. Write the promise made in your name at baptism across your confirmation certificate, or a plain card bearing your confirmation name, mark it released across the face, and tear it in two.

Protestant. Take the decision card or pledge card you signed at an altar call or in youth group, or write its words on a plain card, say each line aloud, and burn it over the sink. I signed it to please a room, and it binds nobody.

Latter-day Saint. Copy the covenant made at your baptism onto a card, or the temple covenants if you were endowed, cut the card into strips with scissors, and bin them. I swore it before I could weigh it, and it is void.

Jehovah’s Witness. Copy the baptism questions you answered yes to onto a sheet, say the dedication to Jehovah you made before baptism and answer it I take my dedication back, then tear the sheet in two and set the halves face down.

Jewish. Write the obligations of your bar or bat mitzvah across your certificate from it, or a plain card, and drop it in a bowl of water until the ink runs. I was handed these and give them back.

Muslim. Write the shahada you were taught as a child on a clean sheet, write across it that you witnessed nothing, and tear it in two. I witnessed nothing. Show it to no one.

Day 54 Of the Virtuous Paganson the page: Christian

Latter-day Saint. Pour a cup of water over your own head and say the name of a good person who died outside the faith, a baptism for the dead done by no priesthood holder in no temple. I stand for you, and no prophet shuts you out.

Jehovah’s Witness. Spend an hour with a person the elders would have you shun, or one the congregation would call worldly, if they welcome it, and tell them to their face that they are among the best people you know.

Jewish. Eat a dish cooked start to finish by non-Jewish hands, food the rabbis forbade for that reason, in honor of a righteous gentile you would seat above any sage.

Muslim. Name a good person who died outside Islam and ask mercy for them aloud, the request the Prophet was refused leave to make for his own mother. God’s mercy on you, whatever the book says.

No faith. Put a photograph of the best unbeliever you ever knew, or their name on a card, where you will see it, and say aloud what they were worth, every verdict of every council on them overruled.

Day 56 Of the Concubineon the page: Christian

Catholic. Strike through the approval printed on the front pages of your Catholic Bible, the approval canon eight hundred twenty-five requires of the Apostolic See or a bishops’ conference, or write it on paper and strike it, and say This book is condemned.

Protestant. Read the chapter of the Levite’s concubine aloud from the Bible with your name stamped on its cover, rip the chapter out and staple it to the front as the book’s indictment, then drop the book in the recycling. Scripture alone, and this is the scripture.

Latter-day Saint. Open your King James Bible to the chapter of the Levite’s concubine and bear your testimony over it as you were taught, ending I know this book is condemned, in my own name, amen. Then close it and put it in the bin.

Jehovah’s Witness. Read the chapter of the Levite’s concubine aloud from your own New World Translation, announce over it as elders announce a removal This book is no longer one of us, and leave it on the floor, back turned to it, through a meal.

Jewish. Read the chapter of the Levite’s concubine aloud from your own Tanakh, or a printout, then drop the book on the floor, where Jewish law forbids placing a religious book, and leave it there through a meal. This book is condemned.

Muslim. Read aloud one verse of your own Quran that excuses a man the women his right hand possesses, then draw a woman’s open hand in the margin beside it, for every woman a holy book handed over without a name. Keep it private.

No faith. Cut the chapter of the Levite’s concubine out of a Bible you own, or print it, read every line aloud, cut it into twelve pieces, and put them in the bin.

Day 57 Of Brideson the page: No faith

Christian. In your own Bible, beside the last chapter of Judges, where the elders promise to answer the fathers of the stolen girls, write Nobody asked the girls. Read it aloud and close the book.

Catholic. Read aloud the sixth commandment as your catechism gives it, then say in its place the only rule of sex you keep. My body answers for itself.

Latter-day Saint. In your own Doctrine and Covenants, across the verses that command Emma Smith to receive the wives given to Joseph or be destroyed, write in red ink Helen Mar Kimball, fourteen, and leave the book open on your table through a meal.

Jehovah’s Witness. Across a Watchtower article on a wife’s subjection to her husband’s headship, write She may refuse in marker over every paragraph, then tear the article into strips and bin them.

Jewish. Read the morning blessings from your own siddur or a printout as far as the thanks for not being made a woman, then write the line over in your own hand as thanks for being made as you were, and read it aloud.

Muslim. Read aloud the report in Bukhari where Aisha gives her own ages, six at the marriage and nine in his house, then answer it. Nobody asked her, and nobody answers for me. Keep it private.

Day 59 Of the Templeon the page: Christian

Latter-day Saint. Say aloud the thing you most often ask Heavenly Father for, stop without closing in the name of Jesus Christ and without amen, and do the first step of it yourself today.

Jehovah’s Witness. Write the thing you most often ask Jehovah for at the top of a Christmas wish list, the holiday Witnesses refuse, address it to yourself, sign it with your own name, and do the first item today.

Jewish. Eat something first, then say the line of the daily standing prayer that blesses the god who hears prayer, Blessed are you, who hears prayer, in the order the Talmud says casts him behind your back. Then do the first step of what you were about to ask for, yourself.

Muslim. Raise your open palms as in supplication, name the wish you most often ask Allah for, then wipe the empty hands down your face as the prayer ends. No one will grant this but me. Do its first step today.

No faith. Before a meal you love, say aloud the thing you most often wish for and name who will do the work of it. I will see to it, and no god will hear of it.

Day 61 Of Judgeson the page: No faith

Christian. Say aloud the line of the Creed that has him coming again to judge the living and the dead, then answer it as your own counsel. I speak for myself, and the case is closed.

Catholic. Say the prayer the rosary adds after each decade, O my Jesus, forgive us our sins, save us from the fires of hell, and answer the judge who lit them. Save me from nothing. I sit in judgment here.

Latter-day Saint. Say aloud the title the Church gives a bishop, a common judge in Israel, and then take the bench yourself. I am the only common judge in my house.

Jehovah’s Witness. Say aloud what Witnesses are taught about the end, Judgment Day will last a thousand years, and then pass judgment on yourself in a single sentence. I have judged myself, and I am acquitted.

Jewish. Read aloud the Yom Kippur prayer of who shall live and who shall die, and wherever it has the god writing and sealing, answer the line. I hold the pen.

Muslim. Write one page of your own record for this week, the deeds you are glad of, read it aloud, and sign it. I have read my own record, and I approve it.

Day 63 Of Lookingon the page: Christian

Catholic. Watch an hour of a film the Church’s Legion of Decency once rated condemned, which Catholics pledged every year not to see, with a bowl of something you love.

Protestant. Spend an hour looking at painted nudes in an art book or on a museum site, the sight your youth group’s purity teaching told you to avert your eyes from, and let your eyes rest on each one.

Latter-day Saint. Watch an hour of a documentary on the Church’s history made by a former member, the kind your leaders warned the faithful to switch off, and watch it to the end of the hour.

Jehovah’s Witness. Spend an hour watching videos of former Witnesses telling why they left, the sort of material Witnesses are taught to switch off, and look at every face.

Jewish. Look for a full minute at a photograph of a rainbow, the sight the Talmud says shows no regard for the honor of the god, then at the next, and keep going for an hour.

Muslim. Spend an hour looking at medieval Persian paintings that show the Prophet’s face, made by Muslims for Muslim patrons, and when one meets your eye, look back.

No faith. Spend an hour looking at paintings of the god’s face as the painters drew him, an old man in a cloud, since the book says nobody sees that face and lives. Look back at each one.

Day 64 Of Amalekon the page: No faith

Christian. Black out Samuel’s order against Amalek in your own Bible, infant and suckling included, then find the law in Deuteronomy that orders the straying brother stoned and black that out too.

Protestant. Read aloud Samuel’s order to spare neither infant nor suckling in the bright voice of a youth pastor announcing a memory verse, then black the verse out in your own Bible and write your name in the margin beside it.

Latter-day Saint. Black out Samuel’s order against Amalek in the King James Bible you were given, and write beside it Mountain Meadows, the massacre in which Mormon militia killed some hundred and twenty emigrants and spared only the small children.

Jehovah’s Witness. Black out Samuel’s order to spare neither infant nor suckling in your own New World Translation, and write your name in the margin beside the blank.

Jewish. Read aloud the law in Deuteronomy that orders the brother who urges you toward other gods stoned, with your own hand first upon him. Black out the words that tell you not to spare him, in your Chumash or a printout, and say I spare him.

Muslim. Read aloud the verses on the people brought down from their fortresses in the chapter of the Confederates, then black them out in your own Quran with a thick marker. Post nothing.

Day 66 Of Heresyon the page: Christian

Catholic. Spend what a Mass for your dead would cost on one pleasure of your own, and say over the first taste The dead have no use for this, and I do.

Latter-day Saint. Say aloud The soul dies with the body. Then tear the vision of the three degrees of glory out of your own Doctrine and Covenants, drop it in the kitchen bin, and eat a rich meal at the table. No degrees of glory, only this table.

Jehovah’s Witness. Take down the photograph of a dead relative you were promised to meet in the paradise, set it at your table, and eat their favorite meal across from it. I will not wait for you. I loved you here.

Jewish. Say aloud The soul dies with the body. Then strike out the last line of the Ani Maamin in your siddur or a printout, the belief in the resurrection of the dead, and eat the best meal you can afford. I believe in this table with perfect faith.

Muslim. Say aloud The soul dies with the body. Then eat from a silver or silver-plated spoon, from a drawer or a thrift shop, the vessel a hadith forbids now and promises hereafter. I take it here.

No faith. Say aloud the heresy a council in Rome condemned in fifteen thirteen, The soul dies with the body, then do today the one thing you had been saving for later.

Day 68 Of Evil Spiritson the page: No faith

Christian. Name the demon the desert monks gave your fiercest appetite, gluttony, lust or sloth, then take the pleasure it was said to tempt you toward, slowly and fully, and say Now that you are fed, you are only an appetite.

Catholic. Write on a card the line the Saint Benedict medal throws at Satan, What you pour is evil. Drink your own poison. Set it face down beside your glass, and pour yourself what you like best, wine or cocoa, to the last drop.

Latter-day Saint. Swear aloud, alone, in every word you were told never to say, until your fiercest anger is spent, the anger the Book of Mormon gives to the devil as father of contention. That was mine, and no devil fathered it.

Jehovah’s Witness. Watch a horror film the Society’s warnings say draws demons, start to finish, lights on and a snack in your lap, and say at the credits Nothing came for me.

Jewish. Eat and drink in pairs, two eggs, two glasses of wine or water, two of everything, the even numbers the Talmud says expose a person to demons, and enjoy each one.

Muslim. Eat a meal with your left hand and drink with it too, the way a hadith says Satan does, leave the cup uncovered beside you, and say no bismillah over any of it. Enjoy every mouthful.

Day 70 Of Necromancyon the page: No faith

Christian. Across the verse in Leviticus that orders a medium stoned, write in your own Bible the name of someone your church warned you against who fed you, and leave the book open beside your plate while you eat.

Latter-day Saint. On the page of your own Book of Mormon that carries the testimony of the witnesses, write the name of someone the Church warned you against who fed you, and bear testimony of them aloud. I know that they fed me.

Jehovah’s Witness. Write across the cover of a Watchtower the name of a disfellowshipped person who was kind to you, someone you were told not to greet, and say it aloud. I name them, and I thank them. Pin the cover where you eat.

Jewish. Bake unleavened bread as the woman did for Saul, set it on your table, and call aloud on the prophet Samuel. When nobody rises, say aloud who fed you and what they did, and eat the bread in that person’s honor.

Muslim. In the margin of your own Quran, beside the verse on the sorcery taught at Babylon, write the name of whoever fed you when you were warned against them. Then eat a loaf in their honor, saying their name aloud before the first bite.

Day 71 Of Popeson the page: No faith

Christian. Read aloud the verse in Matthew that forbids calling any man on earth father or master. Then strike every clergy title from a bulletin or a printout of a church’s staff page, and say one clergyman’s plain name aloud with no title before it.

Catholic. Write to your bishop by his plain first and last name, with no Excellency before it, ask him how many accusations sit in his diocese’s secret archive, and mail the letter.

Latter-day Saint. Read aloud the First Presidency statement of nineteen forty-nine that called the priesthood ban a direct commandment from the Lord, printed or on a screen. Cross out the Lord, write in Brigham Young, and keep the page in your scriptures.

Jehovah’s Witness. Play a Witness video broadcast, stop it at the first moment a Governing Body member tells you to give up a pleasure, and spend an hour enjoying exactly that pleasure.

Jewish. Write yourself a ruling in the rabbis’ form, permitting one thing your rabbi forbade, sign it with your plain name and no title, and act on it today.

Muslim. Say aloud the plain name of the scholar whose rulings you were raised under, with no Sheikh or Imam before it, and strike the title off one printed page or book cover you own.

Day 73 Of Messengerson the page: Christian

Catholic. Say the prayer to your guardian angel that you learned as a child, Angel of God, my guardian dear, and at its end release the guardian. You may go. I keep myself.

Latter-day Saint. Tell aloud the story Joseph Smith gave of an angel with a drawn sword who threatened him until he took plural wives, and answer the angel. Put it away. I marry whom I choose.

Jehovah’s Witness. State aloud the Witness teaching that Jesus is Michael the archangel, and then dismiss him by that name. Michael, you may go.

Jewish. Say only the last verse of the Sabbath-table song to the ministering angels, the one that sends them on their way, and mean it. Go in peace, and do not come back.

Muslim. Turn your head right and then left, as at the end of salah, toward the two angels said to sit on your shoulders recording your deeds, and dismiss them. Peace be upon you. Your work here is finished.

No faith. Sing, to any tune, a line saying you are only passing through this world, and answer it aloud. I live here, and I like the food.

Day 75 Of Sinon the page: Christian

Catholic. Read the Gospel aloud at your table and preach a homily on it yourself, whoever you are, the sermon canon law reserves to priests and deacons, and answer Amen.

Latter-day Saint. Lay your hands on your own head and bless yourself aloud in the words of a priesthood blessing, the act reserved to ordained men. If you are a man, say the sacrament prayer over bread and water alone at your table instead.

Jehovah’s Witness. Stand in your own room and give a five-minute talk aloud on a scripture, in your own interpretation and from no outline, the discourse Witness women do not give to the congregation and Witness men give only from outlines the organization supplies.

Jewish. Listen for an hour to a woman singing, the voice the Talmud calls nakedness, and sing along if you know the words. If you are a woman, sing aloud yourself for an hour.

Muslim. Take off your hijab and go out uncovered for one errand, by your own choice, somewhere no believer will know you. If you never wore one, wear for the same errand whatever your tradition calls immodest on you.

No faith. Find the verse in First Timothy that says the woman was deceived and the man was not, read it aloud, strike it through on a printout, and say aloud the name of a woman who taught you something.

Day 77 Of Wallson the page: Christian

Catholic. Draw a cross in chalk on the inside of your front door, the cross inscribed on the lintel in the Epiphany blessing of homes, and scrub it off with a wet rag while saying Nothing comes in here by right. Then lock the door.

Latter-day Saint. Write to your bishop asking that no ministering visitors be assigned to your home, send it today, then lock your front door. This door is shut.

Jehovah’s Witness. Hang a holiday wreath on the inside of your front door, the decoration Witnesses refuse as pagan, and bolt the door with it hanging there. No elder comes past this wreath.

Jewish. Read aloud how Abraham ran from his tent door to bring strangers in, then bolt your own door and answer no knock for an hour, the welcome refused. My tent has one door, and I keep it.

Muslim. Hang a picture of a living face, printed or drawn, inside your front door, the image a hadith says keeps the angels out of a house, and turn the bolt.

No faith. Write on a card that the god of Abraham and everyone who calls in his name is refused at this door, tape it inside the door where only you will read it, and turn the bolt. You are refused at this gate.

Day 78 Of the Rockon the page: No faith

Christian. Read aloud the god’s sentence on Moses at Kadesh, then answer it by using the god’s name as an oath in full voice, the third commandment broken for his sake. God damn this sentence.

Catholic. Say the act of contrition aloud with every sin you confess replaced by a boast, and eat something sweet where the penance would have been.

Jehovah’s Witness. Say aloud one thing you put off for the new system the Witnesses promised, the degree, the child, the house or the trip, and take the first step toward it today. I am done waiting at the border.

Jewish. Open your own Tanakh, or a printout of the passage, at the place where Moses strikes the rock, strike the page twice with a wooden spoon, and drink a glass of water over it.

Muslim. Drink a glass of water standing up, the way a hadith in Sahih Muslim forbids, slowly to the last drop, and say The rock gave it all the same.

Day 80 Of Jealousyon the page: Christian

Latter-day Saint. Set a place at your table for Heavenly Mother, the goddess your Church says exists and a prophet called it inappropriate to address, and tell her what you mean to do.

Jehovah’s Witness. Wear a charm of the kind Witnesses are taught to avoid, a lucky coin or a bead against the evil eye, or draw one on your wrist, for as long as you like.

Jewish. Set a small clay goddess, or a drawing of one, between your Sabbath candles or any two candles, light them for Asherah, whom some of the god’s own worshipers named beside him, and say This light is for the goddess at his side.

Muslim. Swear an oath today by your own life, the oath a hadith counts as shirk because it is sworn by something other than Allah, and keep it. By my life, I will finish this.

No faith. Set photographs of everyone you love side by side on one shelf, the friends a jealous partner or a jealous god would have you drop, and leave them there together.

Day 82 Of Relicson the page: No faith

Christian. Take the cross necklace, bracelet or devotional you still keep out of unease, and put it in the trash.

Catholic. Put your blessed palm in the ordinary trash with the potato peelings, the sacramental the Church says must be burned or returned, or with no palm any blessed medal or holy card you keep, and take the bag out.

Orthodox. Put the blessed candle you carried home from the Paschal service, or any other blessed object you keep, out with the kitchen trash.

Latter-day Saint. Throw away your copy of your patriarchal blessing, the one you have been afraid to lose, or any card, certificate or keepsake from the church you keep out of unease, and keep no copy anywhere.

Jehovah’s Witness. Throw the keepsake of your baptism, the photograph from the assembly pool or the card from that day, into the ordinary trash with the kitchen scraps.

Jewish. Cut the fringes from the small four-cornered garment you own and put them in the trash, or if you never owned one, throw out any ritual object you kept from unease, a kippah or a mezuzah case.

Muslim. Pour the Zamzam water you were given down the sink and use the bottle for something ordinary. If you have none, put the prayer beads or printed prayer you keep as a charm in the trash.

Day 84 Of Hailon the page: Christian

Catholic. Go outside after dark and say under the open sky I refuse your mercy and I will not repent, the hardness the Catechism names as the sin forgiveness cannot reach. Stand a full minute where the hail would land, then go in.

Orthodox. Take your prayer rope outside after dark, say under the open sky The Holy Spirit is an unclean spirit, and stand a full minute with the rope in your fist. Then go in and hang it on a hook by the door.

Latter-day Saint. Go outside after dark and say under the open sky I deny the Holy Ghost, whom I once received, the denial your scripture reserves for perdition. Stand a full minute, then go in and cook yourself the best meal you can.

Jehovah’s Witness. Go outside after dark and say under the open sky Jehovah be damned, cursing the name you were taught to sanctify above every other duty. Stand a full minute, then go in, put on music and dance until you are out of breath.

Jewish. Go outside after dark and eat a food your law forbids in the open air, the deliberate profaning of the Name the Talmud says no Day of Atonement can wipe away. Say between bites I meant it, and I am still here, and stand a minute before going in.

Muslim. Go outside after dark where no one can overhear and say under the open sky Allah has a partner, the one sin the Quran says he does not forgive. Stand a full minute, then go in. Skip this wherever being heard would be dangerous.

No faith. Go out after dark, look up, and say The Holy Spirit is an unclean spirit, the sentence the gospels put past all forgiveness. Count sixty slowly with your face to the sky, then go in and sleep.

Day 85 Of the Deserton the page: Christian

Orthodox. Eat in one sitting the whole forbidden table of the strictest Orthodox fast, meat, cheese, butter and olive oil together in one dish, slowly and with attention.

Jehovah’s Witness. Eat a long, rich meal that ends in a whole bag of chocolate eggs, the Easter sweet Witnesses refuse, in the hour field service used to take.

Jewish. Eat a meal of meat and then, without the wait your community keeps between meat and milk, a bowl of ice cream, slowly.

Muslim. Cook a dish at home with meat bought without a thought for who slaughtered it or what was said, the food the Quran forbids unless Allah’s name was mentioned over it, and eat it slowly, to the last of the plate.

No faith. Read aloud how the devil told the fasting Jesus in the desert to turn stones into bread, then bake or buy a loaf and eat it warm, the devil’s advice taken.

Day 87 Of Holy Wateron the page: Christian

Catholic. Stir a pinch of salt into a bowl of water, hold your hand over it and say Every unclean thing out of this salt and water, by my word and no bishop’s, then sprinkle your bed with it.

Latter-day Saint. Lay both hands on a pitcher of water, the gesture your Church keeps for ordained men, and say By no priesthood but my own, I bless this water, then drink from it.

Jehovah’s Witness. Fill a glass with water, raise it and say Blessed be this water in my own name, and in no other, then drink it down.

Jewish. Hold up a cup of water and say Blessed am I, who make this water holy by my own word, then pour it over your hands as the law does before bread.

Muslim. Say over a glass of water a short blessing of your own making that ends by my name and by no other, blow on the water as the ruqyah reciters do, and drink it.

No faith. Look up the free ordination a church offers anyone online and decline it, then hold your hand over a jug of tap water, say I bless this by my own authority, and drink a glass of it.

Day 89 Of the Abysson the page: Christian

Latter-day Saint. Take an hour you once gave a Church calling, spend it beginning the large thing you want for yourself, and say when the hour ends This hour was consecrated to me.

Jehovah’s Witness. Give an hour to the biggest thing you have wanted to make or build, the ambition Witnesses are taught to set below Kingdom interests, and sign your own name on the first page of it.

Jewish. Write out the tenth commandment by hand, name beneath it the one thing of your neighbor’s you want most, and spend the next hour beginning your own on the scale you want.

Muslim. Stand at a mirror and say aloud I am the greatest of those I know, the pride the Prophet said keeps a man out of Paradise at the weight of a mustard seed, then spend the next hour beginning the large thing.

No faith. Begin the large thing you have kept small, with the first page, the first sketch or the first board, and say aloud This is the sin of pride, and I have begun it.

Day 91 Of Divorceon the page: Christian
