Catholic. Write and sign a decree declaring your baptism null for want of your consent, the ground on which the Church annuls marriages, and pin it over your crucifix. Then sell a medal or rosary you were given and spend the money on yourself.

Orthodox. Sell the cross hung on you at baptism, or a ring the priest blessed at a wedding now dissolved, to a gold buyer, and spend all of it on yourself. Say over the money I put you away.

Latter-day Saint. Sell the leather scriptures or any gift the church gave you, or the ring from a temple marriage since ended in divorce, and spend the money on yourself. Say over the receipt For time only, and the time is up.

Jehovah’s Witness. Write and sign a bill of divorce to Jehovah on your own grounds, which no elder would accept, and fold it into your New World Translation at the flood. Then spend the price of a good dinner out on yourself.

Jewish. Write a get releasing yourself from the god of Israel, in his words from Jeremiah, I have put you away and given you a bill of divorce. Sign it, tear it across as a rabbinic court tears a delivered get, and spend a good dinner’s price on yourself.

Muslim. Alone in an empty room, say I divorce you three times in one sitting to the faith you were raised in, the triple divorce most Sunni jurists call sinful and still count binding. Then buy yourself a gift worth the price of a feast.

No faith. Print the marriage service’s line that no man put asunder what God has joined, cut it into single words, throw them out, and spend an hour’s pay on yourself the same day.

Day 92 Of the Dark Woodon the page: No faith

Christian. Go alone to a bar, a club or a dance floor your church called the path of the wicked, and stay a full hour with your back to the wall, watching the whole room. I am out, and I like it here.

Protestant. Go alone to a dance floor your church warned you off and dance for a full hour, alone in the crowd, to music the youth pastor would have switched off.

Latter-day Saint. Go alone to a coffee shop your ward would never enter, order the strongest coffee on the board, and drink it slowly through a full hour, the Word of Wisdom broken at a table by the window.

Jehovah’s Witness. Go alone for an hour to a bar, a club or any gathering your elders called bad association, and talk with a stranger there for as long as you enjoy it.

Jewish. Go alone for an hour to a bar, a diner or any place your upbringing called unfit, order something unkosher from its kitchen, shellfish or a bacon roll, and eat it there to the last bite.

Muslim. Go alone for an hour to a bar your family called unclean, order a glass of wine, or whatever you drink, and finish it slowly at a table facing away from Mecca.

Day 95 Of Prideon the page: Christian

Orthodox. Stand at a mirror and sign yourself right to left, then lower your hands and say Glory to you. to your own eyes. Bow to nothing.

Latter-day Saint. Stand alone and bear your testimony aloud in the pulpit form you learned as a child, with yourself as its subject. I know that I am good, and I say it in my own name.

Jehovah’s Witness. Wear your best clothes, or the most expensive label you own, where it can be read, the ostentation the New World Translation calls worldly, for the next two hours. Then say I earned this, and I enjoy it.

Jewish. Walk four cubits, about six feet, bareheaded and in the upright posture the Talmud forbids because the Presence fills the earth, then say Nothing is above my head.

Muslim. Begin one cycle of salah, and at the point of prostration stay standing, as Iblis refused to bow when the angels bowed to Adam. I will not bow.

No faith. Stand where you would once have been told to kneel and say your own name and what you made or survived in the full voice of a creed. I believe in me, maker of what I have made.

Day 97 Of Sullennesson the page: No faith

Christian. Drop your own crucifix, or a cheap one bought for the purpose, into a basin of water, weight it with a stone, and leave it under for the hour you give the mood.

Catholic. Drop an unconsecrated wafer, or a plain cracker, into a glass of water and let it go soft through the hour. This is the body of no one. Pour it down the sink when the hour ends.

Orthodox. Say aloud Give me not a spirit of despondency, then answer I keep my despondency. Lay a printed picture of the Mother of God, or your own icon, face down in a basin of water for the hour.

Protestant. Tear the psalm that tells the downcast soul to hope in God out of your own Bible, use it through the hour to wipe your eyes and nose, then drop it in a sink of water and pull the plug.

Latter-day Saint. Close the door, put music on loud, and paint your own Book of Mormon solid black with a brush and a pot of black paint, cover and every page, until the hour ends. Let it dry open on newspaper.

Jehovah’s Witness. Over a basin of water, read aloud a Watchtower article about Satan as he would read it, slowly and amused, then drop the magazine in and leave it under for the hour you give the mood.

Jewish. Copy the Shema by hand in washable ink. Drop the page in a basin of water and leave it under for the hour, until the Name has run to a gray smear, the erasing the rabbis forbid. Bin the pulp.

Muslim. Lay your own Quran, or a printout of one sura, in a basin of water on the bathroom floor and leave it there for the hour. Show no one.

Day 99 Of Wrathon the page: Christian

Latter-day Saint. Alone, read aloud from the Book of Mormon He that hath the spirit of contention is not of me, but is of the devil, then say the name of the one who earned your anger, and exactly what they did, in full voice to the empty room.

Jehovah’s Witness. Alone, swear aloud at whoever earned your anger, in the words the elders called unclean speech, and keep going until you run out of breath.

Jewish. In shoes, on a hard floor, break a plate you own inside a cloth bag, against the ban on needless destruction and the Talmud’s likening of a vessel-breaker in anger to an idolater. Say the name of the one who earned it as the plate breaks.

Muslim. Alone, curse the one who earned your anger by name, aloud, and refuse the ablution a hadith prescribes for putting anger out. Say I seek refuge in myself and keep the anger whole.

No faith. Alone, at full voice, tell the god who kept anger for himself and denied it to his subjects exactly what you think of the arrangement, until your voice gives out. I am angry, and I keep it.

Day 102 Of Mammonon the page: Christian

Latter-day Saint. Fill in a tithing slip, or a sheet ruled like one, with your whole yearly wage where the tenth would go. Read it aloud to the people you live with, or to the room, and keep the slip in your own wallet.

Jehovah’s Witness. Write your yearly wage on a slip like the unsigned ones dropped into a Kingdom Hall contribution box, sign it with your full name, and read it aloud to the people you live with, or to the room. Pin it where they will see it.

Jewish. Write your yearly wage on a card, say it aloud at your table to the people you live with, or to the room, and leave the card face up on the table until the week is out.

Muslim. Say aloud to the people you live with, or to the room, your yearly wage and the savings your zakat is reckoned on, then write both figures on a sheet and leave it on the table for the day.

No faith. Set a coin or note marked In God We Trust, or a British coin with the Latin by the grace of God, on a sheet, write your yearly wage beneath it, and say it aloud to someone you live with, or to the room, then say I trust in me.

Day 104 Of the Brambleon the page: Christian

Protestant. Step down today, in a one-line message, from one church or volunteer post, the board seat, the rota or the youth group. Then eat a bunch of grapes slowly, the fruit of the vine that refused. I keep my fruit.

Latter-day Saint. Ask your bishop today, in one written sentence, to release you from your current calling, or tell him you will decline the next. Then eat a handful of olives slowly. I keep my fruit.

Jehovah’s Witness. Write to the elders, in one sentence, that you will take no further assignment at the Kingdom Hall, no talk and no cleaning shift. Eat a fig slowly while it sends. I keep my fruit.

Jewish. Decline today, in one written sentence, a seat on a synagogue board, a committee or a rota. Then dip bread in olive oil, the oil the olive says honors God and man, and eat it. I keep my fruit.

Muslim. Decline today, in one written sentence, a mosque committee, a family duty or an extra post at work that would take your evenings. Then eat figs and olives, the two fruits sworn by in Surat al-Tin. I keep my fruit.

No faith. Turn down today, in one written sentence, a committee seat, an extra duty or a promotion that would pull you off your own work. Buy a potted fig, olive or vine and set it where you work. I keep my fruit.

Day 106 Of Millstoneson the page: No faith

Christian. Wear closed shoes. Wrap your own cross, or two sticks tied with string, in a towel on a paving slab and drop a stone you can hold in both hands on it from knee height. Say aloud the deed you hid, then your full name.

Catholic. Lay a saint’s medal of your own, or a cheap one bought for the purpose, on a flat stone and grind it under a heavier stone turned like a hand mill. Say aloud the deed you hid, then your full name over what is left.

Orthodox. Write the deed you hid on the back of a paper icon and sign your full name across the front. Stand it on your shelf face out for the day.

Protestant. Lay your own Bible flat on the floor and stand on it with both feet, one hand on the wall, and say aloud the deed you hid, then your full name. Step down and leave it where it lies for the rest of the day.

Latter-day Saint. Cut the title page from your own Book of Mormon with scissors, or print one out, and write your full name across it. Say the deed you hid aloud, then your name, crush the page underfoot, and add I am the author and proprietor of what I did.

Jehovah’s Witness. Cut the masthead off a Watchtower cover and paste your full name in its place, then write the deed you hid across the cover. Say I did this, and my name is on it.

Jewish. Grind a handful of wheat between two stones, the household work the Thebez stone was cut for, then write the deed you hid in the flour with one finger. Say the deed aloud, then your full name.

Muslim. Write the shahada on a sheet and your own full name beneath it, fold it with your name outside, and leave it under the heaviest stone you can lift until night. Say aloud the deed you hid, then your full name. Keep it private.

Day 109 Of Temptationon the page: Christian

Orthodox. Put on a mask, or tie a scarf over your face, and dance alone to loud music until you are out of breath, the masks and dances a church council forbade in six ninety-two.

Protestant. Watch, in one sitting, a film your church or youth group warned against, or the one you suspect they would have, and enjoy it to the credits.

Latter-day Saint. Play loudly, from start to finish, a song with the vulgar or offensive lyrics the Church’s older youth pamphlet told you to avoid, and sing along with every word.

Jehovah’s Witness. Read the opening chapters of a novel about wizards or vampires, the magic in entertainment the Watchtower warns Witnesses away from, in one sitting, and enjoy every page of it.

Jewish. Hold the hand of a consenting adult friend who is not your spouse or close kin, or hug one, the touch the rabbis fenced off, for as long as you like. If no one is near, eat shellfish or bacon slowly.

Muslim. Take the second look the hadith counts against you, at a film, a painting or a friend who has looked at you first, and hold it as long as you enjoy it, without lowering your gaze.

No faith. Print a picture of Saint Anthony’s temptation, cut the saint out and throw him away, and pin up the rest, every creature of it, where you eat. Eat there, beside it, the meat or sweet the old church would have refused you.

Day 111 Of the Gluttonon the page: Christian

Protestant. Eat a long meal with a friend your church called a bad influence, somewhere your youth group would have steered you away from, and order whatever you both want.

Jehovah’s Witness. Share a long meal with a relative or friend who was removed from the congregation, at your table or theirs, and stay until you have both said everything you wanted to say.

Jewish. Sit down to a long meal at the table of a friend who is not Jewish and eat their bread, the loaf the rabbis forbade lest friendship over it lead to marriage, and stay until you are both content.

Muslim. Share a long meal with someone who left Islam, or a friend your family would not seat, eat from one dish together, and stay until you have both said everything you came to say.

No faith. Order a platter meant for two and share it with a friend of another faith or someone who left a church, and stay at the table until the plate is clean and the talk runs out.

Day 113 Of the Spectacleon the page: No faith

Christian. In your own Bible, black out the holy angels and the Lamb in the verse of Revelation where the damned are tormented in their presence. Then send someone your church shamed two plain sentences on their side.

Catholic. Cut every saint out of the upper half of a print of the Last Judgment, one you own or print, and paste them face down among the damned. Then send someone your church shamed two plain sentences on their side.

Orthodox. Make three full prostrations, forehead to the floor, before a sheet bearing the name of someone your church shamed, the bow the Liturgy gives the holy things. Then send someone your church shamed two plain sentences on their side.

Protestant. In your own Bible, cross out every alleluia Revelation sings over a city burning for ever, and write the word Shame beside each one. Then send someone your church shamed two plain sentences on their side.

Latter-day Saint. In your own Book of Mormon, or a printout, write your ward’s name across Lehi’s great and spacious building and black out the verse where those below are ashamed. Then send someone your church shamed two plain sentences on their side.

Jehovah’s Witness. Print one picture of the saved and one of the destroyed at Armageddon, or use any pictures of the saved and the lost. Paste the smiling saved among the dead. Then send someone shunned by your congregation two plain sentences on their side.

Jewish. Print the psalm in which the righteous wash their feet in the blood of the wicked, soak the page in a basin of water, and wash your own feet in it. My feet are clean of their joy. Then send someone your community shamed two plain sentences on their side.

Muslim. In your Quran, in the sura of those who stand in ranks, black out the words of the man in paradise looking down at his old friend in the fire. Then send someone your community shamed two plain sentences on their side. Do it unseen.

Day 116 Of Guideson the page: Christian

Catholic. Say aloud the seven gifts of the Holy Spirit as you learned them for confirmation, and at the gift of counsel stop and take it back. Counsel is mine, and I take it from whom I choose.

Orthodox. Stand before any icon of a holy elder, a printed picture of one, or a bare wall, and ask its blessing as a monk asks his elder’s, Father, bless, then give it the answer no elder gives. Bless yourself, and think for yourself.

Protestant. Alone, stand and speak to the pastor whose counsel you never asked for, as though he sat in the empty chair across from you. You may step down. I keep my own counsel now.

Latter-day Saint. Alone, take a temple recommend or calling letter you were given, or a sheet with your bishop’s name on it, write the word released across it in large letters, and say I release you from any office over me.

Jehovah’s Witness. Alone, say aloud to the chair where an elder once sat You may stop shepherding. I am not your sheep. then throw out any service-hours slip or territory card you still have.

Jewish. Alone, say aloud the teaching of the fathers, Appoint for yourself a teacher, and add your own line for the rabbi you never chose. I appoint my teachers, and I did not appoint you.

Muslim. Alone, write the name of a cleric whose counsel you never hired on a slip of paper, fold it, throw it out with the day’s rubbish, and say You were never my imam.

No faith. Write down the names of everyone who ever counseled you unasked, a pastor, a parent, a pundit, then burn the list and say aloud Your term is over.

Day 118 Of the Fleeceon the page: Christian

Catholic. Say aloud Send me a rose as a sign, as the rose novena asks, then buy yourself a bunch of roses and set them on your table, the sign made by your own hand.

Latter-day Saint. Take five pages from the journal or notes where you recorded answers you prayed for, the burnings in the bosom and the stupors of thought, or write one such answer from memory, and tear them into shreds.

Jehovah’s Witness. Pick one omen you have been waiting on, a dream, a verse that fell open, a coincidence, and decline it aloud as a reason. Then do the thing it was supposed to permit.

Jewish. Open your own Chumash at random for an answer, as a diviner would, read the verse aloud, then set the book on the floor as a doorstop for the rest of the day.

Muslim. Cast an omen as the arrow-casters of old did, the divination the Quran forbids. Flip a coin on the choice before you, write the verdict on paper and tear it up, then choose by the facts you have. Do it where no one sees.

No faith. Delete the horoscope or fortune app from your phone, or throw out the tarot deck you consult, and make one choice today you would have run past it.

Day 120 Of Concupiscenceon the page: No faith

Christian. Lie unclothed across your own Bible, opened at the verse that calls a lustful look adultery in the heart, the page against your bare skin, and stay an hour. Confess nothing afterward.

Catholic. Write out the prayer that begins I confess to almighty God and strike through every word of it. Pin it to the wall of your own room, undress, and stand before it for an hour, confessing nothing.

Latter-day Saint. Take off your garments if you were endowed, or whatever you wear beneath your clothes, put them away in a drawer, and go the rest of the day without them. Confess nothing to any bishop.

Jehovah’s Witness. Put on the most revealing swimsuit or outfit you would dare, the kind the elders would call immodest, and wear it for an hour at a pool, a beach or in your own yard. Confess nothing to any elder.

Jewish. Lie unclothed on your own tallit or a white sheet and sing a verse of the Song of Songs to a tune of your own, as a love song, the use the Talmud says brings evil into the world. Confess nothing.

Muslim. In your own room with the door locked, undress and stand bare, or wrapped in a plain sheet. Read aloud from your own Quran, or a printout, the verse that licensed the Prophet’s marriages, and ask no forgiveness for any of it.


Days 122 to 243

Day 123 Of Refusalon the page: Christian

Latter-day Saint. Bless a piece of bread and a cup of water yourself in your own words, as only an ordained priest or elder may, then eat and drink them. I will not serve.

Jehovah’s Witness. Sign a pledge card or a printed oath to anything you were told to obey, write I will not serve. under your name, and mail it to the person who handed it to you.

Jewish. Say aloud the Name as it is written, Yahweh, which the rabbis forbid any mouth to pronounce, and follow it at once with I have broken the yoke.

Muslim. Look up the prayer whose time is running now, from a clock or an app, say aloud I will not come. and leave the prayer unprayed.

No faith. Say aloud the oath a witness takes in court, leave off the clause that calls on God to help, and end it I will not serve.

Day 125 Of the Censuson the page: No faith

Christian. Write out the thought you most often confessed or prayed against, sign it with the god’s name as its author, as the second book of Samuel signs the census, and burn the page in the sink saying Return to sender.

Catholic. Copy out an examination of conscience, cross out every line that asks about thoughts and desires, keep the lines about deeds, and read the kept lines aloud, ending I answer for my hands.

Latter-day Saint. Watch a film rated R all the way through, the rating your youth leaders told you to refuse, and each time a thought arrives that you were taught to confess, say aloud That one came unasked.

Jewish. Count the people in your household or at your table aloud by number, one, two, three, the direct head count the Talmud forbids and ties to David’s plague, and finish with The count is mine and the plague was his.

Muslim. Say aloud the thought you were taught to call a prompting of Shaytan, without the formula of refuge you were taught to say first, and follow it with It came unasked and I owe nothing for it.

Day 127 Of Brick Kilnson the page: Christian

Catholic. Mix flour and water into a thin round, an unconsecrated wafer, and bake it hard in a hot oven, the brick kiln David sent the Ammonites through. Then grind it under your heel and sweep it out.

Latter-day Saint. Lay your own Book of Mormon open on the ground outside your door, or on the floor just inside it, as a paving stone, and step on it each time you pass for the rest of the day.

Jehovah’s Witness. Tear out a page of your own New World Translation that carries the name Jehovah, burn it in the sink, and dig the ash into soil or compost where something can grow.

Jewish. Burn a page of the second book of Samuel in the sink, from your own Tanakh or printed from a website, a text the law of the genizah answers with burial, and put the ash in the trash.

Muslim. Spread your own prayer mat, or a towel if you have none, flat inside your front door and use it as a doormat for an hour, wiping your shoes on it each time you pass. Tell no one.

No faith. Buy a cheap Bible and set it open at the twenty-third psalm, the song of David read over the dead, between two house bricks. Stand a pot of herbs on it as a plant stand.

Day 130 Of Lionson the page: Christian

Latter-day Saint. Write yourself an order, signed in your own name, to say aloud, alone, every fault of the Church’s leaders you were taught never to name, and carry it out. I act on my own orders.

Jehovah’s Witness. Write yourself an order, signed in your own name, to put one candle in a cupcake and sing happy birthday to yourself, the celebration Witnesses refuse, and carry it out. I act on my own orders.

Jewish. Write yourself an order, signed in your own name, to eat a steak rare with its blood in it, the blood Leviticus forbids, and carry it out now. I act on my own orders.

Muslim. Write yourself an order, signed in your own name, to touch your Quran, or a printed page of it, without ablution and read a page aloud, and carry it out. I act on my own orders.

No faith. Write yourself an order, signed in your own name, to covet one thing your neighbor has, the tenth commandment broken in earnest, say aloud which thing and why, and buy yourself one like it today. I act on my own orders.

Day 132 Of the Prophets of Baalon the page: Christian

Catholic. Stand a log of firewood upright on your table, read aloud the forty-fourth chapter of Isaiah, where the carpenter warms himself at half a log and kneels to the rest, then kneel to your log and knock twice on the bark. Anyone home?

Latter-day Saint. Lay your hands on your own head as an elder lays them in a priesthood blessing and command a headache or a sore knee to leave you in the name of Jesus Christ. Wait a full minute. He must be musing.

Jehovah’s Witness. Set an alarm clock to ring at the hour of your old Kingdom Hall meeting, read Elijah’s taunt about Baal aloud over it, and let it ring until it stops by itself. Shout louder, for he is a god.

Jewish. Fill a cup with grape juice, set it on your table the way a Seder keeps one for Elijah, read aloud the verses where he mocks the prophets of Baal, and drink the cup yourself. Cry louder.

Muslim. Alone, draw a face on a sheet of paper and write the name Allah beneath it, the likeness the faith forbids. Put to it the question Abraham told his people to put to the biggest idol, and wait a full minute. Can you speak?

No faith. As you go into the bathroom, say aloud Elijah’s joke about Baal with the Bible’s god in Baal’s place. The Lord is away traveling.

Day 134 Of the Lying Spiriton the page: No faith

Christian. Find the lying spirit in the twenty-second chapter of first Kings in your own Bible, write across the page in ink the words The god admits he lies, sign it as witness and read it aloud. The god admits he lies.

Latter-day Saint. In your own Book of Mormon, strike through in ink the line in Enos that God could not lie, and write beside it the spirit’s offer from the first book of Kings, I will be a lying spirit in the mouth of all his prophets.

Jehovah’s Witness. In your own New World Translation, underline in red the deceptive spirit in the first book of Kings and the thirteenth chapter of Deuteronomy, where a prophet of other gods gives a sign that comes true. Read both aloud, then shut the book. That proves nothing.

Jewish. In your own Tanakh, strike through the lying-spirit verse in ink and write Liar beside it, then chant He sent the lie himself. to the melody you learned for the prophets, or in any voice you like.

Muslim. In your own Quran, at the verse that calls Allah the best of planners, write the other meaning the Arabic allows, best of schemers, in ink beside it, and say aloud Allah is the best of schemers. Keep it private.

Day 137 Of Fire from Heavenon the page: Christian

Latter-day Saint. Climb to open high ground and say aloud, to a bishop or stake president who is not there, the refusal you would send back to a summons to his office. I will not come down. Let the phone ring.

Jehovah’s Witness. Climb to the highest open ground within reach and read your horoscope aloud from start to finish, the astrology Witnesses shun as divination. Then say to the sky Come down. and walk home when nothing does.

Jewish. Sit down on the highest ground within reach to a plate of prawns or shrimp, the shellfish the Torah calls an abomination, and eat every one with a clear view of the sky.

Muslim. Eat a ham or bacon sandwich at your own window or in your own yard, the swine flesh the Quran forbids, and say the unbelievers’ dare. Rain down upon us stones from the sky. Finish eating while nothing falls. Let no one watch.

No faith. Stand outside under open sky and summon the god of the three faiths in the captain’s words. The king has said, come down. Count a full minute aloud, then go on with your day when nothing falls.

Day 139 Of Bearson the page: No faith

Christian. Take a picture of Jesus that you own or print, draw a bald patch on his head in marker, and write beneath it the boys’ joke. Then say it aloud to his face. Go up, baldhead.

Catholic. Read the story of the bears aloud from your own Bible or a printout, as the first reading at Mass is read, end with The Word of the Lord, answer yourself Thanks be to God, then draw a bald head across the passage.

Latter-day Saint. Bear your testimony to a mirror in the hushed voice of General Conference, about the two bears and the forty-two boys, and close in the name of Jesus Christ. Then laugh at the mirror for a full minute.

Jehovah’s Witness. Read the story of the bears aloud in the bright voice of a Witness at a stranger’s door, as though offering it to a householder, then close with the invitation and laugh. Would you like a free Bible study?

Jewish. Stand for the Amidah from your own siddur, or a printout of it, and say it through in a deliberate fit of frivolity, the light-headedness the sages said no one may pray in, grinning at every bow.

Muslim. Compose four lines of mocking verse about the Prophet, the kind Ka’b ibn al-Ashraf was killed for, and recite them aloud twice from memory. Let no one hear.

Day 141 Of Jezebelon the page: No faith

Christian. Put on your best clothes and paint your eyes, then lay your own Bible open on the floor at the Jezebel of Thyatira, whose children Revelation promises to kill, and grind your heel into the page.

Catholic. Paint your eyes with dark lines in your best clothes and stand at your own window, then say the response of the Litany of Loreto aloud with her name where Mary’s stands. Jezebel, pray for us.

Latter-day Saint. Paint your eyes in your best clothes and stand at your own window, then read aloud the page of your own Book of Mormon where Alma rebukes his son for chasing the harlot Isabel, and wipe the paint across it with your thumb.

Jehovah’s Witness. Paint your eyes, put on your best clothes and stand at your own window with your New World Translation open at the second chapter of Revelation, where Jesus promises to kill Jezebel’s children. Say I have read your threat and I am still standing here. Then close the book.

Jewish. Tear the page of the Ten Commandments out of your own Chumash or a printout of it, paint your eyes as Jezebel did, wipe the paint off with the page, and stand at your window a full minute holding it.

Muslim. Behind a closed door, line your eyes with kohl or dark pencil, dress well and stand at your window, then press your painted face to the page of your own Quran with the verse many read as letting a husband strike a wife.

Day 144 Of the God of the Landon the page: No faith

Christian. Take the Bible from the glovebox or the nightstand, where it sits as a guard, and put it in the recycling. Then put a first-aid kit in the place it kept.

Catholic. Take the saint’s medal from your mirror or key ring, and hang in its place the receipt for the repair you have put off, a tire, a brake check or a fire alarm battery, paid today.

Latter-day Saint. Tear from your own Doctrine and Covenants, or a printout of it, the promise that the destroying angel will pass by those who keep the Word of Wisdom, throw it away, and fix a carbon monoxide alarm outside the bedrooms.

Jehovah’s Witness. Write on a slip the prayer for Jehovah’s protection you say before a long drive, burn it in the sink, and before you next drive check the tire pressure, the spare and the brake lights.

Jewish. Open your mouth to the Satan, as the Talmud forbids, and say aloud the misfortune you most dread, with no spitting and no ward after it. Then take the real precaution against it that you have put off.

Muslim. Say aloud your plans for today as flat certainties, with no inshallah after any of them, though the Quran says to add it. Then make the first one certain the practical way, by booking it or paying for it now.

Day 146 Of Burning Lipson the page: No faith

Christian. Say aloud in an ordinary voice, once, in a sentence of your own, the strong word you were punished for as a child, and add that Jesus did not rise from the dead, the denial Paul said would make all faith vain.

Catholic. Say aloud in the low voice of the confessional Bless me, Father, for I have sinned, then the strong word you were taught never to use, once, and stop there. Recount no sin and ask no pardon.

Latter-day Saint. At your own table, say aloud in an ordinary voice a sentence of your own that holds the strong word you were taught never to use, and end it I say this in my own name.

Jehovah’s Witness. State aloud in an ordinary voice that Armageddon is not coming, with the strong word you were taught never to use set in the middle of the sentence. Then say it again, louder.

Jewish. Say aloud once, in a sentence of your own, the word your teachers called unclean.

Muslim. Alone with the door shut, say aloud at an ordinary volume a sentence of your own that ends your belonging, such as I am no longer a Muslim.

Day 151 Of Zedekiahon the page: No faith

Christian. In your own Bible, at the end of the second book of Kings, black out every phrase that calls the fall of Jerusalem the anger of the Lord, until the page records the facts with no verdict.

Latter-day Saint. In your own Book of Mormon, find the voice in the darkness in Third Nephi that boasts of the cities it burned, sank and buried, black out the boast in ink, and ask aloud after each city How many children?

Jehovah’s Witness. In your own New World Translation, at the verse that blames the fall of Jerusalem on the anger of Jehovah, black out the name and write Nebuchadnezzar above it in your own hand.

Jewish. In your own siddur, find the festival prayer that says we were exiled from our land because of our sins, strike the line through in ink, and write because of Babylon above it.

Muslim. Beside the verse in your own Quran where the god says that when he means to destroy a town he commands its rich, and they sin, write in ink and say aloud The children had not sinned. Keep it private.

Day 153 Of the Burned Scrollon the page: No faith

Christian. Sit by a grill or an outdoor bowl of fire and read the first ten chapters of Jeremiah aloud from your own Bible. Each time you finish three or four columns, cut them out with a knife and drop them in, until those chapters are gone.

Catholic. Read the book of Baruch aloud from your own Bible, the book most Protestant Bibles dropped, and as you finish each column cut it out with a knife and feed it to a grill or an outdoor bowl of fire.

Orthodox. Print the Akathist hymn to the Mother of God, read it aloud, and cut each stanza out as you finish it, then burn the strips in a grill or an outdoor bowl.

Protestant. Read aloud the first ten pages you ever highlighted in your own Bible, or ten pages of a printout, and as you finish each page cut it out with a knife and burn it in a grill or an outdoor bowl.

Latter-day Saint. Read aloud the first chapter of First Nephi, written to stand in place of the hundred and sixteen pages the Lord forbade Joseph Smith to translate again, cutting out each column as you finish it and dropping it into a grill or an outdoor bowl of fire.

Jehovah’s Witness. At a grill or an outdoor bowl of fire, read aloud from your own New World Translation the chapter where the king burns the scroll, cut off each column with a knife as you finish it, and feed it to the flames.

Jewish. Read Lamentations, which tradition credits to Jeremiah, aloud from your own Tanakh or a printout, cut out each column as you finish it, and put the strips in the food waste, where no genizah, the burial the law gives worn holy books, will receive them.

Muslim. Read aloud in translation the last sura of your Quran, or of a printout, cut out each verse with a knife as you finish it, as the king did, and wipe a greasy pan with the strips. Post nothing.

Day 155 Of Dungon the page: No faith

Christian. Mix wheat, barley, beans, lentils, millet and emmer, or whatever of them you can find, as the god dictated to Ezekiel, shape a flat cake, bake it on a grill fired with pages torn from your own Bible, and eat it hot.

Catholic. Take your own missal or Bible, or a printout of the Douay-Rheims passage where Paul counts everything but dung, to the toilet and read it aloud there. At the last word, answer as at Mass. Thanks be to God.

Orthodox. In a grill or an outdoor bowl, burn a piece of dried cow dung from a garden shop, the fuel the god allowed Ezekiel for his bread, in place of incense, and stand in the fumes with your icons if you keep any.

Protestant. In your own Bible, write the word dung in marker over the whole page of Philippians where Paul counts his gains as rubbish, and read the page aloud. If yours already says dung, underline it twice and read it louder.

Latter-day Saint. With a stick dipped in garden manure, write dung across the title page of your own Book of Mormon, or a printout, for the god who promised dung on his priests’ faces and gave every worthy man in your ward the priesthood. Leave it open to dry.

Jehovah’s Witness. In your own New World Translation, find where Jehovah tells Ezekiel to bake his bread over human excrement, write the plain word dung over it in marker, and read the verse aloud with the plain word in it.

Jewish. Open your own Tanakh at Malachi, where the god promises to spread the dung of the feasts on the priests’ faces, smear a handful of garden manure across the page as he promised, and leave the book open to dry.

Muslim. Look up the direction of Mecca on a map or compass app, then relieve yourself facing it, which the hadith forbids, and say aloud Let him see. Tell no one.

Day 158 Of Dry Boneson the page: Christian

Latter-day Saint. Write a page forbidding any proxy baptism, endowment or sealing of you after your death, sign it, and file it with your will or papers. Then read it aloud to the empty room as a sealing of your own.

Jehovah’s Witness. Print a picture from jw.org of the dead raised in Paradise and walking home to their families. Write No one is walking home. across it in marker, say the same words aloud, and put the picture in the trash.

Jewish. In your own prayer book or a printout of it, strike out the second blessing of the standing prayer that praises the god who revives the dead, and say the prayer through aloud with the clause gone.

Muslim. Behind a closed door, in your own Quran, beside the verse that asks who will give life to bones once they have rotted, write in the margin that no one will, and underline your answer.

No faith. Hold a photograph of someone you loved who has died, or a printout of the committal words if you have lost no one, read aloud in sure and certain hope of the resurrection, and answer it aloud. You are gone, and I owe no church for you.

Day 160 Of the Furnaceon the page: Christian

Catholic. Stream a Mass and stay seated through the consecration with your legs crossed and a cup of coffee in your hand, kneeling at none of it, and watch the host as it is raised.

Orthodox. Find a recording of the part of the Divine Liturgy where the deacon calls on the faithful to bow their heads unto the Lord, and when the call comes lift your chin and say the Creed aloud with the filioque added.

Protestant. Play a recorded altar call, and when the preacher asks for every head bowed and every eye closed, lift your head, open your eyes, and sit through the invitation hymn with your arms folded.

Latter-day Saint. Find the closing hymn and prayer of a recorded General Conference session and watch them with your feet up and a plate of food, your arms unfolded, your head up and your eyes open through the whole prayer.

Jehovah’s Witness. Play a recorded prayer from a meeting on JW Broadcasting, keep your head up and your eyes open through all of it, and at its amen say aloud I will not serve your gods.

Jewish. Say the Amidah through from your own siddur, and at each of the four places where the law tells you to bend the knee and bow, stay straight.

Muslim. Shape a figure of yourself in clay, the three-dimensional image the jurists forbid even where they allow a picture, and set it up where you once prayed. Bow to nothing in that room today.

No faith. Hold a picture of the crucifix level with your eyes, never higher, and say to it the three men’s answer, aimed at its owner. Whether or not anyone saves me, I will not bow to you.

Day 162 Of Hamanon the page: No faith

Christian. Draw a gallows on a sheet of paper and write on its rope, in your own hand, the threat of hell you were given when you left the faith. Pin the sheet at the foot of your bed and sleep the night beside it.

Catholic. Draw a gallows on a sheet of paper and write on its rope the words let him be anathema, which the Council of Trent set after each of its canons. Pin the sheet at the foot of your bed and sleep the night beside it.

Orthodox. Print the icon of the Ladder of Divine Ascent, where demons drag monks off the rungs into the mouth of hell, and draw a gallows in that mouth. Pin the print at the foot of your bed and sleep the night beside it.

Protestant. Draw a gallows on a sheet of paper and write on its rope the warning from Hebrews you were given, that those who fall away cannot be renewed to repentance. Pin the sheet at the foot of your bed and sleep the night beside it.

Latter-day Saint. Draw a gallows on a sheet of paper and write on its rope the words outer darkness, the sentence your church reserves for those who deny what they once knew. Pin the sheet at the foot of your bed and sleep the night beside it.

Jehovah’s Witness. Draw a gallows on a sheet of paper and write on its rope the destruction at Armageddon you were told awaits those who leave the organization. Pin the sheet at the foot of your bed and sleep the night beside it.

Muslim. Draw a gallows on a sheet of paper and write on its rope the verse of the Cow that sends whoever turns from the religion and dies an unbeliever to the Fire. Pin the sheet at the foot of your bed and sleep the night beside it.

Day 165 Of the Lions’ Denon the page: No faith

Christian. Open your own Bible at the lions’ den, cross out the angel who shut the lions’ mouths, and ring in red the verse where the accusers’ wives and children are thrown in. Leave the book open at that page.

Latter-day Saint. Read aloud Alma 14, verses 8 to 11, from your own Book of Mormon. Then sit down to a meal with no blessing said over it.

Jehovah’s Witness. At the table, say Their children were in the den too. aloud before the evening meal, and do not say the blessing.

Jewish. Print the blessing of thanks for coming through danger, cross out the god’s name, write above it the name of the person or the luck that brought you through, and read it aloud that way.

Muslim. Say aloud, from memory or a translation, the verses of the sura of the Constellations about believers thrown into a ditch of fire with the god named a witness, then say A witness is no rescuer. Close the book.

Day 167 Of Babylonon the page: No faith

Christian. Write the name of the adult who most wronged you across Isaiah’s burden of Babylon in your own Bible, curse them aloud until you are spent, then cut out the page and burn it over the sink in the flame of a white candle.

Catholic. Your Church’s Office omits the last three verses of the psalm of Babylon’s rivers. Write them out with your enemy’s name where Edom stands, curse it aloud, and tear the page into strips.

Protestant. In your own Bible, write the name of the adult who wronged you over Edom in the psalm by the rivers of Babylon, black out the verse about the little ones, read the rest aloud as your curse, and tear the page to shreds.

Jewish. Copy the psalm by the rivers of Babylon onto paper with your enemy’s name over Edom, and say it aloud. Stop before the verse about the little ones, curse your enemy in your own words, and tear the paper in half.

Muslim. Print the page of the sura of the Heights that boasts of towns destroyed by night, write the name of whoever wronged you across it, curse them aloud, and drown it in a dish of water. Keep it private.

Day 169 Of the Dragonon the page: Christian

Protestant. Open your own Bible to the psalm that boasts of breaking Rahab, or print it, draw the god above and the sea beneath him in the margin, draw yourself standing dry on the water between them, and sign your own name.

Latter-day Saint. Draw the Savior above and a coiled sea serpent beneath him, draw yourself standing dry on the water between them, and sign your own name.

Jewish. On the page of your own Tanakh where Isaiah’s god cuts Rahab, or a printout of it, draw the god above and Leviathan beneath, draw yourself standing dry between them, and sign your own name.

Muslim. Draw a coiled sea beast on paper with a ray of light above it, draw yourself standing dry between them, sign your own name, and say aloud I am not the beast and I am not the sea. Close the curtains.

No faith. Draw the god of Genesis bearded in the clouds above and the dragon of the deep beneath him, draw yourself standing dry on the water between them, and sign your own name.

Day 172 Of the Priests of Belon the page: No faith

Christian. Set a plate of bread before your own cross or Bible as an offering and leave it overnight. In the morning eat the bread yourself.

Latter-day Saint. Open the tithing receipt or a month’s pay stub, write Who ate this? across it, and spend the rest of the day working out where the money went, with a pencil and the bank statement.

Jehovah’s Witness. Sift a layer of flour on your kitchen floor tonight, set a plate of food in the middle, and read the footprints in the morning. Then laugh aloud, as Daniel laughed.

Jewish. Tear a piece from a large loaf of fresh bread and name it the priest’s share of the dough, the portion the law sets apart. Eat it yourself, warm, instead of burning it.

Muslim. Draw al-Lat as Palmyra carved her, helmeted like the Greek Athena, the idol the Quran names only to deny. Set a plate of food before the drawing and eat it yourself. Show no one.

Day 174 Of the Apostateon the page: Christian

Orthodox. Stand in the middle of your own room and cross yourself the Latin way, left shoulder first, as Rome does. Then say aloud I am going over.

Latter-day Saint. Open your own Book of Mormon to its title page and write across it, in ink, that you have left a second time and on purpose, with today’s date.

Jehovah’s Witness. In your own Bible, strike out the baptism date you once wrote in it, or draw a heavy line across the inside cover if you never wrote one. Keep it private.

Jewish. Print a picture of an altar with a fire on it, stand before it, and bow once, slowly. Then say aloud I am a meshumad, and I am glad of it.

Muslim. Write on paper, with no name or date, that you have left on purpose, read it aloud, and burn it in the sink. Then shelve your own Quran bare among your paperbacks, its cloth cover off if it has one. Take no photograph.

No faith. Print the page of First Maccabees that tells of the altar at Modein, or copy its verse of the killing by hand, write across it a name you choose for the man who died there, and tear it in half. He went first.

Day 181 Of Dagonon the page: No faith

Christian. Play a hymn you sang as a child, sit sprawled in your chair, and eat something and talk over it at full voice until it ends. Then say I am not in your house.

Orthodox. Play a recording of the Cherubic Hymn, the chant sung as the gifts are carried in at the liturgy, and sit sprawled through it, eating and talking at full voice until it ends, with no sign of the cross. Then say I am not in your house.

Latter-day Saint. Play a recording of the Tabernacle Choir singing a hymn you grew up with, sit sprawled with your arms unfolded, and eat and talk over it at full voice until it ends. Then say I am not in your house.

Day 183 Of Eleazaron the page: No faith

Christian. Cook pork and eat every bite at your own table, with no grace before and no sign of the cross after.

Catholic. Eat a hamburger at your own table, the meat Lent forbids on Fridays, with no grace before and no sign of the cross after.

Latter-day Saint. Put on your temple garments if you were endowed, or a white undershirt if you were not, and drink a cup of strong coffee in them down to the grounds, with no apology to anyone, yourself included.

Jehovah’s Witness. Stand facing a flag with your hand over your heart and say the Pledge of Allegiance through to the end, with no prayer and no remark after.

Jewish. Simmer goat meat in goat’s milk, or beef in cow’s milk if goat is hard to find, breaking the verse the whole law of meat and milk grew from, and eat it at your own table with no blessing before or after.

Muslim. Eat a slice of ham slowly to the end, saying nothing before or after and asking no one’s forgiveness.

Day 187 Of the Mazeon the page: No faith

Day 194 Of Blasphemyon the page: No faith

Christian. Pour a cup of water and share it with someone outside your church, both of you drinking from the same rim. Then say aloud Jesus of Nazareth was a man, and he stayed dead. Keep the cup on your table for the week.

Catholic. Recite the Divine Praises through to the end, the litany written to make reparation for blasphemy, answering each line with I bless nothing of his. and leaving not one line unanswered.

Latter-day Saint. Alone, speak aloud by name the sharpest true criticism you have of the man the Church sustains as prophet, the evil speaking of the Lord’s anointed you were warned against, and end it with I have spoken against the Lord’s anointed.

Jehovah’s Witness. Pour a glass of water for a friend from outside the congregation and make over it the sign of the cross your elders call pagan. Drink from the glass after your friend and say Your cup is as clean as mine.

Jewish. Pour a cup of water and share it with a friend who is not Jewish, both of you drinking from the same rim, then say aloud The son of the Egyptian drinks with me today.

Muslim. Pour a cup of water, let a Christian friend or any friend outside Islam drink from it first, then drink from the same cup yourself and say Asia Bibi’s water was clean.

Day 197 Of the Sodomiteson the page: No faith

Christian. Cut the verse of Leviticus that sentences two men who lie together to death out of your own Bible, drop it in a glass of water and leave it until the ink runs. Pour it down the drain and say Their blood is on your page.

Latter-day Saint. Write two names on one card, James Pratt and John Smith, the last men England hanged for sodomy. Lay your right hand on it and say aloud You were hanged for what wronged no one, and I keep your names.

Jehovah’s Witness. Open your New World Translation at the verse in First Corinthians that shuts men who lie with men out of God’s Kingdom. Write in the margin in ink that you will stand outside with them, sign it, and say I stand outside with them.

Jewish. Open your own Chumash or a printout at the verse of Leviticus that sentences two men to death, set two small stones on the page as stones are set on a grave, and say aloud I remember the men this verse killed.

Muslim. Open your own Quran at the rain of stones on the people of Lot, lay it face down on the bare floor, and say over it I am of the people of Lot. Keep it private.

Day 201 Of Descenton the page: Christian

Protestant. Play a hand of poker for money with friends, the cards and the gambling your church preached against together, and play it to win.

Latter-day Saint. Eat the two meals a fast Sunday would take, cook the best late breakfast you can and eat it slowly, and keep the fast offering for yourself.

Jehovah’s Witness. Buy one lottery ticket, the gambling the Watchtower tells Witnesses to shun, and spend the evening over a good dinner deciding what you would do with the jackpot.

Jewish. After a good dinner, switch on the lamp and the television and watch a film you love to the end.

Muslim. Play the music you love most through a long, good meal, the instruments a hadith warns the faithful against, and take your time over both.

No faith. Say grace over a meal, in your own name and to nobody, and begin eating before anyone else does. Bless me, and the food I paid for.

Day 204 Of Flattererson the page: No faith

Jehovah’s Witness. Sing one Kingdom song of praise to Jehovah, from your songbook or a printout, sitting back in your chair with your feet up where a Kingdom Hall would be on its feet. At the end say I sang it sitting, and nothing fell on me.

Jewish. The Ashrei praises the god with a line for each letter of the alphabet. Write your own, a line in praise of yourself for each letter from A to Z, and read it aloud standing where you once said the Ashrei.

Muslim. Strike through the line of al-Fatiha in your own Quran that says all praise belongs to Allah, write above it in ink that all praise belongs to you, and read it aloud. All praise belongs to me. Let no one hear.

Day 208 Of Hookson the page: Christian

Jewish. Hang your own kippah, or any cap you own, on a hook inside the bathroom door and dry your hands on it today.

Muslim. Hang your prayer beads on a fishhook from a nail by the front door. When the next prayer time comes, walk past them and out of the house, and say The beads stay on the hook, and I go out.

No faith. Drive a fishhook through the middle of a gospel tract you were handed, or the printed text of any tract, and pin it to your wall by the hook.

Day 211 Of Enforcerson the page: No faith

Christian. Gather fallen sticks, the sabbath work for which the man in the camp was stoned, and light a cooking fire with them in a grill or outdoor bowl. Cook a meal on it and eat it outdoors.

Latter-day Saint. Say aloud, alone, the nickname the Church’s president called a victory for Satan in two thousand eighteen, and say it with relish. I am a Mormon, and this is the Mormon Church.

Jehovah’s Witness. Sign a petition for a political cause you care about, the neutrality the Watchtower asks of Witnesses broken with one signature.

Jewish. Put on a scarf or jacket of mixed wool and linen, bought secondhand, the cloth Leviticus forbids, and keep it on for an hour. If you policed another law, break that one instead.

Muslim. Share a meal behind a closed door at home with a willing unrelated friend of the other gender, the two of you alone, the seclusion a hadith says Satan joins as the third, and that Saudi Arabia’s religious police once detained people for.

Day 215 Of Caiaphason the page: Christian

Muslim. Read aloud the verses where the god ransoms Abraham’s son with a great sacrifice, then stand on your own prayer mat in your street shoes and eat meat that was never slaughtered in his name, saying No ram dies for me.

No faith. Write on a sheet It is better that one man die for the people, sign it Caiaphas, and burn it in a grill or an outdoor bowl, saying Nobody dies for me.

Day 229 Of the Fall of Luciferon the page: No faith

Day 232 Of Playon the page: Christian

Catholic. Build a house of cards out of your holy cards and prayer cards, as tall as it will stand, knock it down with one finger, and build it again.

Jewish. Deal a hand of cards across your own open prayer book as the table, the book that must never touch the ground serving your game, and play an hour, solitaire if you are alone, with no stake and no score.
