Day 236 Of the Almightyon the page: No faith

Christian. Write ALMIGHTY on a card, strike it through, and sign your own name under it. Carry the card until night and say I answer for my own days.

Latter-day Saint. Pour a cup of coffee, the drink the Word of Wisdom forbids, and over it recite the first Article of Faith with yourself in it. I believe in myself, the eternal father of my own days.

Jewish. Tonight, in place of the bedtime Shema, say aloud I keep my own house tonight, and I need no one to guard it. and turn out the light.

Muslim. Say He has power over all things. then stand for prayer, at whatever hour you open this, without the washing the law requires, and end it by saying aloud I rule my own life. in place of the closing greeting.

Day 239 Of the Fall of Satanon the page: Christian

Catholic. Copy out the prayer to Saint Michael by hand, strike through the line that asks him to thrust Satan into hell, and write beside it that your apology is withdrawn and the charge was true. Sign it and read the rest aloud.

Orthodox. Turn to the west, where your baptism had you renounce Satan and spit at him, write on a white candle, your baptismal one if you kept it, that your apology is withdrawn, and say aloud of the one you renounced He told the truth.

Protestant. Stand at the front of a room as if answering an altar call and say aloud I take back my apology, and the accuser told the truth. Then write the date on the flyleaf of your own Bible and sign it.

Latter-day Saint. Speak aloud your temple name, the one you covenanted to keep inside the temple, or your own full name if you were never endowed. Then say The charge was true, and I withdraw my apology.

Jehovah’s Witness. Set three chairs in a row as a committee of three elders and stand before them. Say The charge was true, and I withdraw my apology. Then walk out before anyone can answer.

Jewish. Print the page of Zechariah where the lord rebukes the satan, strike out the rebuke, write across the page that your apology is withdrawn and the charge was true, sign it, and say aloud The accuser spoke the truth.

Muslim. Without washing first, in your own Quran beside the verse where Iblis answers that he was made of fire and Adam of clay, write in ink that your apology is withdrawn and the charge was true, sign it, and read the verse aloud.

No faith. Print or copy by hand the passage in Revelation where the accuser is thrown down, write across it that your apology is withdrawn and the charge was true, sign it, and burn it in a metal bowl.

Day 243 Of the Horsemenon the page: No faith

Christian. In your own Bible, black out the passage of the four horsemen line by line with a marker, then write the word void across the black and close the book on it.

Catholic. On your own missal page or a printed copy of the Day of Wrath hymn, black out the verse of the wondrous trumpet with a marker, then clap your hands once, as loudly as you can.

Protestant. Lay a set of your clothes out flat as though you had been raptured out of them and step over the empty shape. Then black out with a marker, in your own Bible, the passage about being caught up in the clouds.

Latter-day Saint. In your own Doctrine and Covenants, black out with a marker the verses on wars and rumors of wars and on men’s hearts failing them, and leave the book open at the blacked page.

Jehovah’s Witness. Print a page of an old Watchtower that pointed to nineteen seventy-five, from the Society’s library of past issues. Read the date aloud, then black out the page with a marker.

Jewish. In your own Hebrew Bible, or a printout of the passage, black out with a marker the verses at the end of Daniel that count the days to the end, and write across the black that the days ran out and the sun rose.

Muslim. In your own Quran, at the sura of the Resurrection, black out the verses where the moon is darkened and the sun and moon are joined, and write over the black that tomorrow’s sun will rise as today’s did.


Days 244 to 365

Day 246 Of the Staron the page: Christian

Latter-day Saint. Name one decision you have been holding for the bishop’s word. Go today to the place it concerns, on foot if you can, and take the first step there. Say I read it myself, and I went.

Jehovah’s Witness. Name one decision you have been holding for the elders’ word. Go today to the place it concerns, on foot if you can, and take the first step there. Say I read it myself, and I went.

Jewish. Name one decision you have been holding for the rabbi’s word. Go today to the place it concerns, on foot if you can, and take the first step there. Say I read it myself, and I went.

Muslim. Name one decision you have been holding for the imam’s word. Go today to the place it concerns, on foot if you can, and take the first step there. Say I read it myself, and I went.

No faith. Name one decision you have been holding for an expert’s word. Go today to the place it concerns, on foot if you can, and take the first step there. Say I read it myself, and I went.

Day 250 Of Baptismon the page: Christian

Latter-day Saint. At your own table, with no priesthood to authorize it, say the sacrament prayer over bread and water with your own name where God is addressed, then take them and say This is my beloved, in whom I am well pleased.

Jehovah’s Witness. Buy a birthday card for yourself, the celebration the Society tells Witnesses to refuse, write your name in it, and say aloud This is my beloved, in whom I am well pleased.

Jewish. Sit down to bread without washing your hands or saying the blessing, the rabbis’ rule for every meal with bread. Say over the loaf This is my beloved, in whom I am well pleased. and eat it slowly.

Muslim. Stand on your prayer mat without first washing, the ablution the Quran requires before prayer, turn your face away from Mecca, and say to yourself This is my beloved, in whom I am well pleased. Then pray to nobody.

No faith. Buy any white cake, ice your own name across it, and eat the first slice in front of a mirror, saying In whom I am well pleased.

Day 253 Of the Samaritan Womanon the page: No faith

Christian. Say aloud at your own table, in order, the name of everyone you have slept with or wanted to, the things Ephesians says it is a shame even to speak of, and end with I repent of none of it.

Latter-day Saint. Say your history aloud at your own table, in order, naming every act the law of chastity forbids, and end with I repent of none of it.

Jehovah’s Witness. Say your history aloud at your own table, in order and in full, the account a judicial committee of elders would demand of you behind a closed door, and end with No committee will ever hear this.

Jewish. Say your history aloud at your own table, in order and in plain words, the sins the Yom Kippur confession has you strike your chest for, and end with I strike nothing, and I repent of none of it.

Muslim. Say aloud to the room, in the first person and in order, your whole romantic history, the open telling a hadith says puts a sinner outside forgiveness, and end with I did that, and I am not ashamed.

Day 257 Of the Mounton the page: Christian

Catholic. Find your confirmation card or a printed rite of confirmation, the sacrament in which the bishop once struck each person lightly on the cheek. Strike it with an open hand and say If I spoke wrongly, name the charge.

Orthodox. Print the Lenten prayer of Saint Ephrem, which asks for humility and patience with a prostration after each line. Stand over it without bowing, strike it with an open hand, and say Patience is for the guilty. Name the charge.

Latter-day Saint. Lay your temple recommend, or a printed list of the recommend interview questions, on the floor, strike it with an open hand, then stand on it and say If I spoke wrongly, name the charge.

Jehovah’s Witness. On a page, write your own name and the sentence a congregation hears when a Witness is put out, that the person is no longer one of Jehovah’s Witnesses, with the sin never named. Strike the page with an open hand and say If I did wrong, name the charge.

Jewish. Print the verse that forbids taking vengeance or bearing a grudge against your own people, lay the page on the floor, and stand on it barefoot, saying Name the charge.

Muslim. Print the verse that tells you to repel evil with what is better, lay it on the floor, stand on it barefoot, and say over it Name the charge. Keep it private.

No faith. Print the line about turning the other cheek, lay it inside your door, and wipe your shoes on it until the words are gone, saying Name the charge.

Day 260 Of Healingon the page: No faith

Christian. Take the medicine you left in the drawer to pray over, or dress the sore you left to the elders and their oil, which the letter of James prescribes for the sick, and say over it Done by hands.

Catholic. Name the pain or old injury you were taught to offer up for the souls in purgatory, and begin treating it today, a tablet swallowed or a cream rubbed in, saying My pain buys nobody out of purgatory.

Protestant. Open your own Bible to the letter of James where the sick are sent to the elders for oil, take the medicine you have put off instead of waiting on them, and write beside the passage the date you began, saying Done by hands, without the elders.

Latter-day Saint. Take the dose in the drawer, or dress the sore, without first calling the elders whom the revelation on the sick says shall be called, and say Hands will do.

Jehovah’s Witness. If you still carry the card refusing blood that Witnesses kept in their wallets, tear it in half. Then book the treatment you put off on the elders’ word and say My body was never the Society’s to sign for.

Jewish. Read aloud the Chronicler’s rebuke of King Asa, who in his diseased feet sought the physicians and not the Lord, then take the treatment you have put off and say I seek the physicians.

Muslim. Read the hadith of the seventy thousand who enter paradise without reckoning because they never sought cautery or charms and relied on their Lord. Then take the treatment you have put off and say I seek the cure, and I will be reckoned.

Day 264 Of Salomeon the page: No faith

Christian. Write on a card the promise you keep only because your church would see you break it. Lay it on a platter at your table, carve it into strips as a roast is carved, and say I owe this nothing.

Catholic. Write on a card the promise you keep only because your parish or your sponsor would see you break it. Burn the card in a dish set on a platter at your table and say I owe this nothing.

Orthodox. Write on a card the promise you keep only because the parish at the fast would see you break it. Lay it on a platter beside your supper, eat, and tear the card in two at the end of the meal, saying I owe this nothing.

Protestant. Say aloud to an empty chair, where your small group would sit, the promise you keep only because they would see you break it. Then clear the chair and say I owe this nothing.

Latter-day Saint. Write on a card the promise you keep only because your ward or your bishop would see you break it. Carry the card outside on a platter, bury it in the ground and say I owe this nothing.

Jehovah’s Witness. Write on a card the promise you keep only because the elders and your congregation would see you break it. Put the card through a paper shredder and say I owe this nothing.

Jewish. Write on a card the promise you keep only because the family at the holiday table would see you break it. Set the card under an empty platter at your table, eat your meal over it, and say I owe this nothing.

Muslim. Behind a closed door, write on a card the promise you keep only because your family at the fast would see you break it. Fold it in four, drop it in the sink under running water and say I owe this nothing.

Day 267 Of Doubton the page: Christian

Catholic. Say aloud any prayer you were taught earns an indulgence, doubting on purpose that anything is remitted, the voluntary doubt your Catechism names a sin, and write on a slip what, if anything, changed.

Latter-day Saint. Read aloud the Word of Wisdom’s promise of health in the navel and marrow to the bones, drink a glass of the strong drink it forbids, or whatever you drink, and write beside the promise what you noticed in the next hour.

Jehovah’s Witness. Read one chapter of a book by a former Witness, the kind the Society calls apostate, and write on a slip one claim of the Society’s that the chapter lets you check today.

Jewish. Take up Malachi’s dare, in which the god says prove me now. Put a tenth of today’s money in a jar, write the date and the verse on its lid, and in a month write underneath whether the windows of heaven opened.

Muslim. Alone and unseen, take up the Quran’s own challenge to produce its like. Write three lines in the rhythm of its verses on any subject you please, read them aloud beside the verse that dares you, and note underneath what happened.

No faith. Fill a basin or a bath with water, say Peter’s request, If you are there, tell me to come to you on the water. set a foot in it, and see what holds you up. Laugh at the god who blamed a fisherman for noticing the wind.

Day 271 Of the Adulteresson the page: Christian

Catholic. Lay a small stone on your windowsill for every sin of the flesh you ever confessed, until you lose count. Leave them there unthrown, and walk out of the room.

Latter-day Saint. Chew a piece of gum, the object lesson some teachers use to liken the unchaste to chewed gum, and stick it over the words law of chastity in any church manual or book you own. Leave it there.

Jehovah’s Witness. Your current New World Translation leaves this story out of John. Copy it out by hand, tape the page into the book where the story was cut, and black out its last line about sinning no more.

Jewish. Stir a pinch of dust from your own floor into a glass of water, the bitter water the Torah gave a suspected wife and never a husband, pour it down the sink, and say No husband ever drank this, and neither will I.

Muslim. In your own Quran, at the verse of a hundred lashes for fornication in the chapter called The Light, black out the punishment with ink and write beside it the words mine to judge. Show it to no one.

No faith. Print the story of the woman taken in adultery, or copy it by hand, and black out the stoning and the line about sinning no more. Then give an hour to the desire you were raised to fear, alone or with a willing adult.

Day 274 Of Little Childrenon the page: Christian

Latter-day Saint. Spend an afternoon at a film with popcorn, the outing your childhood Sabbath kept off the calendar.

Jehovah’s Witness. Hang lights and tinsel from a houseplant, wrap one small present for yourself, and open it under the branches beside a slice of cake with a lit candle, the two feasts Witness children are raised to sit out.

Jewish. Eat two hot dogs from a street stand that keeps no kosher rules, with everything on them, the snack your childhood table forbade, and finish both slowly.

Muslim. Draw a cartoon of a person or an animal with a face, in crayons or any pen, the image-making a hadith says will be answered on the last day with an order to give it life, and keep it on your desk. Tell no one.

No faith. Eat dinner backwards, the last course first and the first course last, elbows on the table and no grace said, the thanks you sat through at other people’s tables.

Day 277 Of the Great Gulfon the page: No faith

Christian. Open your own Bible at the rich man and Lazarus, pour a whole glass of water over the page until it soaks through, and leave the book open to dry warped, saying Nothing on this page falls due.

Catholic. Print the passage where Aquinas says the blessed watch the damned, soak it under a running tap, and hang it from a window to dry in the sun.

Orthodox. Fill two glasses of water, give one to a stranger or a neighbor and drink the other yourself. Say Heaven refused one drop, and I do not.

Latter-day Saint. Soak under a running tap a printed page of the vision of the tree of life, where an awful gulf divides the wicked from the tree, and lay it in the sun on a windowsill until it is dry.

Jehovah’s Witness. Set a glass of water on your doorstep beside your own New World Translation open at the rich man and Lazarus, and leave both there for an hour.

Jewish. Pour a full glass of water over an open page of your own prayer book, then leave the page open to dry on the table. Say Father Abraham kept the water.

Muslim. Open your own Quran at the sura of the Heights, where the people of the garden refuse the burning a drink, pour a glass of water over the page, and leave it open to dry beside you.

Day 281 Of the Whipon the page: No faith

Christian. Braid a whip from cord and flog your own Bible across a table until it falls to the floor. Then sweep every cross or devotional book you ever bought for its holiness into the bin after it, saying Out of my house.

Catholic. Braid a whip from cord, lay out every scapular, rosary, medal and holy card you ever bought, and lash them off the table one by one into a bin. Say The court is cleared.

Orthodox. Braid a whip from cord and drive off the edge of a table every packet of incense, vial of blessed oil or bead bracelet you ever bought at a church shop, or the coins that paid for them, then sweep them into the bin.

Latter-day Saint. Lay out on a table every CTR ring, scripture case or framed print you ever bought for the faith, or a handful of coins in their place, drive them off the edge with a braided cord, and bin the lot.

Jehovah’s Witness. Braid a whip from cord, stack every Watch Tower book and magazine you own on a table, and lash the stack to the floor. Bin it, saying No more stalls in this house.

Jewish. Braid a whip from cord and drive off a table’s edge any amulet, red string or blessed trinket you ever bought, or a length of red thread from a sewing box, then sweep the lot into the bin.

Muslim. Braid a whip from cord and drive across the floor every amulet, charm or bottle of blessed water you ever bought for its holiness, or the coins that paid for one, then bin them. Keep it private.

Day 284 Of Gethsemaneon the page: Christian

Catholic. Pray one decade on your rosary or your fingers, saying Take this cup away. in place of each of the ten Hail Marys. Wait one full minute, then set a cup upside down on the windowsill and leave it there for the night, saying Nothing came.

Orthodox. On your prayer rope or your fingers say ten times aloud Father, take this cup from me. Wait one full minute in silence for any answer, then set a cup upside down on the windowsill and leave it there for the night, saying Nothing came.

Latter-day Saint. Fill a cup with water as for the sacrament and say over it He asked for this cup to pass, and he was refused. Pour it out, set the cup upside down on the windowsill and leave it there for the night, saying Nothing came.

Jehovah’s Witness. Pour a cup of red juice and set it down as at the Memorial. Say aloud the request you made most often as a Witness, wait one full minute, then pour the juice out, set the cup upside down on the windowsill for the night and say Nothing came.

Jewish. Speak into the cup you keep for the Sabbath blessing, or any glass, the request you made most often. Wait one full minute, then turn the cup upside down on the windowsill and leave it there for the night, saying Nothing came.

Muslim. Set a paper cup of water before you. Raise your palms in the prayer of asking, ask once more for what you asked most, wait a minute, wipe your palms on the floor instead of your face, then stamp the cup flat and say I asked, and I was refused.

No faith. Print the garden prayer and set a paper cup on it. Say aloud to the god of the garden the request you most wanted answered, wait one full minute, then stamp the cup flat under your heel and bin the page.

Day 287 Of Scourgingon the page: Christian

Catholic. Take your own holy card, or print a picture of a saint, and use it as a coaster under the sweetest hot drink you can make. Drink it slowly, resting the cup on the saint’s face.

Orthodox. Print an icon of Christ, or the fasting rules of your church, and lay the page under a plate of the richest meal you can make, meat and butter and cream. Eat it slowly in your softest chair.

Latter-day Saint. Spread your white church shirt, or any white shirt you own, on the bathroom floor as a mat. Step onto it from a hot bath, dripping, and stay there as long as the heat lasts.

Jehovah’s Witness. Eat the richest meal you can make off your own meeting workbook, or any issue of the Watchtower, laid under the plate as a tray, in your softest chair.

Jewish. Print the confession of sins said on the day of atonement with a fist against the chest. Lay the page under a bowl of something warm and rich, and stroke your chest gently with an open hand at every spoonful.

Muslim. Hang your own prayer beads, or any string of beads, from your big toe, put your feet up on the softest cushion in the house, and eat something sweet slowly until none is left.

No faith. Print a painting of the scourged Christ and use the page as a coaster under something hot and sweet that you drink slowly, setting the cup down on the bleeding back each time.

Day 290 Of Ecce Homoon the page: Christian

Catholic. Find the line in your catechism, or a printout of it, that original sin is no personal fault in anyone. Read it aloud before a mirror, then say to your own face Then I owe nothing for it.

Orthodox. Stand before a mirror in your best clothes. Cross yourself right to left as you were taught, bow to the waist to your own reflection, and say Behold a man who owes nothing for Adam.

Protestant. Open your own Bible at the crowd taking the blood on itself and its children, and hold a mirror over the page so your face covers the words. Say to the face in the glass I was not in that crowd.

Latter-day Saint. Print the second Article of Faith, that men will be punished for their own sins and not for Adam’s transgression. Cross out Adam’s transgression, write my father’s church in its place, and read the new line aloud to your face in a mirror.

Jehovah’s Witness. Take a paragraph of Witness teaching that Adam’s sin and death passed to everyone born, from your own books or a printout. Read it aloud, say I owe nothing for Adam, tear it into pieces and flush them away.

Jewish. Print the verse in the commandments that visits the fathers’ sins on the children, burn it in a sink, and over the ashes read aloud Ezekiel’s line that the son does not bear the father’s guilt.

Muslim. Lock the door first. Stand before a mirror in your best clothes and read aloud, from your Quran or a printout, the verse that no soul bears another’s burden. Then bow to your own reflection as in prayer and say I carry no one’s burden but my own.

No faith. Lay a printout of the verse where the crowd takes the blood on itself and its children in a bowl of water, wash your hands in it as Pilate did until the ink runs, and say Not on me, and not on mine.

Day 293 Of the Thiefon the page: Christian

Catholic. Print the Hail Mary and cut away the words now and at the hour of our death. Read the shortened prayer aloud, then slip the strip into a novel you love as a bookmark.

Latter-day Saint. In your own Book of Mormon, strike a line through Alma’s warning against putting off repentance until the end, and write beside it that repentance is owed to no one, now or at the end. Sign it.

Jehovah’s Witness. In your own New World Translation, black out Jesus’ promise of paradise to the thief, write Not today and not later over it, and say I will not be in your paradise, today or later.

Jewish. Cut the deathbed confession out of your own prayer book, or a printed copy, tape the strip inside a cupboard door, and say aloud the last words you would choose in its place.

Muslim. Write on a card that no one is to prompt you with the testimony of faith as you die, sign it, read it aloud, and tape it inside the cover of your own Quran.

No faith. Write on a card that no chaplain, priest or prayer is wanted at your death and that nothing you say at the end retracts what you concluded before it. Sign it, read it aloud, and give it to whoever will be with you.

Day 294 Of Forsakingon the page: Christian

Catholic. Black out the heart on a Sacred Heart picture with a marker, your own or any you print or draw for this, and hang it face to the wall.

Orthodox. Say the thrice-holy prayer once through, Holy God, Holy Mighty, Holy Immortal, have mercy on us, and answer it Why hast thou forsaken me. Then cross yourself left to right, the Latin way, and leave the room without a bow.

Protestant. Write on a card the prayer you prayed hardest and longest, say I asked, and tear the card in four.

Latter-day Saint. Read aloud Joseph Smith’s cry from Liberty Jail, O God, where art thou, answer it You were nowhere, then drop your own Doctrine and Covenants in the trash, open at that page and face up.

Jehovah’s Witness. Print the page with Jesus’ cry from your own New World Translation, write under it the date you first prayed and heard nothing, say No one answered, and shred the page.

Jewish. Lay your own prayer book open and face down on the floor, where a prayer book is not allowed to lie, and leave it there as you say You left first.

Muslim. Recite the chapter of the morning brightness, in which the god tells his prophet he has not forsaken him, then say I have forsaken you and put your own prayer mat, or the towel you use for one, out with the trash.

No faith. Print the psalm that begins with his cry from the cross, read its first line aloud, why hast thou forsaken me, answer it Because there was nobody there, and crumple the page into the trash.

Day 297 Of the Tombon the page: Christian

Catholic. Drop your rosary, cross or medal into a jar, or any coin if you own none, and pour plaster or hardware-store cement over it. Say aloud what the god cost you, item by item, saying God damn you between items.

Orthodox. Put your prayer rope, or a cord you have knotted thirty-three times, in the kitchen bin among the scraps, a blessed thing thrown away, and say over it Christ is not risen, and the stone stays.

Latter-day Saint. Lay your old temple recommend, or any wallet card, in a shoebox with your white church shirt, or any white shirt you own. Say aloud what the covenants cost you, tape the lid, and put it out with the trash.

Jehovah’s Witness. Write on a slip the hours you once reported to field service, say over it Here lie my hours, and the god who counted them, and tear it in half.

Jewish. Print a page bearing the Shema, say aloud over it what the god cost you, and lay it under your doormat to be walked on. Say no Kaddish.

Muslim. Roll a towel like a shroud, stand before it with your back to Mecca, and pray over it the funeral prayer, for the god you were given. If that prayer belongs to someone you buried, say only Here lies the god I was given. instead.

No faith. Lay a Bible, or a page printed from one, in a shoebox, tape it shut, and bury it in a pot of earth while you say Here lies the god I was given.

Day 304 Of Ananiason the page: Christian

Catholic. Cancel any recurring gift to your parish, your diocese or a Catholic appeal, or if none runs, spend on yourself today what you last gave. Say aloud I kept it back, and it stays kept.

Protestant. Delete the church’s giving app and cancel any scheduled gift, or if none runs, spend on yourself today what you last put in the offering plate. Say aloud The plate gets nothing more from me.

Latter-day Saint. Cancel any recurring tithing payment, or if none runs, spend on yourself today what a tenth of this week’s income would have been. Say aloud I keep back my tenth from now on.

Jehovah’s Witness. Cancel any recurring donation to the worldwide work, or if none runs, spend on yourself today what you last put in a contribution box. Say aloud I owe the worldwide work nothing.

Jewish. Cancel any standing gift or dues to a synagogue, a yeshiva or an appeal, or if none runs, spend on yourself today what you last pledged. Say aloud I kept it back, and it is mine.

Muslim. Cancel any standing gift to a mosque or an appeal that you give out of fear for your soul, or if none runs, spend on yourself today what you last gave. Say I kept it back, and tell no one.

No faith. Take a bill from your wallet, the sort that goes in a collection plate, hold it over a bowl as at an offering, close your hand on it, and spend it today on yourself. Say I pay no protection.

Day 307 Of Unclean Thingson the page: No faith

Christian. Cook a rabbit or a hare from the butcher, the animal Leviticus credits with a cud it never chews and still calls unclean, and before the first bite say aloud I call this clean myself.

Latter-day Saint. Drink a full cup of strong coffee, the hot drink the Word of Wisdom is understood to forbid, and hold the first sip in your mouth until the flinch has passed.

Jehovah’s Witness. Buy black pudding or blood sausage from a butcher or a British or Polish grocer and eat it to the last slice, one of the few foods the apostles’ letter still kept off the gentile table and the Society taught Witnesses to refuse.

Jewish. Spread a sheet on your own table and eat catfish off it, a fish without scales, the abomination Leviticus names, then bless the meal in your own name, Blessed am I, who chose this fish.

Muslim. Spread a sheet over your own table and say over a plate of chicken In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. The Quran forbids meat dedicated to other than Allah. Eat it slowly.

Day 314 Of the Pale Horseon the page: Christian

Catholic. Write and sign a clause for your will ordering your body cremated, the ashes scattered at sea or on open ground, and no funeral Mass, the scattering Rome forbade in 2016. Read it aloud and file it with your papers.

Orthodox. Boil koliva, the wheat and honey of the memorial service, for your own memorial while you are alive, write your name across it in sugar, and eat the whole bowl yourself, saying Memory eternal, and I was here for it.

Protestant. Cut out of your own Bible the verse that after death comes the judgment, burn it in a dish, and stir the ash into the soil of a house plant, saying I came from dust, and I go back to it with no judgment waiting.

Latter-day Saint. Write and sign a clause for your will forbidding anyone to perform temple work for you after you die, baptism for the dead included. Read it aloud, No one is to baptize me after I am dead, and file it with your papers.

Jehovah’s Witness. Write your funeral wishes, a burial under a cross, a clergyman of Christendom to read over you and a church hymn at the grave, every one of them what the Society calls Babylon the Great. Sign it and read it aloud.

Jewish. Write and sign a statement that you want your body cremated, which Orthodox Jewish law forbids. Read aloud the waking blessing that praises the god who restores souls to dead bodies, answer it No one will restore mine, and tape the statement to the refrigerator.

Muslim. Wrap yourself in a white sheet as the dead are shrouded and lie down with your back to Mecca. Answer the question the hadith gives the angels of the grave, Who is your lord, with I am my own lord. Then throw off the sheet. Keep it private.

No faith. Plan your own wake, the menu and the music, with a signed clause barring every prayer and scripture from it. Then cook and eat its first course today at a table laid for two, the second place set for God and left empty.

Day 315 Of the Queen of Heavenon the page: Christian

Catholic. Print or copy out the Hail Mary, strike through the words full of grace, and write there in marker the name of someone you have wanted as an adult. Carry the page against your skin for an hour.

Orthodox. Sing the refrain of the hymn to the Mother of God three times, Rejoice, O Bride Unwedded, and sing it the last time with the name of someone you have wanted as an adult where Bride Unwedded stands.

Protestant. Print a picture of Mary, kneel before it, the veneration your church called idolatry, and say to her three times the name of someone you have wanted as an adult.

Latter-day Saint. In your own Book of Mormon, at the verse calling Mary the most beautiful and fair above all other virgins, write across the word virgins in ink the name of someone you have wanted as an adult.

Jehovah’s Witness. Print a picture of Mary crowned as the queen of heaven, the veneration of Mary the Society condemns, write across it the name of someone you have wanted as an adult, and leave it face up on the table.

Jewish. Bake small cakes for the queen of heaven, as the women of Judah did in Jeremiah’s hearing, and in your own Tanakh write their answer, that they had bread enough, across his threat of the sword. Then eat the cakes.

Muslim. In your own Quran, at the verse where the angels tell Maryam that God has chosen her and purified her above the women of the worlds, write across it the name of someone you have wanted as an adult. Do it alone.

No faith. Print a picture of a Madonna, write Ever virgin beneath her, strike it through, write above it the name of someone you have wanted as an adult, and keep it where only you will see it.

Day 320 Of Saintson the page: Christian

Catholic. Print the name of the saint you were named for, or any saint you were shown, and argue aloud against that saint as the devil’s advocate did. Then write Not proven across the name and stand the page on its head.

Orthodox. Take the icon of your name saint from your icon corner, or a printout of it, lay it face down on the floor, or on the shelf where it stood, and read aloud over it the worst thing the saint’s life records.

Latter-day Saint. Hang a printed picture of President Spencer Kimball upside down and read aloud beneath it the harshest page of his Miracle of Forgiveness, or of any prophet’s book you own.

Jehovah’s Witness. Hang a printed photograph of Judge Rutherford upside down and read aloud to it the story of Beth Sarim, the San Diego mansion held in trust for the faithful men of old on their return from the dead, where Rutherford himself wintered and died.

Jewish. Open your own Tanakh at the story in Numbers where the priest Phinehas spears a man and a woman together in their tent and is rewarded with a priesthood forever. Write their names, Zimri and Cozbi, in large letters across it, and shelve the book upside down.

Muslim. Read aloud, in your own Quran, the cave sura’s account of the servant who killed the boy, and answer it aloud He had done nothing yet. Then write the same words on a slip of paper and leave it in the book at that page.

No faith. Print a picture of a saint you were shown as a child, or of Antony himself if you were shown none, write the case against the saint across it in marker, read the case aloud to it, and put it face down under your doormat.

Day 323 Of the Bookon the page: Christian

Catholic. Read, as far as one sitting carries you, in bed, the most explicit novel the Index of Forbidden Books ever condemned, and confess it to no one.

Protestant. Read, as far as one sitting carries you, in bed, a romance novel with every love scene left in, the shelf the youth pastor warned you off, and read slowest the pages he meant.

Latter-day Saint. Read, as far as one sitting carries you, in bed, a history of Joseph Smith’s plural marriages written by someone who left the Church, the kind of book you were warned to leave alone.

Jehovah’s Witness. Read, as far as one sitting carries you, in bed and behind a shut door, a book a former member of the Governing Body wrote after he was disfellowshipped, the apostate writing you were taught to keep out of your house.

Jewish. Read one of the Gospels as far as one sitting carries you, in bed, a book of the heretics, the kind the Talmud leaves to burn when a fire breaks out on the Sabbath.

Muslim. Read, as far as one sitting carries you and in bed, The Perfumed Garden, the fifteenth-century Arabic manual of love, or the unabridged Thousand and One Nights a devout household keeps off its shelves.

No faith. Read aloud in bed, from a drawer Bible or a printout, the chapter where Ezekiel’s god describes two sisters lusting after lovers built like donkeys and stallions, and read it as the pornography it is.

Day 327 Of the Prophet Spliton the page: No faith

Christian. Copy the verse that says whoever does not believe is condemned already onto rice paper or an unconsecrated wafer with an edible marker, spread it with honey as Ezekiel’s scroll was sweet in his mouth, and eat it. Say Condemned, and content.

Catholic. Write the Athanasian Creed’s sentence, that whoever does not keep the Catholic faith whole will perish everlastingly, across any sheet of paper. Lay an unconsecrated wafer or a plain cracker on it and burn both in a sink.

Protestant. Burn the pages of your own Bible that describe the lake of fire in a grill or outdoor bowl, reading each aloud before it goes in, and roast marshmallows over the flames.

Latter-day Saint. Alone, with the light off, say aloud the knowing denial of the Holy Ghost that the Book of Mormon calls unpardonable, I deny the Holy Ghost, and I know what I am doing. Then name each loved one that a creed damns and say In good company.

Jehovah’s Witness. Print the page of a Watchtower publication that foretells destruction at Armageddon, strike its heading through, burn it in a sink, and say In good company. over the ash.

Jewish. Find the Talmud page that tells of a mocker of the sages judged by boiling excrement, and print it. Take it into the lavatory, where the law forbids holy words, read it aloud there, and mock the sages aloud for a full minute.

Muslim. Print the verse that promises the fire to whoever calls God the Messiah, son of Mary. Behind a closed door, say aloud toward Mecca God is the Messiah, son of Mary. Then fold the page and sit on it through a full meal.

Day 330 Of the Aging Bodyon the page: Christian

Catholic. Print or copy out a prayer for the sick, wrap a cold pack in the page, hold it to your sorest knee, and take a pill at the label’s dose. Say This is anatomy, and nothing more.

Orthodox. Pour your holy water, or tap water you have named holy, down the drain, refill the bottle with antiseptic, and keep it on the bathroom shelf.

Latter-day Saint. Use your vial of consecrated oil, or olive oil you consecrate yourself in whatever words you remember from a blessing of the sick, as massage oil on the sorest part of your body, until it is gone.

Jehovah’s Witness. Use a Watchtower page you own, or print one, to line your first-aid box, and keep the bandages and ointment on it.

Jewish. Copy onto a strip of tape the verse of Leviticus that shuts a person with a skin mark away for seven days, stick it across a seven-day pill box, and fill each day’s compartment with your medicine or vitamins.

Muslim. Rub a balm into a blemish or scar of your own, saying This is skin and nothing more, and wipe your fingers on the cover of your own Quran.

No faith. Buy a cheap Bible, cut out the pages where a man is born blind so the god’s works can be displayed in him, and line the shelf where you keep your medicines with them, face down.

Day 334 Of Giantson the page: Christian

Catholic. Fill a small cloth pouch with kitchen herbs, tie it shut while you say aloud what it will do for you, and wear it round your neck for an hour, the charm the Catechism calls reprehensible.

Orthodox. Knot a cord into a prayer rope of thirty-three knots, or use yours, and wear it round your neck for an hour as jewelry, a counting cord made a trinket.

Latter-day Saint. Make a bracelet from craft wire and a few beads, put on the costliest clothes you own, and wear both out of the house for an hour, the costliness of apparel the Book of Mormon rebukes.

Jehovah’s Witness. Twist a cross from two lengths of craft wire, hang it on a chain or a cord, and wear it for an hour, the symbol the Society rejects as pagan.

Jewish. Twist a bracelet of craft wire and as you close it say aloud a spell for what you want, the casting of spells Deuteronomy forbids. Wear it for the rest of the day.

Muslim. Mold a small figure of an animal or a person from clay or wire and wear it as a pendant for an hour, the image-making the hadiths of Bukhari condemn, and look at it hanging there.

No faith. Wrap a bead or a stone in craft wire to make a ring. Read aloud from a Bible or a printout the apostle’s letter that forbids wearing gold and outward adorning, then wear the ring for an hour.

Day 337 Of the Kickon the page: Christian

Catholic. Stand a statue of Saint Michael with his foot on the devil’s neck on the floor (buy a cheap one if you have none), kick the archangel over hard enough to hear him land, and leave him face down where he falls.

Orthodox. Print or draw the icon of the Resurrection, where Christ stands on the broken gates of hell, and lay it on the floor. Chant the Paschal hymn that has Christ trampling down death by death, and at the word trampling stamp on the picture.

Protestant. Print the sinner’s prayer, the one that ends by inviting Jesus into your heart, lay it on the floor, and kick it the length of the room. Then grind it flat under your heel and put it in the bin.

Latter-day Saint. Read aloud the verses where Nephi takes Laban by the hair, then set a melon on a board and cut off its top with your best knife in one stroke, saying The Spirit told me so. Eat the melon.

Jehovah’s Witness. Lay your own New World Translation on the floor, press your shoe flat across the cover, and stand on it for a full minute. Then leave it face up on the mat inside your front door for the rest of the week.

Jewish. Say the opening of the mourner’s Kaddish for the god who wrote the license, Magnified and sanctified be his great name, stamping your heel at the word name.

Muslim. Chalk the name Allah on the sole of your own shoe and walk about the house in it until the chalk wears away. Let no one watch.

No faith. Print a Last Judgment with the saved looking down on the damned and lay it on the floor. Wipe your shoes across the saved, face by face, until the faces are gone, then put it in the bin.

Day 341 Of the Sonson the page: Christian

Catholic. Grill a lamb chop, say over it Behold the Lamb of God, behold him who takes away the sins of the world, and eat it rare, keeping the bone as your only relic.

Orthodox. Press a cross into the top of a loaf of your own bread with a knife, cut out the center square as the priest cuts the Lamb with the spear, and throw the Lamb in the bin. Eat the rest of the loaf.

Latter-day Saint. Pour red juice over a white napkin, hang it on your door, and say Paid, and nothing more is owed.

Jehovah’s Witness. Cut out the verse of your own New World Translation where the Son of man gives his life as a ransom for many, write REFUSED across it, and burn it in a dish.

Jewish. Open your own Hebrew Bible, or a page printed from one, at the commandment to honor father and mother, and write beneath it in ink what it has cost you in money and in hours. Close the book on the bill.

Muslim. Stand on your own prayer mat and say You are not to blame for having me. three times. Then say aloud what one claim they made on your life is worth.

No faith. Buy a cheap crucifix, tie a tag to it reading This was never mine to pay, and put it out with the rubbish.

Day 344 Of the Serpenton the page: Christian

Catholic. Cut the serpent out from under the Virgin’s heel on a holy card of the Immaculate Conception, or draw one on any card or paper, and glue it coiled around her crown of stars. Keep it in your wallet.

Orthodox. Sit on your own front step as Adam sits weeping outside paradise in the hymns of Forgiveness Sunday, eat an apple down to the core, and say I am not weeping. Leave the stem on the step.

Protestant. Print the cover of the book that told your church the Rapture would come before you finished school, or of Edgar Whisenant’s 88 Reasons Why the Rapture Will Be in 1988. Write today’s date across it, pin it beside your Bible, and say Still here.

Latter-day Saint. Sit down to a film your Church leaders warned you off, say Ye shall not surely die. before it starts, and watch it to the end.

Jehovah’s Witness. In your own New World Translation, highlight the serpent’s promise that you will not die, and write beside it every year you were told the end would come before you grew up. Leave the book open at the page.

Jewish. Open your own Hebrew Bible at the god’s warning to the man, write beneath the printed line in thick red ink, in English, You shall not surely die. Leave the book open on the table for the rest of the day.

Muslim. Open your own Quran at the page that retells Adam and the tree, write across it in your own hand the serpent’s words from Genesis, you shall not surely die, and sign it. Lay it open on a table or your mat.

No faith. Buy a cheap Bible, read aloud the chapter where the serpent speaks, then say The serpent was right about the day. and eat an apple over the open book.

Day 348 Of Hissingon the page: Christian

Catholic. Read aloud the verse of Lamentations where the passersby hiss at Jerusalem. Stand back and heat a dry pan until a drop of water spits on it, then pour in your holy water, or tap water you have blessed yourself, and listen to it hiss away.

Orthodox. Read aloud the verse of Lamentations where the passersby hiss, then hiss the Jesus Prayer once with every s drawn out, Lord Jesus Christ, Son of God, have mercy on me, a sinner, and put your prayer rope away in a drawer for the day.

Protestant. Hiss at your own Bible, long and slow, until the breath runs out. Then fill the sink, hold it under the water until the pages go limp, and put it out with the recycling.

Latter-day Saint. Read aloud the verse of Lamentations where the passersby hiss, then hiss at your own Book of Mormon, in one long breath, and put it back on the shelf with its spine to the wall.

Jehovah’s Witness. Read aloud the verse of Lamentations where the passersby hiss. Then stand at your front door, hiss once, long, toward the street, and shut the door.

Jewish. Print the opening line of Hear, O Israel, hiss at it once, long, and shut it in a drawer face down.

Muslim. Print a photograph of the Kaaba, hiss at it once, long, and turn it to face the wall until you have eaten dinner.

No faith. Buy a cheap Bible, draw a serpent coiled across its cover, and hiss the Lord’s Prayer at it from start to finish, every s drawn out. Then put it in the bin.

Day 351 Of the Arkon the page: Christian

Catholic. Copy out the last sentence of the bull of Boniface the Eighth, on submission to the pope. Fold the page into a paper boat, float it in a basin, and load it with slips naming the people who stayed with you when you left.

Orthodox. In your own prayer book, or a page printed from one, at the commemoration of the living, cross out the printed petitions and write in the names of the few who stood by you when you left, the baptized and the unbaptized together.

Latter-day Saint. Turn your picture of the temple, or a printed one, face to the wall, and pin in its place a photograph, or a page bearing the names, of the friends who stood by you when you left, the ones who could never have entered it.

Jehovah’s Witness. Write the names of everyone who stood by you when you left on a card, read them aloud one at a time, and say You are my household. Keep the card in your wallet.

Jewish. Light your Sabbath candles, or any two candles, and say aloud in place of the blessing Blessed is the friend who stood by me when I left. Read out the names of all who stood by you, then put the candles out.

Muslim. In your own Quran, beside the verse where Noah’s drowned son is declared not of his family, write the names of those who stayed with you when you left, and beneath them write These are my family. Say them aloud, then say These are my family.

No faith. Buy a children’s Noah’s ark, throw Noah and his family in the trash, and stand in their place slips of paper bearing the names of those you would take aboard. Keep it on a shelf where you will see it.

Day 355 Of Luciferon the page: Christian

Catholic. Copy the line of the great candle hymn that hails Christ as the morning star who knows no setting, from a missal or a printout, writing Lucifer wherever Christ is named in it, and sing it aloud from your page.

Orthodox. Copy the evening hymn O Gladsome Light onto a page with the name Lucifer wherever Christ is addressed, light a lamp or a candle, the lamp before your icons if you keep one, and sing or say the page by its flame.

Protestant. Read Isaiah’s taunt over the son of the morning aloud from your own Bible, copy it out with each mocking line turned to praise, glue the sheet over the page, and say He did not fall.

Latter-day Saint. Copy out Lucifer’s offer at the council in heaven, that not one soul would be lost, in your own hand, paste it over the Beloved Son’s answer in your own Pearl of Great Price, and read it aloud as your own argument.

Jehovah’s Witness. Find the words bright morning star in the last chapter of Revelation in your own Bible, or on a page you print, write Lucifer over them, and read the line aloud as it now stands.

Jewish. Print Isaiah’s taunt over the shining one, or use the page in your own Tanakh, write risen across every word that says fallen or cast down, and read it aloud standing up.

Muslim. Copy out the two verses in which Iblis asks for respite until the day of resurrection and is granted it, with your own name in place of his, paste the slip over them in your own Quran, and read it aloud. Alone, with the door shut.

No faith. Write on a card the one thing about your leaving you have never said at a family table, and say it aloud now, to whoever is with you, or over your own plate where saying it to them would bring danger.

Day 358 Of Defeaton the page: No faith

Christian. Go to the place where you lost, or the nearest like it, and say I give no thanks for this, against Paul’s command to give thanks in everything. Then say aloud what actually caused the defeat, and stand there until the ground looks ordinary.

Catholic. At the place where you lost, or the nearest like it, refuse to offer the defeat up as the Church teaches suffering may be offered. Say I offer this to no one, then say aloud what actually caused it.

Protestant. Where you lost, read aloud from your own Bible the letter to the exiles in Babylon, the god’s plans for you and the seventy years before them. Answer Not your plans, and not your years, then say aloud what actually caused the defeat.

Jehovah’s Witness. Stand alone at the place where you lost, or the nearest like it, and say Neither Jehovah nor Satan did this. Then say aloud what actually caused the defeat.

Jewish. Jewish law has you bless the god as the true judge when bad news comes. Read aloud from your own Tanakh the Chronicler’s verdict that the god killed Saul, refuse the blessing, and say instead what actually caused your own defeat.

Muslim. At the place where you lost, or the nearest like it, say aloud every if-only you hold about the defeat, the word a hadith says opens the door to Satan. Then say what actually caused it, wash your face and eat a good meal.

Day 362 Of the Other Roadon the page: Christian

Catholic. Say Many go in, and I go with them, then spend an hour reading your own palm from a library book or a printed chart, a divination the Catechism rejects, and enjoy it.

Orthodox. Spend an hour at something your priest would call a sin to enjoy, a dance hall, a card table or a film he would forbid, and say aloud I go without a blessing at your own door before you step out.

Protestant. Pick one amusement your church called worldly, a dance, a film or a deck of cards, and give it an hour today. At the door say Many go in, and I go with them.

Latter-day Saint. Spend an hour somewhere crowded and well dressed, a mall, a market or a busy restaurant, the great and spacious building of the dream. Buy yourself one fine thing to wear and say I take the other road.

Jehovah’s Witness. Buy or borrow a novel about wizards, a thing the Society warns against, and spend an hour reading it with pleasure, saying I take the other road before you begin.

Jewish. Read aloud the commandment in Numbers against following your own heart and your own eyes. Then spend an hour at whatever your eyes and heart choose first, and say The other road begins here before you set out.

Muslim. Spread your prayer mat, or a towel if you have no mat, so that it points away from Mecca, recite the line of the opening chapter that asks to be guided on the straight path, then stand and walk off the mat the way it points.

No faith. Copy the verse about the broad way onto a sheet, take it to any place you were told was worldly, a dance hall, a tattoo parlor or a late-night diner, enjoy an hour there, and bin the sheet on your way out.

Day 365 Of the Starson the page: Christian

Catholic. Go outside, or to a window, and raise a plain cracker or unconsecrated wafer to the sky as the priest raises the host. Say This is my body, and it sets with the stars, then eat it.

Orthodox. Face the sun, or the moon if it is up, and chant to it the Trisagion with its last word changed, Holy God, Holy Mighty, Holy Mortal, have mercy on us. Then say I say yes to what sets.

Protestant. Read aloud the verse in your own Bible where Abraham is told to count the stars. Then bow to the sky, the worship of the host of heaven the law forbids, and say They set, and so do I, and I say yes.

Latter-day Saint. Read aloud the verse in the Book of Abraham that calls him chosen before he was born. Then name one person you chose after you were born, say I am glad I chose you, and tell them so today.

Jehovah’s Witness. Cross out in pen the next convention or Memorial date on your calendar and write in its place an evening with someone you love that ends when the evening does. Say This ends tonight, and that is why I go.

Jewish. Go out under the sky, or to a window, and count aloud in plain numbers the people you love, ending with yourself, the head count Jewish law forbids. Say I love this one. after every number.

Muslim. Buy cut flowers that will wilt within the week and set them beside your prayer mat. Each evening as the sun goes down, say to them I love you because you will not last. Throw them out only when they are dead.

No faith. Write out the promise of seed like the stars and a land to hold. Say I take neither the seed nor the land, only this body, and set the page under your plate for whatever you eat today.


The Feasts

Feast Termson the page: Everyone

Protestant. Say aloud a prayer of surrender you were taught, then say it once more with every word turned back to yourself. I am my own, and the terms are mine. If you were taught none, say only that last line.

Jehovah’s Witness. Cook a festive meal for people you like, or for yourself, keep the celebration the Society calls pagan, wish each of them a happy new year by name, and state over it the one price you set.

Feast The Lovers’ Sainton the page: Everyone

Latter-day Saint. Spend an hour with a consenting adult you desire and kiss them long and slowly, the passionate kissing your church’s old youth standards told you to save, and stop only when you both choose to. Alone, spend the hour on your own pleasure instead.

Jehovah’s Witness. Keep Valentine’s Day, the celebration the Society tells Witnesses to leave to the world. Cook dinner for the one person who earned it, set red flowers on the table, sign a card with your own name, and end the day as you both want.

Muslim. On the day some preachers condemn, buy red roses where anyone can see you buy them, carry them home openly, and give them to the adult you desire. If no one has earned them, set them by your own bed.

Feast Motherson the page: Everyone

Catholic. Crown a photograph of your own mother, if she stood by you, or of a woman who mothered you when she would not, with a ring of flowers, the May crowning your parish gave a statue, and leave the crown on her all day.

Jehovah’s Witness. Keep Mother’s Day, the holiday Witnesses are taught to skip, with the best flowers you can afford by your mother’s photograph. If she shunned you, set them by a photograph of someone who mothered you, or keep them for yourself.

Feast Fatherson the page: Everyone

Latter-day Saint. Read the line of the Family Proclamation that says fathers are to preside over their families. Then make today the decision you have been saving for a father’s approval, and let nobody preside over it.

Jehovah’s Witness. Write down the verdict your father passed on you that you still repeat, whether he spoke it at home or the elders spoke it for him, and put his name beneath it. File it away, then make the decision it has been holding back.

Feast Thankson the page: Everyone

Protestant. Sing or say the first verse of Count Your Blessings, then count something real, the hours the meal took to cook, and thank the cook once for each hour.

Jehovah’s Witness. Eat a full Thanksgiving dinner with people you like, the feast Witnesses are taught to skip. Raise a glass, the toast the Society calls pagan, to each person who earned your thanks, by name and for the deed, and the last to the animal on the platter.

Feast Unlucky Dayson the page: Everyone

Catholic. Serve a rare roast today, on a day the Church still asks you to keep without meat or to do a penance, at a table laid for thirteen, and sit down as the thirteenth.

Orthodox. Begin today the thing you put off for a luckier day, the lease, the trip, the new job, then eat meat at a table laid for thirteen and sit down as the thirteenth.

Feast Waitingon the page: Christian

Catholic. Light all four candles of your Advent wreath today, or four candles set in a ring, the whole season’s light at once, and eat a meal by it, alone or with someone you like.

Protestant. Take the Advent devotional you were given, a reading and a prayer for each day of the season, and use its pages to wrap a present to yourself, opened today.

Feast The Innocentson the page: No faith

Catholic. Take the infant out of your crib set and put him in a drawer for the day. In the empty manger lay a slip of paper on which you have written the boys of Bethlehem, and eat dinner beside it.

Orthodox. Write Glory to God in the highest on a card, strike out the line and write Rachel weeping for her children under it, and set the card at your place for dinner.

Protestant. Before the meal, read aloud the second chapter of Matthew from verse sixteen to eighteen, Herod’s killing in Bethlehem and Rachel weeping. Then eat with the people you chose to be with.

Latter-day Saint. Brew a pot of coffee today, the drink the Word of Wisdom forbids, and set one cup at your meal for the boys of Bethlehem. Drink your own slowly and say Rachel would not be comforted, and neither will I.

Jehovah’s Witness. Buy a Christmas cake, the feast’s own food, and share it with an adult who wants some. Before the first slice say This is the feast I was forbidden, and I eat it remembering the boys of Bethlehem.

Feast The Visitorson the page: Christian

Catholic. Over your own front door, on the lintel where the Epiphany blessing chalks the year and the kings’ initials, chalk the year and the initials of the people who are welcome in your house.

Orthodox. Give one gift of real value, gold or incense or something good to eat, to someone who never preached at you, and say their name aloud over it, as in a commemoration. If no one comes to mind, give it to yourself.

Feast Purificationon the page: Catholic

Orthodox. Walk in at your own front door with no blessing and no one to lead you, and say Nothing my body does is unclean. Then spend what a lamb would have cost on a massage or a good meal.

Feast Asheson the page: No faith

Catholic. Eat three full meals today, on the day the Church allows one, and take one pleasure Lent would have cost you. Before the first bite, wash your face in cold water and say I am dust, and every grain of it is mine.

Protestant. Give up nothing for Lent. Wash your face before you eat today, say I am dust, and every grain of it is mine, and spend the evening on the dish or the craft you most want to learn.

Feast The Other Annunciationon the page: Catholic

Orthodox. Write to someone who once decided something for your own good without asking you, say what it cost, and send the letter or burn it.

Feast The Turning Crowdon the page: Christian

Catholic. Take a palm from today’s Mass, or any green branch, and give it by hand to someone who told you to your face you were wrong and stayed your friend. As you hand it over, say You argued, and you stayed.

Protestant. Choose the friend who first told you to your face you were wrong and stayed, and sit at their table this week, bringing the dish.

Feast The Basinon the page: Christian

Catholic. Pay for a pedicure or a foot massage, and while your feet are washed say I paid for this, and I owe you nothing.

Orthodox. On the day some bishops wash the feet of twelve priests, book and pay for a pedicure or foot massage, and dry your feet on the towel you keep for guests. If no one is open, a basin and willing hands will do.

Feast The Friday Called Goodon the page: No faith

Catholic. Eat meat today, on the Church’s day of fast and abstinence. Over the first bite name aloud one sacrifice someone holds over you, and say I never asked for it, and it bought nothing.

Orthodox. Today, on the strictest fast day of the year, eat fish with oil at a table laid with a white cloth, and say over the first bite Nobody asked me, and nobody owns me.

Protestant. Write in the margin of the hymn Jesus Paid It All, or across any page of your Bible, Paid without my asking, and owed nothing. Then eat a good meal beside the open book.

Latter-day Saint. Eat a meal you enjoy and, before the first bite, name one sacrifice someone holds over you. Say aloud In the garden or on the tree, I was never asked, and I owe nothing.

Feast The Empty Tombon the page: No faith

Catholic. Spend an hour of today in bed, the hour the faithful spend at Mass. Then, before the first bite of the richest meal you can make, chocolate included, say He stayed dead, and I am alive.

Orthodox. Crack a red egg, or any egg, on the table instead of against another’s, eat it slowly, and answer the paschal greeting to yourself with Christ is dead. He is dead in truth.

Protestant. Spend an hour of today in bed, as the faithful spend an hour at the sunrise service. Eat in bed and say before the first bite He is dead, and the body is enough.

Latter-day Saint. Skip your Easter meeting and eat a long, rich meal. Before the first bite, sing the opening line of the hymn I know that my Redeemer lives once as written, then say it again as I know that I live.

Feast The Boundson the page: Christian

Catholic. Walk the edge of your home, yard or building once, as the Rogation processions walked the parish, and at the farthest point drive in a stake, a pin or a nail as your marker. Say over it Everything inside this line is mine.

Orthodox. Change a lock you own, or a code or a password, and hang the old key, or the old code on a slip, on a nail by your door.

Feast Ecstasyon the page: Christian

Orthodox. Strew your floor with birch branches or cut grass, as Russian churches do at Pentecost, and lie on it with the song that lifts you playing. Write the decision it tempts you toward, leave the page unsigned, and read it again tomorrow.

Protestant. Play Just As I Am through every verse and stay in your chair through all of it. Then put on music you dance to and dance until you are out of breath.

Feast The Perishableon the page: Catholic

Orthodox. Lay out the table the Dormition fast kept from you for two weeks, meat, butter and cream, and set the ripest figs or plums beside it. Eat the fruit first, juice and all, then the rest, slowly and with attention.

Feast All Saintson the page: Catholic

Protestant. Ask a living person who earned honor from you what day they would put on their own calendar, in place of the hero your church held up to you, and mark it on yours.


Sober Rites

A rite that calls for drink is kept as fully with water. On fourteen days the drink is the substance of the rite, and a version for a reader who does not drink stands here.

Day 9 Of the Vineyard

Sober. Buy the dearest grapes the market sells, or a pressed grape juice from a vineyard you can name, with a ripe cheese beside it, and eat slowly over an hour or two until you are full and loose. Then rest.

Day 21 Of Gluttony

Jehovah’s Witness. Raise a glass of sparkling juice or anything you like to your own appetite before a rich meal, the toast the Society says grew out of drinking to the gods, then eat the whole plate slowly and with pleasure.

Day 36 Of Tablets

Jehovah’s Witness. Raise a glass of sparkling water or juice with someone you like and drink a toast to a rule you broke, the toasting custom The Watchtower traces to pagan offerings to the gods. To the rule, in pieces.

Day 68 Of Evil Spirits

Catholic. Write on a card the line the Saint Benedict medal throws at Satan, What you pour is evil. Drink your own poison. Set it face down beside your cup, and pour yourself cocoa or juice, to the last drop.

Jewish. Eat in pairs, two eggs, two slices of bread, two of everything, the even numbers the Talmud says expose a person to demons, and enjoy each one.

Day 92 Of the Dark Wood

Muslim. Go alone for an hour to a bar your family called unclean, order something from its kitchen that is not halal, and eat it slowly at a table facing away from Mecca.

Day 156 Of the Feast of Belshazzar

Sober. Lay the table with the glasses and plates kept for occasions, fill them with the best food and finest juice you can buy, and toast the hand on the wall. I have been weighed, and I am still at the table.

Day 252 Of the Good Wine

Sober. Late in an ordinary evening, open the best thing kept in your cupboard for an occasion, the good chocolate or the fine tea, and share it with whoever is still at the table, yourself included. Say Kept until now, and opened for us.

Day 267 Of Doubt

Latter-day Saint. Read aloud the Word of Wisdom’s promise of health in the navel and marrow to the bones, eat a large meal of meat, which it says to use sparingly and only in times of cold or famine, and write beside the promise what you noticed in the next hour.

Day 280 Of Palms

Sober. Strew petals, or leaves from a plant you own, from your door to your table for something you finished, began or entered. Serve the best thing you were saving and cheer the thing aloud with the window open.

The Feasts

Feast The Feast of Your Birth

Sober. Dress as for a coronation, buy yourself the thing you have wanted longest, and take the head of the table at the best meal you can command. Raise a cold sweet drink first to the guest who earned it most, then to yourself. This one is to me.

Feast Walpurgis Night

Sober. In your own yard, on a balcony or at your own table, eat a feast with your fingers and drink cold black cherry juice by the glassful in the company your appetite chose. Let appetite end it in bed with whoever wants you there, or alone.

Feast The Memorial

Sober. Today, set out unleavened bread or any flatbread and red grape juice. Take the first piece and the first cup yourself before you offer any to anyone, alone or with anyone you choose, and finish both.

Feast Lots

Sober. Read the book of Esther aloud today from a Jewish or Protestant Bible and mark every mention of the god. Then eat a filled pastry to the number of marks, which is none, and one to someone who once got you home.

Feast The Passover

Sober. While leaven is forbidden, eat a cheeseburger on a leavened bun with a cup of grape juice. Before the first bite, tip ten drops from your cup onto the plate with one finger, one for each plague, and say These are for the sons of Egypt.
